articleTitle: Entropic CLT for Smoothed Convolutions and Associated Entropy Bounds
abstract: We explore an asymptotic behavior of entropies for sums of independent random variables that are convolved with a small continuous noise.

articleTitle: A Sharp Multidimensional Hermite–Hadamard Inequality
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega \subset {\mathbb{R}}^d $</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d \geq 2$</tex>, be a bounded convex domain and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\colon \Omega \to{\mathbb{R}}$</tex> be a non-negative subharmonic function. In this paper, we prove the inequality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*} \frac{1}{|\Omega|}\int_{\Omega} f(x)\, \textrm{d}x \leq \frac{d}{|\partial\Omega|}\int_{\partial\Omega} f(x)\, \textrm{d}\sigma(x)\,. \end{equation*}$$</tex> Equivalently, the result can be stated as a bound for the gradient of the Saint Venant torsion function. Specifically, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega \subset{\mathbb{R}}^d$</tex> is a bounded convex domain and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u$</tex> is the solution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\Delta u =1$</tex> with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*} \|\nabla u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} < d\frac{|\Omega|}{|\partial\Omega|}\,. \end{equation*}$$</tex> Moreover, both inequalities are sharp in the sense that if the constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> is replaced by something smaller there exist convex domains for which the inequalities fail. This improves upon the recent result that the optimal constant is bounded from above by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d^{3/2}$</tex> due to Beck et al. [2].

articleTitle: Abelian Groups Are Polynomially Stable
abstract: In recent years, there has been a considerable amount of interest in stability of equations and their corresponding groups. Here, we initiate the systematic study of the quantitative aspect of this theory. We develop a novel method, inspired by the Ornstein–Weiss quasi-tiling technique, to prove that abelian groups are polynomially stable with respect to permutations, under the normalized Hamming metrics on the groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{Sym}(n)$</tex>. In particular, this means that there exists <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D\geq 1$</tex> such that for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A,B\in \textrm{Sym}(n)$</tex>, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$AB$</tex> is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta $</tex>-close to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$BA$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon $</tex>-close to a commuting pair of permutations, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon \leq O\left (\delta ^{1/D}\right )$</tex>. We also observe a property-testing reformulation of this result, yielding efficient testers for certain permutation properties.

articleTitle: Topologies of Random Geometric Complexes on Riemannian Manifolds in the Thermodynamic Limit
abstract: We investigate the topologies of random geometric complexes built over random points sampled on Riemannian manifolds in the so-called “thermodynamic” regime. We prove the existence of universal limit laws for the topologies; namely, the random normalized counting measure of connected components (counted according to homotopy type) is shown to converge in probability to a deterministic probability measure. Moreover, we show that the support of the deterministic limiting measure equals the set of all homotopy types for Euclidean connected geometric complexes of the same dimension as the manifold.

articleTitle: A Proof of the Gaudin Bethe Ansatz Conjecture
abstract: The Gaudin algebra is the commutative subalgebra in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U({\mathfrak g})^{\otimes N}$</tex> generated by higher integrals of the quantum Gaudin magnet chain attached to a semisimple Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathfrak g}$</tex>. This algebra depends on a collection of pairwise distinct complex numbers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z_1,\ldots ,z_N$</tex>. We prove that this subalgebra has a cyclic vector in the space of singular vectors of the tensor product of any finite-dimensional irreducible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathfrak g}$</tex>-modules, for all values of the parameters <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z_1,\ldots ,z_N$</tex>. We deduce from this result the Bethe Ansatz conjecture in the Feigin–Frenkel form that states that the joint eigenvalues of the higher Gaudin Hamiltonians on the tensor product of irreducible finite-dimensional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathfrak g}$</tex>-modules are in 1-1 correspondence with monodromy-free <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^LG$</tex>-opers on the projective line with regular singularities at the points <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z_1,\ldots ,z_N,\infty $</tex>, and the prescribed residues at the singular points.

articleTitle: Deformation Theory of the Trivial mod p Galois Representation for GLn
abstract: We study the rigid generic fiber <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{X}^\square _{\overline \rho }$</tex> of the framed deformation space of the trivial representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline \rho : G_K \to \textrm{GL}_n(k)$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> is a finite field of characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p>0$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_K$</tex> is the absolute Galois group of a finite extension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K/\textbf{Q}_p$</tex>. Under some mild conditions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> we prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{X}^\square _{\overline \rho }$</tex> is normal. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p> n$</tex> we describe its irreducible components and show Zariski density of its crystalline points.

articleTitle: Vanishing Estimates for Fully Bubbling Solutions of SU (n + 1) Toda Systems at a Singular Source
abstract: For Gauss curvature equation (or more general Toda systems) defined on 2D spaces, the vanishing rate of certain curvature functions on blowup points is a key estimate for numerous applications. However, if these equations have singular sources, very few vanishing estimates can be found. In this article we consider a Toda system with singular sources defined on a Riemann surface and we prove a very surprising vanishing estimates and a reflection phenomenon for certain functions involving the Gauss curvature.

articleTitle: Euclidean Distance Degree of Projective Varieties
abstract: We give a positive answer to a conjecture of Aluffi–Harris on the computation of the Euclidean distance degree of a possibly singular projective variety in terms of the local Euler obstruction function.

articleTitle: Higher Complex Structures
abstract: We introduce and analyze a new geometric structure on topological surfaces generalizing the complex structure. To define this so-called higher complex structure, we use the punctual Hilbert scheme of the plane. The moduli space of higher complex structures is defined and is shown to be a generalization of the classical Teichmüller space. We give arguments for the conjectural isomorphism between the moduli space of higher complex structures and Hitchin's component.

articleTitle: Finiteness Properties of Pseudo-Hyperbolic Varieties
abstract: Motivated by Lang–Vojta’s conjecture, we show that the set of dominant rational self-maps of an algebraic variety over a number field with only finitely many rational points in any given number field is finite by combining Amerik’s theorem for dynamical systems of infinite order with properties of Prokhorov–Shramov’s notion of quasi-minimal models. We also prove a similar result in the geometric setting by using again not only Amerik’s theorem and Prokhorov–Shramov’s notion of quasi-minimal model but also Weil’s regularization theorem for birational self-maps and properties of dynamical degrees. Furthermore, in the geometric setting, we obtain an analogue of Kobayashi–Ochiai’s finiteness result for varieties of general type and thereby generalize Noguchi’s theorem (formerly Lang’s conjecture).

articleTitle: On the Continuity of the Integrated Density of States in the Disorder
abstract: Recently, Hislop and Marx studied the dependence of the integrated density of states on the underlying probability distribution for a class of discrete random Schrödinger operators and established a quantitative form of continuity in weak* topology. We develop an alternative approach to the problem, based on Ky Fan inequalities, and establish a sharp version of the estimate of Hislop and Marx. We also consider a corresponding problem for continual random Schrödinger operators on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^d$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Local Limit Theorem and Delocalization of Eigenvectors for Polynomials in Two Matrices
abstract: We propose a boundary regularity condition for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_n({\mathbb{C}})$</tex>-valued subordination functions in free probability to prove a local limit theorem and delocalization of eigenvectors for self-adjoint polynomials in two random matrices. We prove this through estimating the pair of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_n({\mathbb{C}})$</tex>-valued approximate subordination functions for the sum of two <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_n({\mathbb{C}})$</tex>-valued random matrices <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma _1\otimes C_N+\gamma _2\otimes U_N^*D_NU_N$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_N$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_N$</tex> are deterministic diagonal matrices, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_N$</tex> is Haar unitary.

articleTitle: Shifted Symplectic Lie Algebroids
abstract: Shifted symplectic Lie and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\infty }$</tex> algebroids model formal neighborhoods of manifolds in shifted symplectic stacks and serve as target spaces for twisted variants of the classical topological field theory defined by Alexandrov—Kontsevich—Schwarz—Zaboronsky. In this paper, we classify zero-, one-, and two-shifted symplectic algebroids and their higher gauge symmetries, in terms of classical geometric “higher structures”, such as Courant algebroids twisted by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega ^{2}$</tex>-gerbes. As applications, we produce new examples of twisted Courant algebroids from codimension-two cycles, and we give symplectic interpretations for several well-known features of higher structures (such as twists, Pontryagin classes, and tensor products). The proofs are valid in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{\infty }$</tex>, holomorphic, and algebraic settings and are based on a number of technical results on the homotopy theory of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\infty }$</tex> algebroids and their differential forms, which may be of independent interest.

articleTitle: Deformations of Lie Groupoids
abstract: We study deformations of Lie groupoids by means of the cohomology which controls them. This cohomology turns out to provide an intrinsic model for the cohomology of a Lie groupoid with values in its adjoint representation. We prove several fundamental properties of the deformation cohomology including Morita invariance, a van Est theorem, and a vanishing result in the proper case. Combined with Moser’s deformation arguments for groupoids, we obtain several rigidity and normal form results.

articleTitle: Bispectrality and Time–Band Limiting: Matrix-valued Polynomials
abstract: The subject of time–band limiting, originating in signal processing, is dominated by the miracle that a naturally appearing integral operator admits a commuting differential one allowing for a numerically efficient way to compute its eigenfunctions. Bispectrality is an effort to dig into the reasons behind this miracle and goes back to joint work with H. Duistermaat. This search has revealed unexpected connections with several parts of mathematics, including integrable systems. Here we consider a matrix-valued version of bispectrality and give a general condition under which we can display a constructive and simple way to obtain the commuting differential operator. Furthermore, we build an operator that commutes with both the time-limiting operator and the band-limiting operators.

articleTitle: Poisson Λ-brackets for Differential–Difference Equations
abstract: We introduce the notion of a multiplicative Poisson <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>-bracket, which plays the same role in the theory of Hamiltonian differential–difference equations as the usual Poisson <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>-bracket plays in the theory of Hamiltonian partial differential equations (PDE). We classify multiplicative Poisson <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>-brackets in one difference variable up to order 5. As an example, we demonstrate how to apply the Lenard–Magri scheme to a compatible pair of multiplicative Poisson <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>-brackets of order 1 and 2, to establish integrability of the Volterra chain.

articleTitle: On Cyclic Descents for Tableaux
abstract: The notion of descent set, for permutations as well as for standard Young tableaux (SYT), is classical. Cellini introduced a natural notion of cyclic descent set for permutations, and Rhoades introduced such a notion for SYT—but only for rectangular shapes. In this work we define cyclic extensions of descent sets in a general context and prove existence and essential uniqueness for SYT of almost all shapes. The proof applies nonnegativity properties of Postnikov’s toric Schur polynomials, providing a new interpretation of certain Gromov–Witten invariants.

articleTitle: Bounds for the Number of Cohomological Automorphic Representations of GL3/ℚ in the Weight Aspect
abstract: We prove a power saving over the trivial bound for the number of cohomological cuspidal automorphic representations of fixed level and growing weight on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_3/{\mathbb{Q}}$</tex> by adapting the methods of our earlier paper on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_2$</tex>.

articleTitle: M∖L is Not Closed
abstract: We show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1+3/\sqrt{2}$</tex> is a point of the Lagrange spectrum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> that is accumulated by a sequence of elements of the complement <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M\!\setminus\! L$</tex> of the Lagrange spectrum in the Markov spectrum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>. In particular, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M\!\setminus\! L$</tex> is not a closed subset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}$</tex>, so that a question by T. Bousch has a negative answer.

articleTitle: Minimal Bubbling for Willmore Surfaces
abstract: In this paper, we build an explicit example of a minimal bubble on a Willmore surface, showing there cannot be compactness for Willmore immersions of Willmore energy above <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16 \pi $</tex>. Additionally, we prove an inequality on the 2nd residue for limits of sequences of Willmore immersions with simple minimal bubbles. Doing so, we exclude some gluing configurations and prove compactness for immersed Willmore tori of energy below <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$12 \pi $</tex>.

articleTitle: Contact Dual Pairs
abstract: We introduce and study the notion of contact dual pair adopting a line bundle approach to contact and Jacobi geometry. A contact dual pair is a pair of Jacobi morphisms defined on the same contact manifold and satisfying a certain orthogonality condition. Contact groupoids and contact reduction are the main sources of examples. Among other properties, we prove the characteristic leaf correspondence theorem for contact dual pairs that parallels the analogous result of Weinstein for symplectic dual pairs.

articleTitle: The First Integral Cohomology of Pure Mapping Class Groups
abstract: It is a classical result that pure mapping class groups of connected, orientable surfaces of finite type and genus at least 3 are perfect. In stark contrast, we construct nontrivial homomorphisms from infinite-genus mapping class groups to the integers. Moreover, we compute the first integral cohomology group associated to the pure mapping class group of any connected orientable surface of genus at least 2 in terms of the surface’s simplicial homology. In order to do this, we show that pure mapping class groups of infinite-genus surfaces split as a semi-direct product.

articleTitle: Spaces of Low-Degree Rational Curves on Fano Complete Intersections
abstract: In this paper, we prove that the moduli space of low degree rational curves on a low-degree complete intersection passing several suitable points is a complete intersection. The proof involves some relationships among some divisors on the Kontsevich spaces, advanced techniques of deformations of rational curves, and classical projective geometry.

articleTitle: Dimension Theory and Degenerations of de Jonquières Divisors
abstract: This paper aims at settling the issue of the validity of the de Jonquières formulas. Consider the space of divisors with prescribed multiplicity, or de Jonquières divisors, contained in a linear series on a smooth projective curve. Under the assumption that this space is zero dimensional, the de Jonquières formulas compute the expected number of de Jonquières divisors. Using degenerations to nodal curves we show that, for a general curve equipped with a complete linear series, the space is of expected dimension, which shows that the counts are in fact true. This implies that in the case of negative expected dimension a general linear series on a general curve does not admit de Jonquières divisors of the expected type.

articleTitle: Large Deviation Estimates and Hölder Regularity of the Lyapunov Exponents for Quasi-periodic Schrödinger Cocycles
abstract: We consider one-dimensional quasi-periodic Schrödinger operators with analytic potentials. In the positive Lyapunov exponent regime, we prove large deviation estimates, which lead to refined Hölder continuity of the Lyapunov exponents and the integrated density of states, in both small Lyapunov exponent and large coupling regimes. Our results cover all the Diophantine frequencies and some Liouville frequencies.

articleTitle: Ext-groups in the Category of Strict Polynomial Functors
abstract: The aim of this paper is to study, by using the mathematical tools developed by Chałupnik, Touzé, and Van der Kallen, the effect of the Frobenius twist on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Ext}$</tex>-group in the category of strict polynomial functors. As an application, we obtain explicit formulas of cohomology of the orthogonal groups and symplectic ones.

articleTitle: Double Points of Free Projective Line Arrangements
abstract: We prove the Anzis–Tohăneanu conjecture, that is, the Dirac–Motzkin conjecture for supersolvable line arrangements in the projective plane over an arbitrary field of characteristic zero. Moreover, we show that a divisionally free arrangements of lines contain at least one double point that can be regarded as the Sylvester–Gallai theorem for some free arrangements. This is a corollary of a general result that if you add a line to a free projective line arrangement, then that line has to contain at least one double point. Also, we prove some conjectures and one open problems related to supersolvable line arrangements and the number of double points.

articleTitle: Vector-valued Littlewood-Paley-Stein Theory for Semigroups II
abstract: Inspired by a recent work of Hytönen and Naor, we solve a problem left open in our previous work joint with Martínez and Torrea on the vector-valued Littlewood-Paley-Stein theory for symmetric diffusion semigroups. We prove a similar result in the discrete case, namely, for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> which is the square of a symmetric diffusion Markovian operator on a measure space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Omega , \mu )$</tex>. Moreover, we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T\otimes{ \textrm{Id}}_X$</tex> extends to an analytic contraction on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p(\Omega ; X)$</tex> for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1<p<\infty $</tex> and any uniformly convex Banach space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>.

articleTitle: Deformation of Tilting-type Derived Equivalences for Crepant Resolutions
abstract: We say that an exact equivalence between the derived categories of two algebraic varieties is tilting type if it is constructed by using tilting bundles. The aim of this article is to understand the behavior of tilting-type equivalences for crepant resolutions under deformations. As an application of the method that we establish in this article, we study the derived equivalence for stratified Mukai flops and stratified Atiyah flops in terms of tilting bundles.

articleTitle: No Percolation at Criticality on Certain Groups of Intermediate Growth
abstract: We prove that critical percolation has no infinite clusters almost surely on any unimodular quasi-transitive graph satisfying a return probability upper bound of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_n(v,v) \leq \exp \left [-\Omega (n^\gamma )\right ]$</tex> for some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma>1/2$</tex>. The result is new in the case that the graph is of intermediate volume growth.

articleTitle: A Unique Continuation Property for the Level Set Equation
abstract: We prove the following unique continuation result: if a solution to the level set equation for mean curvature flow in a mean convex domain agrees to infinite order at the point where it attains its maximum with the solution for a ball, then it agrees everywhere and the domain is a ball.

articleTitle: Stability of Pure Nilpotent Structures on Collapsed Manifolds
abstract: The goal of this paper is to study the stability of pure nilpotent structures on an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-manifold for different collapsed metrics. We prove that if two metrics with bounded sectional curvature are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_0$</tex>-bi-Lipschitz equivalent and sufficient collapsed (depending on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_0$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>), then up to a diffeomorphism, the underlying nilpotent Killing structures coincide with each other, or one is embedded into another as a subsheaf. It improves Cheeger–Fukaya–Gromov’s local compatibility of pure nilpotent Killing structures for one collapsed metric to two Lipschitz equivalent metrics. As an application, we prove that those pure nilpotent Killing structures constructed by various smoothing methods to a Lipschitz equivalent metric with bounded sectional curvature are uniquely determined by the original metric modulo a diffeomorphism.

articleTitle: Thomae-Weber Formula: Algebraic Computations of Theta Constants
abstract: We give an algebraic method to compute the fourth power of the quotient of any even theta constants associated with a given non-hyperelliptic curve in terms of geometry of the curve. In order to apply the method, we work out non-hyperelliptic curves of genus 4, in particular, such curves lying on a singular quadric, which arise from del Pezzo surfaces of degree 1. Indeed, we obtain a complete level 2 structure of the curves by studying their theta characteristic divisors via exceptional divisors of the del Pezzo surfaces as the structure is required for the method.

articleTitle: Axisymmetric Diffeomorphisms and Ideal Fluids on Riemannian 3-Manifolds
abstract: We study the Riemannian geometry of 3D axisymmetric ideal fluids. We prove that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex> exponential map on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>-manifold is Fredholm along axisymmetric flows with sufficiently small swirl. Along the way, we define the notions of axisymmetric and swirl-free diffeomorphisms of any manifold with suitable symmetries and show that such diffeomorphisms form a totally geodesic submanifold of infinite <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex> diameter inside the space of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms whose diameter is known to be finite. As examples, we derive the axisymmetric Euler equations on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>-manifolds equipped with each of Thurston’s eight model geometries.

articleTitle: Codimension One Holomorphic Distributions on the Projective Three-space
abstract: We study codimension one holomorphic distributions on the projective three-space, analyzing the properties of their singular schemes and tangent sheaves. In particular, we provide a classification of codimension one distributions of degree at most 2 with locally free tangent sheaves and show that codimension one distributions of arbitrary degree with only isolated singularities have stable tangent sheaves. Furthermore, we describe the moduli space of distributions in terms of Grothendieck’s Quot-scheme for the tangent bundle. In certain cases, we show that the moduli space of codimension one distributions on the projective space is an irreducible, nonsingular quasi-projective variety. Finally, we prove that every rational foliation and certain logarithmic foliations have stable tangent sheaves.

articleTitle: Novikov Fundamental Group
abstract: Given a degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> cohomology class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u$</tex> on a closed manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>, we define a Novikov fundamental group associated with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u$</tex>, generalizing the usual fundamental group in the same spirit as Novikov homology generalizes Morse homology to the case of non exact <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>-forms. As an application, lower bounds for the minimal number of indexes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex> critical points of Morse closed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>-forms are obtained, that are different in nature from those derived from the Novikov homology.

articleTitle: Erratum to “Every symplectic toric orbifold is a centered reduction of a Cartesian product of weighted projective spaces”
The Kauffman Skein Module at 1st Order
abstract: For a three-manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> with boundary, we study the Kauffman module with indeterminate equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-1+\epsilon $</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon ^2=0$</tex>. We conjecture an explicit relation between this module and the Reidemeister torsion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>, which we prove in particular cases. As a maybe-useful tool, we then introduce a notion of twisted self-linking and prove that it satisfies the Kauffman relations at 1st order. These questions come from considerations on asymptotics of quantum invariants.

articleTitle: A Complete Classification of Unitary Fusion Categories Tensor Generated by an Object of Dimension $\frac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}$
abstract: In this paper we give a complete classification of unitary fusion categories <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\otimes $</tex>-generated by an object of dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}$</tex>. We show that all such categories arise as certain wreath products of either the Fibonacci category or of the dual even part of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2D2$</tex> subfactor. As a by-product of proving our main classification result we produce a classification of finite unitarizable quotients of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Fib}^{*N}$</tex> satisfying a certain symmetry condition.

articleTitle: Homological Projective Duality for Linear Systems with Base Locus
abstract: We show how blowing up varieties in base loci of linear systems gives a procedure for creating new homological projective duals from old. Starting with a homological projective (HP) dual pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X,Y$</tex> and smooth orthogonal linear sections <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_L,Y_L$</tex>, we prove that the blowup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_L$</tex> is naturally HP dual to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y_L$</tex>. The result also holds true when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> is a noncommutative variety or just a category. We extend the result to the case where the base locus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_L$</tex> is a multiple of a smooth variety and the universal hyperplane has rational singularities; here the HP dual is a weakly crepant categorical resolution of singularities of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y_L$</tex>. Finally we give examples where, starting with a noncommutative <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>, the above process nevertheless gives geometric HP duals.

articleTitle: Galois Closures of Non-commutative Rings and an Application to Hermitian Representations
abstract: Galois closures of commutative rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> ring extensions were introduced by Bhargava and the 2nd author. In this paper, we generalize the construction to the case of non-commutative rings. We show that noncommutative Galois closures commute with base change and satisfy a product formula. As an application, we give a uniform construction of many of the representations arising in arithmetic invariant theory, including many Vinberg representations.

articleTitle: The Differences Between Consecutive Primes, V
abstract: We show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*}\sum_{\substack{p_n\le x\\ p_{n+1}-p_n\ge\sqrt{p_n}}}(p_{n+1}-p_n) \ll_{\varepsilon} x^{3/5+\varepsilon}\end{equation*}$$</tex>or any fixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon>0$</tex>. This improves a result of Matomäki, in which the exponent was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2/3$</tex>.

articleTitle: Classification of Toric Manifolds over an n-Cube with One Vertex Cut
abstract: A complete nonsingular toric variety (called a toric manifold) is over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> if its quotient by the compact torus is homeomorphic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> as a manifold with corners. Bott manifolds are toric manifolds over an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-cube <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I^n$</tex> and blowing them up at a fixed point produces toric manifolds over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{vc}(I^n)$</tex> an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-cube with one vertex cut. They are all projective. On the other hand, Oda’s three-fold, the simplest non-projective toric manifold, is over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{vc}(I^3)$</tex>. In this paper, we classify toric manifolds over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{vc}(I^n)$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(n\ge 3)$</tex> as varieties and as smooth manifolds. It consequently turns out that there are many non-projective toric manifolds over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{vc}(I^n)$</tex> but they are all diffeomorphic, and toric manifolds over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{vc}(I^n)$</tex> in some class are determined by their cohomology rings as varieties.

articleTitle: On a Conjecture of Sharifi and Mazur’s Eisenstein Ideal
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> be prime numbers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq 5$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> divides <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N-1$</tex>. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex> be Mazur’s Eisenstein ideal of level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_+$</tex> be the plus part of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_1(X_0(N), \mathbf Z_{p})$</tex> for the complex conjugation. We give a conjectural explicit description of the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I\cdot H_+/I^2\cdot H_+$</tex> in terms of the 2nd <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-group of the cyclotomic field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf Q(\zeta _N)$</tex>. We prove that this conjecture follows from a conjecture of Sharifi about some Eisenstein ideal of level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma _1(N)$</tex>. Following the work of Fukaya–Kato, we prove partial results on Sharifi’s conjecture. This allows us to prove partial results on our conjecture.

articleTitle: Generalized Logarithmic Hardy–Littlewood–Sobolev Inequality
abstract: This paper is devoted to logarithmic Hardy–Littlewood–Sobolev inequalities in the 2D Euclidean space, in the presence of an external potential with logarithmic growth. The coupling with the potential introduces a new parameter, with two regimes. The attractive regime reflects the standard logarithmic Hardy–Littlewood–Sobolev inequality. The 2nd regime corresponds to a reverse inequality, with the opposite sign in the convolution term, which allows us to bound the free energy of a drift–diffusion–Poisson system from below. Our method is based on an extension of an entropy method proposed by E. Carlen, J. Carrillo, and M. Loss, and on a nonlinear diffusion equation.

articleTitle: Finiteness Properties of Affine Difference Algebraic Groups
abstract: We establish several finiteness properties of groups defined by algebraic difference equations. One of our main results is that a subgroup of the general linear group defined by possibly infinitely many algebraic difference equations in the matrix entries can indeed be defined by finitely many such equations. As an application, we show that the difference ideal of all difference algebraic relations among the solutions of a linear differential equation is finitely generated.

articleTitle: Conformal Invariance of CLEΚ on the Riemann Sphere for Κ ∈(4,8)
abstract: The conformal loop ensemble (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{CLE}}$</tex>) is the canonical conformally invariant probability measure on non-crossing loops in a simply connected domain in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbbm{C}$</tex> and is indexed by a parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa \in (8/3,8)$</tex>. We consider <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{CLE}}_\kappa $</tex> on the whole-plane in the regime in which the loops are self-intersecting (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa \in (4,8)$</tex>) and show that it is invariant under the inversion map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \mapsto 1/z$</tex>. This shows that whole-plane <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{CLE}}_\kappa $</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa \in (4,8)$</tex> defines a conformally invariant measure on loops on the Riemann sphere. The analogous statement in the regime in which the loops are simple (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa \in (8/3,4]$</tex>) was proven by Kemppainen and Werner and together with the present work covers the entire range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa \in (8/3,8)$</tex> for which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{CLE}}_\kappa $</tex> is defined. As an intermediate step in the proof, we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{CLE}}_\kappa $</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa \in (4,8)$</tex> on an annulus, with any specified number of inner-boundary-surrounding loops, is well defined and conformally invariant.

articleTitle: The Cycle Structure of Unicritical Polynomials
abstract: A polynomial with integer coefficients yields a family of dynamical systems indexed by primes as follows: for any prime <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>, reduce its coefficients mod <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> and consider its action on the field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ {{\mathbb{F}}}_p$</tex>. The questions of whether and in what sense these families are random have been studied extensively, spurred in part by Pollard’s famous “rho” algorithm for integer factorization (the heuristic justification of which is the conjectural randomness of one such family). However, the cycle structure of these families cannot be random, since in any such family, the number of cycles of a fixed length in any dynamical system in that family is bounded. In this paper, we show that the cycle statistics of many of these families are as random as possible. As a corollary, we show that most members of these families have many cycles, addressing a conjecture of Mans et al.

articleTitle: Picard Groups of Moduli Spaces of Curves with Symmetry
abstract: We study the Picard groups of moduli spaces of smooth complex projective curves that have a group of automorphisms with a prescribed topological action. One of our main tools is the theory of symmetric mapping class groups. In the 1st part of the paper, we show that, under mild restrictions, the moduli spaces of smooth curves with an abelian group of automorphisms of a fixed topological type have finitely generated Picard groups. In certain special cases, we are able to compute them exactly. In the 2nd part of the paper, we show that finite abelian level covers of the hyperelliptic locus in the moduli space of smooth curves have finitely generated Picard groups. We also compute the Picard groups of the moduli spaces of hyperelliptic curves of compact type.

articleTitle: Integrals Derived from the Doubling Method
abstract: In this note, we use a basic identity, derived from the generalized doubling integrals of [2], in order to explain the existence of various global Rankin–Selberg integrals for certain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions. To derive these global integrals, we use the identities relating Eisenstein series in [11], together with the process of exchanging roots. We concentrate on several well-known examples, and explain how to obtain them from the basic identity. Using these ideas, we also show how to derive a new global integral.

articleTitle: Dilations of q-Commuting Unitaries
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q = e^{i \theta } \in \mathbb{T}$</tex> (where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta \in \mathbb{R}$</tex>), and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u,v$</tex> be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-commuting unitaries, that is, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v$</tex> are unitaries such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$vu = quv$</tex>. In this paper, we find the optimal constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c = c_{\theta }$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u,v$</tex> can be dilated to a pair of operators <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c U, c V$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> are commuting unitaries. We show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*} c_{\theta} = \frac{4}{\|u_{\theta}+u_{\theta}^*+v_{\theta}+v_{\theta}^*\|}, \end{equation*}$$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_{\theta }, v_{\theta }$</tex> are the universal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-commuting pair of unitaries, and we give numerical estimates for the above quantity. In the course of our proof, we also consider dilating <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-commuting unitaries to scalar multiples of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q^{\prime}$</tex>-commuting unitaries. The techniques that we develop allow us to give new and simple “dilation theoretic” proofs of well-known results regarding the continuity of the field of rotations algebras. In particular, for the so-called “almost Mathieu operator” <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h_{\theta } = u_{\theta }+u_{\theta }^*+v_{\theta }+v_{\theta }^*$</tex>, we recover the fact that the norm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\|h_{\theta }\|$</tex> is a Lipschitz continuous function of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta $</tex>, as well as the result that the spectrum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma (h_{\theta })$</tex> is a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{1}{2}$</tex>-Hölder continuous function in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta $</tex> with respect to the Hausdorff metric. In fact, we obtain this Hölder continuity of the spectrum for every self-adjoint *-polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p(u_{\theta },v_{\theta })$</tex>, which in turn endows the rotation algebras with the natural structure of a continuous field of C*-algebras.

articleTitle: An Isoperimetric-Type Inequality for Spacelike Submanifold in the Minkowski Space
abstract: We prove an isoperimetric-type inequality for maximal, spacelike submanifold in the Minkowski space. The argument is based on the recent work of Brendle.

We show that the 4th integral cohomology of Conway’s group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Co}_0$</tex> is a cyclic group of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$24$</tex>, generated by the 1st fractional Pontryagin class of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$24$</tex>-dimensional representation.

articleTitle: Halfway to Rota’s Basis Conjecture
abstract: In 1989, Rota made the following conjecture. Given <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> bases <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{1},\dots ,B_{n}$</tex> in an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-dimensional vector space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>, one can always find <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> disjoint bases of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>, each containing exactly one element from each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{i}$</tex> (we call such bases transversal bases). Rota’s basis conjecture remains wide open despite its apparent simplicity and the efforts of many researchers (e.g., the conjecture was recently the subject of the collaborative “Polymath” project). In this paper we prove that one can always find <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left (1/2-o\left (1\right )\right )n$</tex> disjoint transversal bases, improving on the previous best bound of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega \left (n/\log n\right )$</tex>. Our results also apply to the more general setting of matroids.

articleTitle: Semibricks
abstract: In representation theory of finite-dimensional algebras, (semi)bricks are a generalization of (semi)simple modules, and they have long been studied. The aim of this paper is to study semibricks from the point of view of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau $</tex>-tilting theory. We construct canonical bijections between the set of support <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau $</tex>-tilting modules, the set of semibricks satisfying a certain finiteness condition, and the set of 2-term simple-minded collections. In particular, we unify Koenig–Yang bijections and Ingalls–Thomas bijections generalized by Marks–Št’ovíček, which involve several important notions in the derived categories and the module categories. We also investigate connections between our results and two kinds of reduction theorems of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau $</tex>-rigid modules by Jasso and Eisele–Janssens–Raedschelders. Moreover, we study semibricks over Nakayama algebras and tilted algebras in detail as examples.

articleTitle: Dirac Induction for Rational Cherednik Algebras
abstract: We introduce the local and global indices of Dirac operators for the rational Cherednik algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathsf{H}_{t,c}(G,\mathfrak{h})$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is a complex reflection group acting on a finite-dimensional vector space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{h}$</tex>. We investigate precise relations between the (local) Dirac index of a simple module in the category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathsf{H}_{t,c}(G,\mathfrak{h})$</tex>, the graded <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>-character of the module, the Euler–Poincaré pairing, and the composition series polynomials for standard modules. In the global theory, we introduce integral-reflection modules for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathsf{H}_{t,c}(G,\mathfrak{h})$</tex> constructed from finite-dimensional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>-modules. We define and compute the index of a Dirac operator on the integral-reflection module and show that the index is, in a sense, independent of the parameter function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c$</tex>. The study of the kernel of these global Dirac operators leads naturally to a notion of dualised generalised Dunkl–Opdam operators.

articleTitle: Compactness and Rigidity of λ-Surfaces
abstract: In this paper we develop the compactness theorem for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda $</tex>-surface in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^3$</tex> with uniform <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda $</tex>, genus, and area growth. This theorem can be viewed as a generalization of Colding–Minicozzi's compactness theorem for self-shrinkers in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^3$</tex>. As an application of this compactness theorem, we prove a rigidity theorem for convex <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda $</tex>-surfaces.

articleTitle: From Hierarchical to Relative Hyperbolicity
abstract: We provide a simple, combinatorial criteria for a hierarchically hyperbolic space to be relatively hyperbolic by proving a new formulation of relative hyperbolicity in terms of hierarchy structures. In the case of clean hierarchically hyperbolic groups, this criteria characterizes relative hyperbolicity. We apply our criteria to graphs associated to surfaces and prove that the separating curve graph of a surface is relatively hyperbolic when the surface has zero or two punctures. We also recover a celebrated theorem of Brock and Masur on the relative hyperbolicity of the Weil–Petersson metric on Teichmüller space for surfaces with complexity three.

articleTitle: Exponential-Square Integrability, Weighted Inequalities for the Square Functions Associated to Operators, and Applications
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> be a metric space with a doubling measure. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> be a nonnegative self-adjoint operator acting on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2(X)$</tex>, hence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> generates an analytic semigroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e^{-tL}$</tex>. Assume that the kernels <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_t(x,y)$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e^{-tL}$</tex> satisfy Gaussian upper bounds and Hölder continuity in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex>, but we do not require the semigroup to satisfy the preservation condition <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e^{-tL}1 = 1$</tex>. In this article we aim to establish the exponential-square integrability of a function whose square function associated to an operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> is bounded, and the proof is new even for the Laplace operator on the Euclidean spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb R^n}$</tex>. We then apply this result to obtain: (1) estimates of the norm on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^p$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> becomes large for operators such as the square functions or spectral multipliers; (2) weighted norm inequalities for the square functions; and (3) eigenvalue estimates for Schrödinger operators on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb R}^n$</tex> or Lipschitz domains of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb R}^n$</tex>.

articleTitle: On the Probability That a Stationary Gaussian Process With Spectral Gap Remains Non-negative on a Long Interval
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> be a zero mean continuous stationary Gaussian process on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}$</tex> whose spectral measure vanishes in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta $</tex>-neighborhood of the origin. Then, the probability that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> stays non-negative on an interval of length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> is at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e^{-c\delta ^2 L^2}$</tex> with some absolute <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c>0$</tex> and the result is sharp without additional assumptions.

articleTitle: The Surface Quasi-geostrophic Equation With Random Diffusion
abstract: Consider the surface quasi-geostrophic equation with random diffusion, white in time. We show global existence and uniqueness in high probability for the associated Cauchy problem satisfying a Gevrey type bound. This article is inspired by a recent work of Glatt-Holtz and Vicol [16].

articleTitle: Stability Parameters for Quiver Sheaves
abstract: In this paper, we will begin the systematic study of the influence of the choice of a faithful representation on the notion of (semi)stability for decorated principal bundles. We will prove boundedness for slope semistable quiver sheaves.

articleTitle: Decomposition Rules for the Ring of Representations of Non-Archimedean GLn
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{R}$</tex> be the Grothendieck ring of complex smooth finite-length representations of the sequence of p-adic groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{GL_n(F)\}_{n=0}^\infty $</tex>, with multiplication defined through parabolic induction. We study the problem of the decomposition of products of irreducible representations in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{R}$</tex>. We obtain a necessary condition on irreducible factors of a given product by introducing a width invariant. Width <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> representations form the previously studied class of ladder representations. We later focus on the case of a product of two ladder representations, for which we establish that all irreducible factors appear with multiplicity one. Finally, we propose a general rule for the composition series of a product of two ladder representations and prove its validity for cases in which the irreducible factors correspond to smooth Schubert varieties.

articleTitle: N = 4 Superconformal Algebras and Diagonal Cosets
abstract: Coset constructions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{W}}}$</tex>-algebras have many applications and were recently given for principal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{W}}}$</tex>-algebras of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> types by Arakawa together with the 1st and 3rd authors. In this paper, we give coset constructions of the large and small <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N=4$</tex> superconformal algebras, which are the minimal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{W}}}$</tex>-algebras of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathfrak{d}}}(2,1;a)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathfrak{p}}}{{\mathfrak{s}}}{{\mathfrak{l}}}(2|2)$</tex>, respectively. From these realizations, one finds a remarkable connection between the large <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N=4$</tex> algebra and the diagonal coset <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{k_1, k_2} = \textrm{Com}(V^{k_1+k_2}({{\mathfrak{s}}}{{\mathfrak{l}}}_2), V^{k_1}({{\mathfrak{s}}}{{\mathfrak{l}}}_2) \otimes V^{k_2}({{\mathfrak{s}}}{{\mathfrak{l}}}_2))$</tex>, namely, as two-parameter vertex algebras, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{k_1, k_2}$</tex> coincides with the coset of the large <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N=4$</tex> algebra by its affine subalgebra. We also show that at special points in the parameter space, the simple quotients of these cosets are isomorphic to various <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{W}}}$</tex>-algebras. As a corollary, we give new examples of strongly rational principal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{W}}}$</tex>-algebras of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> at degenerate admissible levels.

articleTitle: Differential Graded Lie Algebras and Leibniz Algebra Cohomology
abstract: In this note, we interpret Leibniz algebras as differential graded (DG) Lie algebras. Namely, we consider two fully faithful functors from the category of Leibniz algebras to that of DG Lie algebras and show that they naturally give rise to the Leibniz cohomology and the Chevalley–Eilenberg cohomology. As an application, we prove a conjecture stated by Pirashvili in [9].

articleTitle: The Inverse Spectral Problem for Periodic Conservative Multi-peakon Solutions of the Camassa–Holm Equation
abstract: We solve the inverse spectral problem associated with periodic conservative multi-peakon solutions of the Camassa–Holm equation. The corresponding isospectral sets can be identified with finite-dimensional tori.

articleTitle: Dependence of the Density of States on the Probability Distribution for Discrete Random Schrödinger Operators
abstract: We prove that the density of states measure (DOSm) for random Schrödinger operators on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}^d$</tex> is weak-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\ast }$</tex> Hölder-continuous in the probability measure. The framework we develop is general enough to extend to a wide range of discrete, random operators, including the Anderson model on the Bethe lattice, as well as random Schrödinger operators on the strip. An immediate application of our main result provides quantitive continuity estimates for the disorder dependence of the DOSm and the integrated density of states (IDS) in the weak disorder regime. These results hold for a general compactly supported single-site probability measure, without any further assumptions. The few previously available results for the disorder dependence of the IDS valid for dimensions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d \geqslant 2$</tex> assumed absolute continuity of the single-site measure and thus excluded the Bernoulli–Anderson model. As a further application of our main result, we establish quantitative continuity results for the Lyapunov exponent of random Schrödinger operators for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d=1$</tex> in the probability measure with respect to the weak-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\ast }$</tex> topology.

articleTitle: Double Jump Phase Transition in a Soliton Cellular Automaton
abstract: In this paper, we consider the soliton cellular automaton introduced in [26] with a random initial configuration. We give multiple constructions of a Young diagram describing various statistics of the system in terms of familiar objects like birth-and-death chains and Galton–Watson forests. Using these ideas, we establish limit theorems showing that if the 1st <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> boxes are occupied independently with probability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p\in (0,1)$</tex>, then the number of solitons is of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> and the length of the longest soliton is of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log n$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p<1/2$</tex>, order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt{n}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p=1/2$</tex>, and order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p>1/2$</tex>. Additionally, we uncover a condensation phenomenon in the supercritical regime: for each fixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$j\geq 1$</tex>, the top <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$j$</tex> soliton lengths have the same order as the longest for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p\leq 1/2$</tex>, whereas all but the longest have order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log n$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p>1/2$</tex>. As an application, we obtain scaling limits for the lengths of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k^{\textrm{th}}$</tex> longest increasing and decreasing subsequences in a random stack-sortable permutation of length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> in terms of random walks and Brownian excursions.

articleTitle: Algebraic Reduced Genus One Gromov–Witten Invariants for Complete Intersections in Projective Spaces
abstract: In [17, 18], Zinger defined reduced Gromov–Witten (GW) invariants and proved a comparison theorem of standard and reduced genus one GW invariants for every symplectic manifold (with all dimension). In [3], Chang and Li provided a proof of the comparison theorem for quintic Calabi–Yau three-folds in algebraic geometry by taking a definition of reduced invariants as an Euler number of certain vector bundle. In [5], Coates and Manolache have defined reduced GW invariants in algebraic geometry following the idea by Vakil and Zinger in [14] and proved the comparison theorem for every Calabi–Yau threefold. In this paper, we prove the comparison theorem for every (not necessarily Calabi–Yau) complete intersection of Dimension 2 or 3 in projective spaces by taking a definition of reduced GW invariants in [5].

articleTitle: A Transformation Rule for Natural Multiplicities
abstract: For multiplicities arising from a family of ideals we provide a general approach to transformation rules for a ring extension that is étale in codimension one. Our result can be applied to bound the size of the local étale fundamental group of a singularity in terms of F-signature, recovering a recent result of Carvajal-Rojas, Schwede, and Tucker, and differential signature, providing the 1st characteristic-free effective bound.

articleTitle: Complex Geometry of Iwasawa Manifolds
abstract: An Iwasawa manifold is a compact complex homogeneous manifold isomorphic to a quotient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G/\Lambda $</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is the group of complex unipotent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3 \times 3$</tex> matrices and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda \subset G$</tex> is a cocompact lattice. In this work, we study holomorphic submanifolds in Iwasawa manifolds. We prove that any compact complex curve in an Iwasawa manifold is contained in a holomorphic subtorus. We also prove that any complex surface in an Iwasawa manifold is either an abelian surface or a Kähler non-projective isotrivial elliptic surface of Kodaira dimension one. In the Appendix, we show that any subtorus in Iwasawa manifold carries complex multiplication.

articleTitle: Product Matrix Processes as Limits of Random Plane Partitions
abstract: We consider a random process with discrete time formed by squared singular values of products of truncations of Haar-distributed unitary matrices. We show that this process can be understood as a scaling limit of the Schur process, which gives determinantal formulas for (dynamical) correlation functions and a contour integral representation for the correlation kernel. The relation with the Schur processes implies that the continuous limit of marginals for q-distributed plane partitions coincides with the joint law of squared singular values for products of truncations of Haar-distributed random unitary matrices. We provide structural reasons for this coincidence that may also extend to other classes of random matrices.

articleTitle: The Local Structure of Generalized Contact Bundles
abstract: Generalized contact bundles are odd-dimensional analogues of generalized complex manifolds. They have been introduced recently and very little is known about them. In this paper we study their local structure. Specifically, we prove a local splitting theorem similar to those appearing in Poisson geometry. In particular, in a neighborhood of a regular point, a generalized contact bundle is either the product of a contact and a complex manifold or the product of a symplectic manifold and a manifold equipped with an integrable complex structure on the gauge algebroid of the trivial line bundle.

articleTitle: Schemes Supported on the Singular Locus of a Hyperplane Arrangement in ℙn
abstract: A hyperplane arrangement in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^n$</tex> is free if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R/J$</tex> is Cohen–Macaulay (CM), where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R = k[x_0,\dots ,x_n]$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> is the Jacobian ideal. We study the CM-ness of two related unmixed ideals: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ J^{un}$</tex>, the intersection of height two primary components, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt{J}$</tex>, the radical. Under a mild hypothesis, we show these ideals are CM. Suppose the hypothesis fails. For equidimensional curves in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^3$</tex>, the Hartshorne–Rao module measures the failure of CM-ness and determines the even liaison class of the curve. We show that for any positive integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>, there is an arrangement for which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R/J^{un}$</tex> (resp. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R/\sqrt{J}$</tex>) fails to be CM in only one degree, and this failure is by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>. We draw consequences for the even liaison class of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J^{un}$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt{J}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Finiteness Theorems for Kac–Moody Groups over Non-archimedean Local Fields
