abstract: We prove the finiteness of formal analogs of the spherical function (Spherical Finiteness), the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf c}$</tex>-function (Gindikin–Karpelevich Finiteness), and obtain a formal analog of Harish-Chandra's limit (Approximation Theorem) relating spherical and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf c}$</tex>-function in the setting of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic Kac–Moody groups. The finiteness theorems imply that the formal analog of the Gindikin–Karpelevich integral is well defined in local Kac–Moody settings. These results extend Braverman–Garland–Kazhdan–Patnaik's affine Gindikin–Karpelevich finiteness theorems from [4] and provide an algebraic analog of the combinatorial results of Gaussent–Rousseau [10] and Hébert [14].

articleTitle: Measure Rigidity for Horospherical Subgroups of Groups Acting on Trees
abstract: We prove analogues of some of the classical results in homogeneous dynamics in nonlinear setting. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> be a closed subgroup of the group of automorphisms of a biregular tree and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma \leq G$</tex> a discrete subgroup. For a large class of groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>, we give a classification of the probability measures on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G/\Gamma $</tex> invariant under horospherical subgroups. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> is a cocompact lattice, we show the unique ergodicity of the horospherical action. We prove Hedlund's theorem for geometrically finite quotients. Finally, we show equidistribution of large compact orbits.

articleTitle: Non-Commutative Crepant Resolutions for Some Toric Singularities I
abstract: We give a criterion for the existence of noncommutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) for certain toric singularities. In particular, we recover Broomhead’s result that a three-dimensional toric Gorenstein singularity has an NCCR. Our result also yields the existence of an NCCR for a four-dimensional toric Gorenstein singularity, which is known to have no toric NCCR.

articleTitle: Salem Numbers and the Spectrum of Hyperbolic Surfaces
abstract: We give a reformulation of Salem’s conjecture about the absence of Salem numbers near one in terms of a uniform spectral gap for certain arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces.

articleTitle: Rigidity of Nonnegatively Curved Surfaces Relative to a Curve
abstract: We prove that any properly oriented <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{C}^{2,1}$</tex> isometric immersion of a positively curved Riemannian surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> into Euclidean 3-space is uniquely determined, up to a rigid motion, by its values on any curve segment in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>. A generalization of this result to nonnegatively curved surfaces is presented as well under suitable conditions on their parabolic points. Thus, we obtain a local version of Cohn-Vossen’s rigidity theorem for convex surfaces subject to a Dirichlet condition. The proof employs in part Hormander’s unique continuation principle for elliptic partial differential equations. Our approach also yields a short proof of Cohn-Vossen’s theorem.

articleTitle: Asymptotics for the Nodal Components of Non-Identically Distributed Monochromatic Random Waves
abstract: We study monochromatic random waves on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{R}}^n$</tex> defined by Gaussian variables whose variances tend to zero sufficiently fast. This has the effect that the Fourier transform of the monochromatic wave is an absolutely continuous measure on the sphere with a suitably smooth density, which connects the problem with the scattering regime of monochromatic waves. In this setting, we compute the asymptotic distribution of the nodal components of random monochromatic waves, showing that the number of nodal components contained in a large ball <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_R$</tex> grows asymptotically like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R/\pi $</tex> with probability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_n>0$</tex> and is bounded uniformly in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> with probability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1-p_n$</tex> (which is positive if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geqslant 3$</tex>). In the latter case, we show the existence of a unique noncompact nodal component. We also provide an explicit sufficient stability criterion to ascertain when a more general Gaussian probability distribution has the same asymptotic nodal distribution law.

articleTitle: Givental's Non-linear Maslov Index on Lens Spaces
abstract: Givental's non-linear Maslov index, constructed in 1990, is a quasimorphism on the universal cover of the identity component of the contactomorphism group of real projective space. This invariant was used by several authors to prove contact rigidity phenomena such as orderability, unboundedness of the discriminant and oscillation metrics, and a contact geometric version of the Arnold conjecture. In this article, we give an analogue for lens spaces of Givental's construction and its applications.

articleTitle: Higher Order Polars of Quasi-Ordinary Singularities
abstract: A quasi-ordinary polynomial is a monic polynomial with coefficients in the power series ring such that its discriminant equals a monomial up to unit. In this paper, we study higher derivatives of quasi-ordinary polynomials, also called higher order polars. We find factorizations of these polars. Our research in this paper goes in two directions. We generalize the results of Casas–Alvero and our previous results on higher order polars in the plane to irreducible quasi-ordinary polynomials. We also generalize the factorization of the first polar of a quasi-ordinary polynomial (not necessarily irreducible) given by the first-named author and González-Pérez to higher order polars. This is a new result even in the plane case. Our results remain true when we replace quasi-ordinary polynomials by quasi-ordinary power series.

articleTitle: The Geometric Structure of Symplectic Contraction
abstract: We show that the symplectic contraction map of Hilgert–Manon–Martens [9], a symplectic version of Popov’s horospherical contraction, is simply the quotient of a Hamiltonian manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> by a “stratified null foliation” that is determined by the group action and moment map. We also show that the quotient differential structure on the symplectic contraction of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> supports a Poisson bracket. We end by proving a very general description of the topology of fibers of Gelfand–Zeitlin (also spelled Gelfand–Tsetlin or Gelfand–Cetlin) systems on multiplicity-free Hamiltonian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U(n)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SO(n)$</tex> manifolds.

articleTitle: Non-Kähler Mirror Symmetry of the Iwasawa Manifold
abstract: We propose a new approach to the mirror symmetry conjecture in a form suitable to possibly non-Kähler compact complex manifolds whose canonical bundle is trivial. We apply our methods by proving that the Iwasawa manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>, a well-known non-Kähler compact complex manifold of dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>, is its own mirror dual to the extent that its Gauduchon cone, replacing the classical Kähler cone that is empty in this case, corresponds to what we call the local universal family of essential deformations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. These are obtained by removing from the Kuranishi family the two “superfluous” dimensions of complex parallelisable deformations that have a similar geometry to that of the Iwasawa manifold. The remaining four dimensions are shown to have a clear geometric meaning including in terms of the degeneration at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_2$</tex> of the Frölicher spectral sequence. On the local moduli space of “essential” complex structures, we obtain a canonical Hodge decomposition of weight <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex> and a variation of Hodge structures, construct coordinates and Yukawa couplings while implicitly proving a local Torelli theorem. On the metric side of the mirror, we construct a variation of Hodge structures parametrised by a subset of the complexified Gauduchon cone of the Iwasawa manifold using the sGG property (which means that all the Gauduchon metrics are strongly Gauduchon) of all the small deformations of this manifold proved in earlier joint work of the author with L. Ugarte. Finally, we define a mirror map linking the two variations of Hodge structures and we highlight its properties.

articleTitle: Scattering Fans
abstract: Scattering diagrams arose in the context of mirror symmetry, Donaldson–Thomas theory, and integrable systems. We show that a consistent scattering diagram with minimal support cuts the ambient space into a complete fan. A special class of scattering diagrams, the cluster scattering diagrams, is closely related to cluster algebras. We show that the cluster scattering fan associated to an exchange matrix <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> refines the mutation fan for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> (a complete fan that encodes the geometry of mutations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex>). We conjecture that, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\times n$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n>2$</tex>, these two fans coincide if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> is of finite mutation type.

articleTitle: Canonical Gelfand–Zeitlin Modules over Orthogonal Gelfand–Zeitlin Algebras
abstract: We prove that every orthogonal Gelfand–Zeitlin algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex> acts (faithfully) on its Gelfand–Zeitlin subalgebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex>. Considering the dual module, we show that every Gelfand–Zeitlin character of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> is realizable in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex>-module. We observe that the Gelfand–Zeitlin formulae can be rewritten using divided difference operators. It turns out that the action of the latter operators on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> gives rise to an explicit basis in a certain Gelfand–Zeitlin submodule of the dual module mentioned above. This gives, generically, both in the case of regular and singular Gelfand–Zeitlin characters, an explicit construction of simple modules, which realize the given Gelfand–Zeitlin characters.

articleTitle: Characteristic Polynomials of Complex Random Matrices and Painlevé Transcendents
abstract: We study expectations of powers and correlation functions for characteristic polynomials of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N \times N$</tex> non-Hermitian random matrices. For the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>-point and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>-point correlation function, we obtain several characterizations in terms of Painlevé transcendents, both at finite <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> and asymptotically as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N \to \infty $</tex>. In the asymptotic analysis, two regimes of interest are distinguished: boundary asymptotics where parameters of the correlation function can touch the boundary of the limiting eigenvalue support and bulk asymptotics where they are strictly inside the support. For the complex Ginibre ensemble this involves Painlevé IV at the boundary as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N \to \infty $</tex>. Our approach, together with the results in [49], suggests that this should arise in a much broader class of planar models. For the bulk asymptotics, one of our results can be interpreted as the merging of two “planar Fisher–Hartwig singularities” where Painlevé V arises in the asymptotics. We also discuss the correspondence of our results with a normal matrix model with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-fold rotational symmetries known as the lemniscate ensemble, recently studied in [15, 18]. Our approach is flexible enough to apply to non-Gaussian models such as the truncated unitary ensemble or induced Ginibre ensemble; we show that in the former case Painlevé VI arises at finite <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>. Scaling near the boundary leads to Painlevé V, in contrast to the Ginibre ensemble.

articleTitle: Wall-Crossings for Hassett Descendant Potentials
abstract: This paper solves the combinatorics relating the intersection theory of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi $</tex>-classes of Hassett spaces to that of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{{\mathcal{M}}}_{g,n}$</tex>. A generating function for intersection numbers of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi $</tex>-classes on all Hassett spaces is obtained from the Gromov–Witten potential of a point via a non-invertible transformation of variables. When restricting to diagonal weights, the changes of variables are invertible and explicitly described as polynomial functions. Finally, the comparison of potentials is extended to the level of cycles: the pinwheel cycle potential, a generating function for tautological classes of rational tail type on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{{\mathcal{M}}}_{g,n}$</tex> is the right instrument to describe the pull-back to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{{\mathcal{M}}}_{g,n}$</tex> of all monomials of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi $</tex>-classes on Hassett spaces.

articleTitle: On Intermediate Subalgebras of C*-simple Group Actions
abstract: We show that for a large class of actions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma \curvearrowright \mathcal{A}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*$</tex>-simple groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> on unital <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*$</tex>-algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex>, including any non-faithful action of a hyperbolic group with trivial amenable radical, every intermediate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*$</tex>-subalgebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{B}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{\lambda }^*(\Gamma )\subseteq \mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{A}\rtimes _{r}\Gamma $</tex>, is of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}_1\rtimes _{r}\Gamma $</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}_1$</tex> is a unital <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex>-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*$</tex>-subalgebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Minimal Representation of the Orthosymplectic Lie Supergroup
abstract: We construct a minimal representation of the orthosymplectic Lie supergroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$OSp(p,q|2n)$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p+q$</tex> even, generalizing the Schrödinger model of the minimal representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(p,q)$</tex> to the super case. The underlying Lie algebra representation is realized on functions on the minimal orbit inside the Jordan superalgebra associated with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{osp}(p,q|2n)$</tex>, so that our construction is in line with the orbit philosophy. Its annihilator is given by a Joseph-like ideal for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{osp}(p,q|2n)$</tex>, and therefore the representation is a natural generalization of a minimal representation to the context of Lie superalgebras. We also calculate its Gelfand–Kirillov dimension and construct a nondegenerate sesquilinear form for which the representation is skew-symmetric and which is the analogue of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-inner product in the supercase.

articleTitle: On Automorphisms of Enveloping Algebras
abstract: Given an algebraic Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{g}$</tex> over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{C}$</tex>, we canonically associate to it a Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{L}_{\infty }(\mathfrak{g})$</tex> defined over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{C}_{\infty }$</tex>, the reduction of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{C}$</tex> modulo the infinitely large prime, and show that for a class of Lie algebras, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{L}_{\infty }(\mathfrak{g})$</tex> is an invariant of the derived category of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{g}$</tex>-modules. We give two applications of this construction. First, we show that the bounded derived category of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{g}$</tex>-modules determines algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{g}$</tex> for a class of Lie algebras. Second, given a semi-simple Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{g}$</tex> over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{C}$</tex>, we construct a canonical homomorphism from the group of automorphisms of the enveloping algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{U}\mathfrak{g}$</tex> to the group of Lie algebra automorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{g}$</tex>, such that its kernel does not contain a non-trivial semi-simple automorphism. As a corollary, we obtain that any finite subgroup of automorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{U}\mathfrak{g}$</tex> is isomorphic to a subgroup of Lie algebra automorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{g}.$</tex>

articleTitle: Crystal Basis Theory for a Quantum Symmetric Pair U, Uj
abstract: We study the representation theory of a quantum symmetric pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{U},\mathbf{U}^{\jmath })$</tex> with two parameters <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p,q$</tex> of type AIII, by using highest weight theory and a variant of Kashiwara’s crystal basis theory. Namely, we classify the irreducible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{U}^{\jmath }$</tex>-modules in a suitable category and associate with each of them a basis at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p=q=0$</tex>, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\jmath $</tex>-crystal basis. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\jmath $</tex>-crystal bases have nice combinatorial properties as the ordinary crystal bases do.

articleTitle: The Kodaira Dimension of Contact 3-Manifolds and Geography of Symplectic Fillings
abstract: We introduce the Kodaira dimension of contact 3-manifolds and establish some basic properties. Contact 3-manifolds with distinct Kodaira dimensions behave differently when it comes to the geography of various kinds of symplectic fillings. On the other hand, we also prove that, given any contact 3-manifold, there is a lower bound of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\chi +3\sigma $</tex> for all of its minimal symplectic fillings. This is motivated by Stipsicz’s result in [38] for Stein fillings. Finally, we discuss various aspects of exact self-cobordisms of fillable contact 3-manifolds.

articleTitle: Large-Degree Asymptotics of Rational Painlevé-IV Functions Associated to Generalized Hermite Polynomials
abstract: The Painlevé-IV equation has three families of rational solutions generated by the generalized Hermite polynomials. Each family is indexed by two positive integers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>. These functions have applications to nonlinear wave equations, random matrices, fluid dynamics, and quantum mechanics. Numerical studies suggest the zeros and poles form a deformed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\times m$</tex> rectangular grid. Properly scaled, the zeros and poles appear to densely fill certain curvilinear rectangles as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m,n\to \infty $</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r:=m/n$</tex> a fixed positive real number. Generalizing a method of Bertola and Bothner [2] used to study rational Painlevé-II functions, we express the generalized Hermite rational Painlevé-IV functions in terms of certain non-Hermitian orthogonal polynomials. Using the Deift–Zhou nonlinear steepest-descent method, we asymptotically analyze the associated Riemann–Hilbert problem in the limit <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\to \infty $</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m=r\cdot n$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex> fixed. We obtain an explicit characterization of the boundary curve and determine the leading-order asymptotic expansion of the rational Painlevé-IV functions associated to generalized Hermite polynomials in the pole-free region.

articleTitle: Stacky Hamiltonian Actions and Symplectic Reduction
abstract: We introduce the notion of a Hamiltonian action of an étale Lie group stack on an étale symplectic stack and establish versions of the Kirwan convexity theorem, the Meyer–Marsden–Weinstein symplectic reduction theorem, and the Duistermaat–Heckman theorem in this context.

articleTitle: Erratum to “Visibility and Directions in Quasicrystals”
Quasimaps to Zero-Dimensional A∞-Quiver Varieties
abstract: We consider the moduli spaces of quasimaps to zero-dimensional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{\infty }$</tex> Nakajima quiver varieties. An explicit combinatorial formula for the equivariant Euler characteristic of these moduli spaces is obtained and applications to symplectic duality are discussed.

articleTitle: Homeomorphisms of S1 and Factorization
abstract: For each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n>0$</tex> there is a one complex parameter family of homeomorphisms of the circle consisting of linear fractional transformations “conjugated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \to z^n$</tex>”. We show that these families are free of relations, which determines the structure of “the group of homeomorphisms of finite type”. We next consider factorization for more robust groups of homeomorphisms. We refer to this as root subgroup factorization (because the factors correspond to root subgroups). We are especially interested in how root subgroup factorization is related to triangular factorization (i.e., conformal welding) and correspondences between smoothness properties of the homeomorphisms and decay properties of the root subgroup parameters. This leads to interesting comparisons with Fourier series and the theory of Verblunsky coefficients.

articleTitle: Inhomogeneous Dual Diophantine Approximation on Affine Subspaces
abstract: We prove the convergence and divergence cases of an inhomogeneous Khintchine–Groshev-type theorem for dual approximation restricted to affine subspaces in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R} ^n$</tex>. The divergence results are proved in the more general context of Hausdorff measures.

articleTitle: Prescribed k-Curvature Problems on Complete Noncompact Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: To study the prescribed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-curvature problem of 2nd-order symmetric curvature tensors on complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds, we consider a class of fully nonlinear elliptic partial differential equations. It is proved that on a Riemannian manifold with negative sectional curvature and Ricci curvature bounded from below, the equation is solvable provided that all the eigenvalues of the tensor are negative. The result is applicable to the prescribed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-curvature problems of modified Schouten tensor and Bakry–Émery Ricci tensor.

articleTitle: Combinatorics of Generalized Exponents
abstract: We give a purely combinatorial proof of the positivity of the stabilized forms of the generalized exponents associated to each classical root system. In finite type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{n-1}$</tex>, we rederive the description of the generalized exponents in terms of crystal graphs without using the combinatorics of semistandard tableaux or the charge statistic. In finite type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{n}$</tex>, we obtain a combinatorial description of the generalized exponents based on the so-called distinguished vertices in crystals of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{2n-1}$</tex>, which we also connect to symplectic King tableaux. This gives a combinatorial proof of the positivity of Lusztig <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>-analogs associated to zero-weight spaces in the irreducible representations of symplectic Lie algebras. We also present three applications of our combinatorial formula and discuss some implications to relating two type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> branching rules. Our methods are expected to extend to the orthogonal types.

articleTitle: Low Degree Points on Curves
abstract: In this paper, we investigate an arithmetic analogue of the gonality of a smooth projective curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> over a number field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>: the minimal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e$</tex> such that there are infinitely many points <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P \in C(\bar{k})$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[k(P):k] \leqslant e$</tex>. Developing techniques that make use of an auxiliary smooth surface containing the curve, we show that this invariant can take any value subject to constraints imposed by the gonality. Building on work of Debarre–Klassen, we show that this invariant is equal to the gonality for all sufficiently ample curves on a surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> with trivial irregularity.

articleTitle: The 2-Component BKP Grassmannian and Simple Singularities of Type D
abstract: It was proved in 2010 that the principal Kac–Wakimoto hierarchy of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> is a reduction of the 2-component BKP hierarchy. On the other hand, it is known that the total descendant potential of a singularity of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> is a tau-function of the principal Kac–Wakimoto hierarchy. We find explicitly the point in the Grassmannian of the 2-component BKP hierarchy (in the sense of Shiota) that corresponds to the total descendant potential. We also prove that the space of tau-functions of Gaussian type is parametrized by the base of the miniversal unfolding of the simple singularity of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>.

articleTitle: Sign Changes of Kloosterman Sums with Almost Prime Moduli. II: Corrigendum
abstract: We give a corrigendum to the previous paper [8] and recover the same quantitative statement: the Kloosterman sum changes sign infinitely often as the modulus runs over squarefree numbers with at most seven prime factors.

articleTitle: Berry–Esseen Type Estimate and Return Sequence for Parabolic Iteration in the Upper Half-Plane
abstract: We prove a Berry–Esseen type theorem for the convergence rate in the monotone central limit theorem. When the underlying measure is singular relative to Lebesgue measure, this central limit process is viewed as an infinite measure-preserving dynamical system and we prove that it has a regularly varying return sequence of index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/2$</tex>.

articleTitle: Higher Brackets on Cyclic and Negative Cyclic (Co)Homology
abstract: The purpose of this article is to embed the string topology bracket developed by Chas–Sullivan and Menichi on negative cyclic cohomology groups as well as the dual bracket found by de Thanhoffer de Völcsey–Van den Bergh on negative cyclic homology groups into the global picture of a noncommutative differential (or Cartan) calculus up to homotopy on the (co)cyclic bicomplex in general, in case a certain Poincaré duality is given. For negative cyclic cohomology, this in particular leads to a Batalin–Vilkoviskiĭ (BV) algebra structure on the underlying Hochschild cohomology. In the special case in which this BV bracket vanishes, one obtains an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e_3$</tex>-algebra structure on Hochschild cohomology. The results are given in the general and unifying setting of (opposite) cyclic modules over (cyclic) operads.

articleTitle: Metric Properties of Parabolic Ample Bundles
abstract: We introduce a notion of admissible Hermitian metrics on parabolic bundles and define positivity properties for the same. We develop Chern–Weil theory for parabolic bundles and prove that our metric notions coincide with the already existing algebro-geometric versions of parabolic Chern classes. We also formulate a Griffiths conjecture in the parabolic setting and prove some results that provide evidence in its favor for certain kinds of parabolic bundles. For these kinds of parabolic structures, we prove that the conjecture holds on Riemann surfaces. We also prove that a Berndtsson-type result holds and that there are metrics on stable bundles over surfaces whose Schur forms are positive.

articleTitle: Row Contractions Annihilated by Interpolating Vanishing Ideals
abstract: We study similarity classes of commuting row contractions annihilated by what we call higher-order vanishing ideals of interpolating sequences. Our main result exhibits a Jordan-type direct sum decomposition for these row contractions. We illustrate how the family of ideals to which our theorem applies is very rich, especially in several variables. We also give two applications of the main result. First, we obtain a purely operator theoretic characterization of interpolating sequences for the multiplier algebra of the Drury–Arveson space. Second, we classify certain classes of cyclic commuting row contractions up to quasi-similarity in terms of their annihilating ideals. This refines some of our recent work on the topic. We show how this classification is sharp: in general quasi-similarity cannot be improved to similarity. The obstruction to doing so is a scarcity of norm-controlled similarities between commuting tuples of nilpotent matrices, and we investigate this question in detail.

articleTitle: Fourier Coefficients of Modular Forms of Half-Integral Weight in Arithmetic Progressions
abstract: We study the probabilistic behavior of sums of Fourier coefficients in arithmetic progressions. We prove a result analogous to previous work of Fouvry–Ganguly–Kowalski–Michel and Kowalski–Ricotta in the context of half-integral weight holomorphic cusp forms and for prime power modulus. We actually show that these sums follow in a suitable range a mixed Gaussian distribution that comes from the asymptotic mixed distribution of Salié sums.

articleTitle: Approximable Algebras as Subalgebras of Section Rings
abstract: In [2], Huayi Chen introduced approximable graded algebras, which he uses to prove a Fujita-type theorem in the arithmetic setting, and asked if any such algebra is the graded ring of a big line bundle on a projective variety. This was proved to be false in [8]. Continuing the analysis started in [8], we show that while not every approximable graded algebra is a sub algebra of the section ring of a big line bundle, we can associate to any approximable graded algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{B}$</tex> a projective variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X(\textbf{B})$</tex> and an infinite divisor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D(\textbf{B}) =\sum _{i=1}^\infty a_i D_i$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a_i\rightarrow 0$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{B}$</tex> is a subalgebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*} R( D(\textbf{B}))=\oplus_n H^0(X(\textbf{B}), n D(\textbf{B})).\end{equation*}$$</tex> We also establish a partial converse to these results by showing that if an infinite divisor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D=\sum _i a_iD_i$</tex> converges in the space of numerical classes, then any full-dimensional sub-graded algebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\oplus _mH^0(X, \lfloor mD \rfloor ))$</tex> is approximable.

articleTitle: Rational Picard Group of Moduli of Pointed Hyperelliptic Curves
abstract: We determine the rational divisor class group of the moduli spaces of smooth pointed hyperelliptic curves and of their Deligne–Mumford compactification, over the field of complex numbers.

articleTitle: Principal Actions of Stacky Lie Groupoids
abstract: Stacky Lie groupoids are generalizations of Lie groupoids in which the “space of arrows” of the groupoid is a differentiable stack. In this paper, we consider actions of stacky Lie groupoids on differentiable stacks and their associated quotients. We provide a characterization of principal actions of stacky Lie groupoids, that is, actions whose quotients are again differentiable stacks in such a way that the projection onto the quotient is a principal bundle. As an application, we extend the notion of Morita equivalence of Lie groupoids to the realm of stacky Lie groupoids, providing examples that naturally arise from non-integrable Lie algebroids.

articleTitle: Local Models of Isolated Singularities for Affine Special Kähler Structures in Dimension Two
abstract: We construct local models of isolated singularities for special Kähler structures in real dimension two assuming that the associated holomorphic cubic form does not have essential singularities. As an application we compute the holonomy of the flat symplectic connection, which is a part of the special Kähler structure.

articleTitle: Factorizable Maps and Traces on the Universal Free Product of Matrix Algebras
abstract: We relate factorizable quantum channels on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_n({\mathbb{C}})$</tex>, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \ge 2$</tex>, via their Choi matrix, to certain matrices of correlations, which, in turn, are shown to be parametrized by traces on the unital free product <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_n({\mathbb{C}}) \ast _{\mathbb{C}} M_n({\mathbb{C}})$</tex>. Factorizable maps with a finite dimensional ancilla are parametrized by finite dimensional traces on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_n({\mathbb{C}}) \ast _{\mathbb{C}} M_n({\mathbb{C}})$</tex>, and factorizable maps that approximately factor through finite dimensional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^\ast $</tex>-algebras are parametrized by traces in the closure of the finite dimensional ones. The latter set of traces is shown to be equal to the set of hyperlinear traces on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_n({\mathbb{C}}) \ast _{\mathbb{C}} M_n({\mathbb{C}})$</tex>. We finally show that each metrizable Choquet simplex is a face of the simplex of tracial states on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_n({\mathbb{C}}) \ast _{\mathbb{C}} M_n({\mathbb{C}})$</tex>.

articleTitle: Low Pseudomoments of the Riemann Zeta Function and Its Powers
abstract: The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 q$</tex>-th pseudomoment <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Psi _{2q,\alpha }(x)$</tex> of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex>-th power of the Riemann zeta function is defined to be the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 q$</tex>-th moment of the partial sum up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\zeta ^\alpha $</tex> on the critical line. Using probabilistic methods of Harper, we prove upper and lower bounds for these pseudomoments when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q \le \frac{1}{2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \ge 1$</tex>. Combined with results of Bondarenko et al., these bounds determine the size of all pseudomoments with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q> 0$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \ge 1$</tex> up to powers of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log \log x$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> is the length of the partial sum, and it turns out that there are three different ranges with different growth behaviours. In particular, the results give the order of magnitude of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Psi _{2 q, 1}(x)$</tex> for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q> 0$</tex>.

articleTitle: On the h-Cobordism Category I
abstract: We consider the topological category of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex>-cobordisms between smooth manifolds with boundary and compare its homotopy type with the standard <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex>-cobordism space of a compact smooth manifold.

articleTitle: Topological Moduli Space for Germs of Holomorphic Foliations
abstract: This work deals with the topological classification of germs of singular foliations on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbb{C}^{2},0)$</tex>. Working in a suitable class of foliations we fix the topological invariants given by the separatrix set, the Camacho–Sad indices, and the projective holonomy representations and we compute the moduli space of topological classes in terms of the cohomology of a new algebraic object that we call group-graph. This moduli space may be an infinite-dimensional functional space but under generic conditions we prove that it has finite dimension and we describe its algebraic and topological structure.

articleTitle: On the Boundary Behavior for the Blow-up Solutions of the sinh-Gordon Equation and Rank N Toda Systems in Bounded Domains
abstract: In this paper we are concerned with the blow-up analysis of two classes of problems in bounded domains arising in mathematical physics: sinh-Gordon equation and some general rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> Toda systems. The presence of a residual mass in the blowing up limit makes the analysis quite delicate; nevertheless, by exploiting suitable Pohozaev identities and a detailed blow-up analysis we exclude blowup at the boundary. This is the 1st result in this direction in the presence of a residual mass. As a byproduct we obtain general existence results in bounded domains.

articleTitle: Computing Euler Obstruction Functions Using Maximum Likelihood Degrees
abstract: We give a numerical algorithm computing Euler obstruction functions using maximum likelihood degrees. The maximum likelihood degree is a well-studied property of a variety in algebraic statistics and computational algebraic geometry. In this article we use this degree to give a new way to compute Euler obstruction functions. We define the maximum likelihood obstruction function and show how it coincides with the Euler obstruction function. With this insight, we are able to bring new tools of computational algebraic geometry to study Euler obstruction functions.

articleTitle: The Massive Feynman Propagator on Asymptotically Minkowski Spacetimes II
abstract: We consider the massive Klein–Gordon equation on short-range asymptotically Minkowski spacetimes. Extending our results in [7], we show that the Klein–Gordon operator with Feynman-type boundary conditions at infinite times is invertible and that its inverse, called the Feynman inverse, satisfies the microlocal conditions of Feynman parametrices in the sense of Duistermaat and Hörmander. This supplements the recent work of Vasy [10] with more explicit techniques.

articleTitle: Bykovskii-Type Theorem for the Picard Manifold
abstract: We generalise a result of Bykovskii to the Gaussian integers and prove an asymptotic formula for the prime geodesic theorem in short intervals on the Picard manifold. Previous works show that individually the remainder is bounded by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(X^{13/8+\epsilon })$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(X^{3/2+\theta +\epsilon })$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex> is the subconvexity exponent for quadratic Dirichlet <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Q}(i)$</tex>. By combining arithmetic methods with estimates for a spectral exponential sum and a smooth explicit formula, we obtain an improvement for both of these exponents. Moreover, by assuming two standard conjectures on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions, we show that it is possible to reduce the exponent below the barrier <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3/2$</tex> and get <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(X^{34/23+\epsilon })$</tex> conditionally. We also demonstrate a dependence of the remainder in the short interval estimate on the classical Gauss circle problem for shifted centres.

articleTitle: Exponential Moments and Piecewise Thinning for the Bessel Point Process
abstract: We obtain exponential moment asymptotics for the Bessel point process. As a direct consequence, we improve on the asymptotics for the expectation and variance of the associated counting function and establish several central limit theorems. We show that exponential moment asymptotics can also be interpreted as large gap asymptotics, in the case where we apply the operation of a piecewise constant thinning on several consecutive intervals. We believe our results also provide important estimates for later studies of the global rigidity of the Bessel point process.

articleTitle: A Manin–Mumford Theorem for the Maximal Compact Subgroup of a Universal Vectorial Extension of a Product of Elliptic Curves
abstract: We study the intersection of an algebraic variety with the maximal compact subgroup of a universal vectorial extension of a product of elliptic curves. For this intersection we show a Manin–Mumford-type statement. This answers some questions posed by Corvaja–Masser–Zannier, which arose in connection with their investigation of the intersection of an algebraic curve with the maximal compact subgroup of various algebraic groups. In particular they proved that these intersections are finite for universal vectorial extensions of elliptic curves. Using Khovanskii's zero-estimates combined with a stratification result of Gabrielov–Vorobjov and recent work of the authors, we obtain effective bounds for this intersection that only depend on the degree of the algebraic variety and the dimension of the group. As a corollary, we obtain new uniform results of Manin–Mumford type for additive extensions of certain abelian varieties.

articleTitle: Density of g-Vector Cones From Triangulated Surfaces
abstract: We study <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex>-vector cones associated with clusters of cluster algebras defined from a marked surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S,M)$</tex> of rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>. We determine the closure of the union of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex>-vector cones associated with all clusters. It is equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^n$</tex> except for a closed surface with exactly one puncture, in which case it is equal to the half space of a certain explicit hyperplane in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^n$</tex>. Our main ingredients are laminations on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S,M)$</tex>, their shear coordinates, and their asymptotic behavior under Dehn twists. As an application, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S,M)$</tex> is not a closed surface with exactly one puncture, the exchange graph of cluster tilting objects in the corresponding cluster category is connected. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S,M)$</tex> is a closed surface with exactly one puncture, it has precisely two connected components.

articleTitle: Affine Function-Valued Valuations
abstract: A classification of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{SL}(n)$</tex> contravariant, continuous function-valued valuations on convex bodies is established. Such valuations are natural extensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{SL}(n)$</tex> contravariant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> Minkowski valuations, the classification of which characterized <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> projection bodies, which are fundamental in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> Brunn–Minkowski theory, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p \geq 1$</tex>. Hence, our result will help to better understand extensions of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> Brunn–Minkowski theory. In fact, our results characterize general projection functions, which extend <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> projection functions (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-th powers of the support functions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> projection bodies) to projection functions in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> Brunn–Minkowski theory for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0< p < 1$</tex> and in the Orlicz Brunn–Minkowski theory.

articleTitle: Corrigendum to: “Arithmetic Correlations Over Large Finite Fields”
Abstract Bivariant Cuntz Semigroups
abstract: We show that abstract Cuntz semigroups form a closed symmetric monoidal category. Thus, given Cuntz semigroups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>, there is another Cuntz semigroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\![ S,T ]\!] $</tex> playing the role of morphisms from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>. Applied to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{\ast }$</tex>-algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex>, the semigroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\![ \operatorname{Cu}(A),\operatorname{Cu}(B) ]\!] $</tex> should be considered as the target in analogs of the universal coefficient theorem for bivariant theories of Cuntz semigroups. Abstract bivariant Cuntz semigroups are computable in a number of interesting cases. We also show that order-zero maps between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{\ast }$</tex>-algebras naturally define elements in the respective bivariant Cuntz semigroup.

articleTitle: On Morin Configurations of Higher Length
abstract: This paper studies finite Morin configurations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> of planes in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^5$</tex> having higher length—a question naturally related to the theory of Gushel–Mukai varieties. The uniqueness of the configuration of maximal cardinality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20$</tex> is proven. This is related to the canonical genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6$</tex> curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{\ell }$</tex> union of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10$</tex> lines in a smooth quintic Del Pezzo surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^5$</tex> and to the Petersen graph. More in general an irreducible family of special configurations of length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq 11$</tex>, we name as Morin–Del Pezzo configurations, is considered and studied. This includes the configuration of maximal cardinality and families of configurations of lenght <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq 16$</tex>, previously unknown. It depends on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9$</tex> moduli and is defined via the family of nodal and rational canonical curves of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>. The special relations between Morin–Del Pezzo configurations and the geometry of special threefolds, like the Igusa quartic or its dual Segre primal, are focused.

articleTitle: Spectral Multipliers of Self-Adjoint Operators on Besov and Triebel–Lizorkin Spaces Associated to Operators
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> be a space of homogeneous type and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> be a nonnegative self-adjoint operator on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2(X)$</tex> that satisfies a Gaussian estimate on its heat kernel. In this paper we prove a Hörmander-type spectral multiplier theorem for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> on the Besov and Triebel–Lizorkin spaces associated to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>. Our work not only recovers the boundedness of the spectral multipliers on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^p$</tex> spaces and Hardy spaces associated to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> but also is the 1st one that proves the boundedness of a general spectral multiplier theorem on Besov and Triebel–Lizorkin spaces.

articleTitle: Prescribing Centro-Affine Curvature From One Convex Body to Another
abstract: We study a curvature flow on smooth, closed, strictly convex hypersurfaces in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^n$</tex>, which commutes with the action of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SL(n)$</tex>. The flow shrinks the initial hypersurface to a point that, if rescaled to enclose a domain of constant volume, is a smooth, closed, strictly convex hypersurface in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^n$</tex> with centro-affine curvature proportional, but not always equal, to the centro-affine curvature of a fixed hypersurface. We outline some consequences of this result for the geometry of convex bodies and the logarithmic Minkowski inequality.

articleTitle: Existence of Self-similar Solutions to the Anisotropic Affine Curve-shortening Flow
abstract: In this paper the existence of positive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\pi $</tex>-periodic solutions to the ordinary differential equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*} u^{\prime\prime}+u=\frac{f}{u^3} \ \textrm{ in } \mathbb{R} \end{equation*}$$</tex>is studied, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> is a positive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\pi $</tex>-periodic smooth function. By virtue of a new generalized Blaschke–Santaló inequality, we obtain a new existence result of solutions.

articleTitle: Integration of Differential Graded Manifolds
abstract: We consider the problem of integration of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_\infty $</tex>-algebroids (differential non-negatively graded manifolds) to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_\infty $</tex>-groupoids. We first construct a “big” Kan simplicial manifold (Fréchet or Banach) whose points are solutions of a (generalized) Maurer–Cartan equation. The main analytic trick in our work is an integral transformation sending the solutions of the Maurer–Cartan equation to closed differential forms. Following the ideas of Ezra Getzler, we then impose a gauge condition that cuts out a finite-dimensional simplicial submanifold. This “smaller” simplicial manifold is (the nerve of) a local Lie <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell $</tex>-groupoid. The gauge condition can be imposed only locally in the base of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_\infty $</tex>-algebroid; the resulting local <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell $</tex>-groupoids glue up to a coherent homotopy, that is, we get a homotopy coherent diagram from the nerve of a good cover of the base to the (simplicial) category of local <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell $</tex>-groupoids. Finally, we show that a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-symplectic differential non-negatively graded manifold integrates to a local <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-symplectic Lie <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell$</tex>-groupoid; globally, these assemble to form an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_\infty$</tex>-functor. As a particular case for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k=2$</tex>, we obtain integration of Courant algebroids.

articleTitle: Antisymmetric Paramodular Forms of Weights 2 and 3
abstract: We define an algebraic set in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$23$</tex>-dimensional projective space whose <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb{Q}}}$</tex>-rational points correspond to meromorphic, antisymmetric, paramodular Borcherds products. We know two lines inside this algebraic set. Some rational points on these lines give holomorphic Borcherds products and thus construct examples of Siegel modular forms on degree 2 paramodular groups. Weight <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex> examples provide antisymmetric canonical differential forms on Siegel modular three-folds. Weight <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex> is the minimal weight and these examples, via the paramodular conjecture, give evidence for the modularity of some rank 1 abelian surfaces defined over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Q}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Complex Multiplication in Twistor Spaces
abstract: Despite the transcendental nature of the twistor construction, the algebraic fibres of the twistor space of a K3 surface share certain arithmetic properties. We prove that for a polarised K3 surface with complex multiplication, all algebraic fibres of its twistor space away from the equator have complex multiplication as well.

articleTitle: Multiplicity and Concentration Results for a Magnetic Schrödinger Equation With Exponential Critical Growth in ℝ2
abstract: In this paper we study the following nonlinear Schrödinger equation with magnetic field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{align*} \left(\frac{\varepsilon}{i}\nabla-A(x)\right)^{2}u+V(x)u=f(| u|^{2})u,\quad x\in\mathbb{R}^{2}, \end{align*}$$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon>0$</tex> is a parameter, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V:\mathbb{R}^{2}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A: \mathbb{R}^{2}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{2}$</tex> are continuous potentials, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f:\mathbb{R}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$</tex> has exponential critical growth. Under a local assumption on the potential <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>, by variational methods, penalization technique, and Ljusternik–Schnirelmann theory, we prove multiplicity and concentration of solutions for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon $</tex> small.

articleTitle: Uniformizing the Moduli Stacks of Global G-Shtukas
abstract: This is the 2nd in a sequence of articles, in which we explore moduli stacks of global <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{G}$</tex>-shtukas, the function field analogs for Shimura varieties. Here <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{G}$</tex> is a flat affine group scheme of finite type over a smooth projective curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> over a finite field. Global <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{G}$</tex>-shtukas are generalizations of Drinfeld shtukas and analogs of abelian varieties with additional structure. We prove that the moduli stacks of global <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{G}$</tex>-shtukas are algebraic Deligne–Mumford stacks separated and locally of finite type. They generalize various moduli spaces used by different authors to prove instances of the Langlands program over function fields. In the 1st article we explained the relation between global <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{G}$</tex>-shtukas and local <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb{P}}}$</tex>-shtukas, which are the function field analogs of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-divisible groups. Here <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb{P}}}$</tex> is the base change of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{G}$</tex> to the complete local ring at a point of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb{P}}}$</tex> is smooth with connected reductive generic fiber we proved the existence of Rapoport–Zink spaces for local <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb{P}}}$</tex>-shtukas. In the present article we use these spaces to (partly) uniformize the moduli stacks of global <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{G}$</tex>-shtukas for smooth <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{G}$</tex> with connected fibers and reductive generic fiber. This is our main result. It has applications to the analog of the Langlands–Rapoport conjecture for our moduli stacks.

articleTitle: Energy Counterexamples in Two Weight Calderón–Zygmund Theory
abstract: We show that the energy conditions are not necessary for boundedness of Riesz transforms in dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 2$</tex>. In dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=1$</tex>, we construct an elliptic singular integral operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\flat } $</tex> for which the energy conditions are not necessary for boundedness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\flat }$</tex>. The convolution kernel <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{\flat }\left ( x\right ) $</tex> of the operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\flat }$</tex> is a smooth flattened version of the Hilbert transform kernel <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K\left ( x\right ) =\frac{1}{x}$</tex> that satisfies ellipticity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \vert K_{\flat }\left ( x\right ) \vert \gtrsim \frac{1}{\left \vert x\right \vert }$</tex>, but not gradient ellipticity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \vert K_{\flat }^{\prime }\left ( x\right ) \vert \gtrsim \frac{1}{ \vert x \vert ^{2}}$</tex>. Indeed the kernel has flat spots where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{\flat }^{\prime }\left ( x\right ) =0$</tex> on a family of intervals, but <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{\flat }^{\prime }\left ( x\right ) $</tex> is otherwise negative on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}\setminus \left \{ 0\right \} $</tex>. On the other hand, if a one-dimensional kernel <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K\left ( x,y\right ) $</tex> is both elliptic and gradient elliptic, then the energy conditions are necessary, and so by our theorem in [30], the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T1$</tex> theorem holds for such kernels on the line. This paper includes results from arXiv:16079.06071v3 and arXiv:1801.03706v2.

articleTitle: Singular Curves of Low Degree and Multifiltrations from Osculating Spaces
abstract: In order to study projections of smooth curves, we introduce multifiltrations obtained by combining flags of osculating spaces. We classify all configurations of singularities occurring for a projection of a smooth curve embedded by a complete linear system away from a projective linear space of dimension at most two. In particular, we determine all configurations of singularities of non-degenerate degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> rational curves in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{P}^n$</tex> when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d-n\leq 3$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d<2n$</tex>. Along the way, we describe the Schubert cycles giving rise to these projections. We also reprove a special case of the Castelnuovo bound using these multifiltrations: under the assumption <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d<2n$</tex>, the arithmetic genus of any non-degenerate degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> curve in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{P}^n$</tex> is at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d-n$</tex>.

articleTitle: Affinoids in the Lubin–Tate Perfectoid Space and Simple Supercuspidal Representations I: Tame Case
abstract: We construct a family of affinoids in the Lubin–Tate perfectoid space and their formal models such that the middle cohomology of the reductions of the formal models realizes the local Langlands correspondence and the local Jacquet-Langlands correspondence for simple supercuspidal representations in the case where the dimension of Galois representations is prime to the residue characteristic. The reductions of the formal models are isomorphic to the perfections of Artin–Schreier varieties associated to quadratic forms.

articleTitle: Frobenius Splitting of Thick Flag Manifolds of Kac–Moody Algebras
abstract: We explain that the Plücker relations provide the defining equations of the thick flag manifold associated to a Kac–Moody algebra. This naturally transplants the result of Kumar–Mathieu–Schwede about the Frobenius splitting of thin flag varieties to the thick case. As a consequence, we provide a description of the space of global sections of a line bundle of a thick Schubert variety as conjectured in Kashiwara–Shimozono [13]. This also yields the existence of a compatible basis of thick Demazure modules and the projective normality of the thick Schubert varieties.

articleTitle: An Action of the Polishchuk Differential Operator via Punctured Surfaces
abstract: For a family of Jacobians of smooth pointed curves, there is a notion of tautological algebra. There is an action of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathfrak{s}}l_2$</tex> on this algebra. We define and study a lifting of the Polishchuk operator, corresponding to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathfrak{f}} \in{\mathfrak{s}}l_2$</tex>, on an algebra consisting of punctured Riemann surfaces. As an application, we compare a class of tautological relations on moduli of curves, discovered by Faber and Zagier and relations on the universal Jacobian. We prove that the so called top Faber–Zagier relations come from a class of relations on the Jacobian side.

articleTitle: Nontangential Estimates on Layer Potentials and the Neumann Problem for Higher-Order Elliptic Equations
abstract: We solve the Neumann problem, with nontangential estimates, for higher-order divergence form elliptic operators with variable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>-independent coefficients. Our results are accompanied by nontangential estimates on higher-order layer potentials.

articleTitle: Full Exceptional Collections on Lagrangian Grassmannians
abstract: We show fullness of the exceptional collections of maximal length constructed by Kuznetsov and Polishchuk in the bounded derived categories of coherent sheaves on Lagrangian Grassmannians.

articleTitle: Global Rigidity of 2D Linearly Constrained Frameworks
abstract: A linearly constrained framework in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^d$</tex> is a point configuration together with a system of constraints that fixes the distances between some pairs of points and additionally restricts some of the points to lie in given affine subspaces.
