It is globally rigid if the configuration is uniquely defined by the constraint system. We show that a generic linearly constrained framework in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^2$</tex> is globally rigid if and only if it is redundantly rigid and “balanced”. For unbalanced generic frameworks, we determine the precise number of solutions to the constraint system whenever the rigidity matroid of the framework is connected. We obtain a stress matrix sufficient condition and a Hendrickson type necessary condition for a generic linearly constrained framework to be globally rigid in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^d$</tex>.

articleTitle: General Variational Formulas for Abelian Differentials
abstract: We use the jump problem technique developed in a recent paper [9] to compute the variational formula of any stable differential and its periods to arbitrary precision in plumbing coordinates. In particular, we give the explicit variational formula for the degeneration of the period matrix, easily reproving the results of Yamada [21] for nodal curves with one node and extending them to an arbitrary stable curve. Concrete examples are included. We also apply the same technique to give an alternative proof of the sufficiency part of the theorem in [1] on the closures of strata of differentials with prescribed multiplicities of zeroes and poles.

articleTitle: Hyperelliptic d-Tangential Covers and d× d-Matrix KdV Elliptic Solitons
abstract: More than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$40$</tex> years ago I. Krichever developed the Theory of (vector) Baker–Akhiezer functions and devised a criterion for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-marked compact Riemann surface to provide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\times d$</tex>-matrix solutions to the KdV equation. Later on he also found a criterion for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-marked curve to provide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\times d$</tex>-matrix solutions to the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (KP) equation, doubly periodic with respect to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex>, the 1st KP flow. In particular, when both criteria apply, one should obtain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\times d$</tex>-matrix KdV elliptic solitons. It seems, however, that the latter issue has been completely neglected until very recently (cf. [10] where the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d=2$</tex> case is treated). In this article we fix a complex elliptic curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X=\mathbb{C}/\Lambda$</tex>, corresponding to a lattice <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda \subset \mathbb{C}$</tex>, and define so-called hyperelliptic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-tangential covers as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-marked covers of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> satisfying a geometric condition inside their Jacobians. They satisfy Krichever’s criteria and give rise, therefore, to families of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\times d$</tex>-matrix KdV elliptic solitons. We also construct an anticanonical rational surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal S}$</tex> naturally attached to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>, with a Picard group of rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10$</tex>. It turns out that the former covers of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> correspond to rational irreducible curves in suitable divisor classes of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal S}$</tex>. We thus reduce their construction to proving that the associated Severi Varieties (of rational irreducible nodal curves) are not empty. The final key to the problem consists in finding rational reducible nodal curves in the latter divisor classes that can be deformed to irreducible ones, according to A. Tannenbaum’s criterion (see [5]). At last we deduce, for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geq 2$</tex>, infinite families (of arbitrary high genus and degree) of hyperelliptic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-tangential covers, giving rise to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\times d$</tex>-matrix KdV elliptic solitons.

articleTitle: Distances and Intersections of Curves
abstract: We obtain a coarse relationship between geometric intersection numbers of curves and the sum of their subsurface projection distances with explicit quasi-constants. By using this relationship, we study intersection numbers of curves contained in geodesics in the curve graph. Furthermore, we generalize a well-known result on intersection number growth of curves under iteration of Dehn twists and multitwists for all kinds of pure mapping classes.

articleTitle: Finite-Dimensional Representations of Yangians in Complex Rank
abstract: We classify the “finite-dimensional” irreducible representations of the Yangians <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y(\mathfrak{g}\mathfrak{l}_t)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y(\mathfrak{s}\mathfrak{l}_t)$</tex>. These are associative ind-algebras in the Deligne category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{Rep}(GL_t)$</tex>, which generalize the regular Yangians <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y(\mathfrak{g}\mathfrak{l}_n)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y(\mathfrak{s}\mathfrak{l}_n)$</tex> to complex rank. They were first defined in the paper [14]. Here we solve [14, Problem 7.2]. We work with the Deligne category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{Rep}(GL_t)$</tex> using the ultraproduct approach introduced in [7] and [16].

articleTitle: K-Theoretic Generalized Donaldson–Thomas Invariants
abstract: We introduce the notion of almost perfect obstruction theory on a Deligne–Mumford stack and show that stacks with almost perfect obstruction theories have virtual structure sheaves, which are deformation invariant. The main components in the construction are an induced embedding of the coarse moduli sheaf of the intrinsic normal cone into the associated obstruction sheaf stack and the construction of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-theoretic Gysin map for sheaf stacks. We show that many stacks of interest admit almost perfect obstruction theories. As a result, we are able to define virtual structure sheaves and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-theoretic classical and generalized Donaldson–Thomas invariants of sheaves and complexes on Calabi–Yau three-folds.

articleTitle: Real Tropicalization and Analytification of Semialgebraic Sets
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> be a real closed field with a nontrivial non-archimedean absolute value. We study a refined version of the tropicalization map, which we call real tropicalization map, that takes into account the signs on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>. We study images of semialgebraic subsets of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K^n$</tex> under this map from a general point of view. For a semialgebraic set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S \subseteq K^n$</tex> we define a space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_r^{{\operatorname{an}}}$</tex> called the real analytification, which we show to be homeomorphic to the inverse limit of all real tropicalizations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>. We prove a real analogue of the tropical fundamental theorem and show that the tropicalization of any semialgebraic set is described by tropicalization of finitely many inequalities, which are valid on the semialgebraic set. We also study the topological properties of real analytification and tropicalization. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is an algebraic variety, we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_r^{{\operatorname{an}}}$</tex> can be canonically embedded into the real spectrum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_r$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>, and we study its relation with the Berkovich analytification of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>.

articleTitle: Multiplicity One for Pairs of Prasad–Takloo-Bighash Type
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{E}}/{\textrm{F}}$</tex> be a quadratic extension of non-archimedean local fields of characteristic different from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{A}}$</tex> be an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{F}}$</tex>-central simple algebra of even dimension so that it contains <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{E}}$</tex> as a subfield, set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{G}}={\textrm{A}}^\times $</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{H}}$</tex> for the centralizer of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{E}}^\times $</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{G}}$</tex>. Using a Galois descent argument, we prove that all double cosets <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{H}} g {\textrm{H}}\subset{\textrm{G}}$</tex> are stable under the anti-involution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\mapsto g^{-1}$</tex>, reducing to Guo's result for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{F}}$</tex>-split <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{G}}$</tex> [14], which we extend to fields of positive characteristic different from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>. We then show, combining global and local results, that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{H}}$</tex>-distinguished irreducible representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{G}}$</tex> are self-dual and this implies that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\textrm{G}},{\textrm{H}})$</tex> is a Gelfand pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*}\operatorname{dim}_{\mathbb{C}}(\operatorname{Hom}_{{\textrm{H}}}(\pi,\mathbb{C}))\leq 1\end{equation*}$$</tex>for all smooth irreducible representations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi $</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{G}}$</tex>. Finally we explain how to obtain the multiplicity one statement in the archimedean case using the criteria of Aizenbud and Gourevitch ([1]), and we then show self-duality of irreducible distinguished representations in the archimedean case too.

articleTitle: Geometric Realization of Dynkin Quiver Type Quantum Affine Schur–Weyl Duality
abstract: For a Dynkin quiver <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathsf{ADE}$</tex> and a sum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta $</tex> of simple roots, we construct a bimodule over the quantum loop algebra and the quiver Hecke algebra of the corresponding type via equivariant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-theory, imitating Ginzburg–Reshetikhin–Vasserot’s geometric realization of the quantum affine Schur–Weyl duality. Our construction is based on Hernandez–Leclerc’s isomorphism between a certain graded quiver variety and the space of representations of the quiver <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> of dimension vector <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta $</tex>. We identify the functor induced from our bimodule with Kang–Kashiwara–Kim’s generalized quantum affine Schur–Weyl duality functor. As a by-product, we verify a conjecture by Kang–Kashiwara–Kim on the simpleness of some poles of normalized <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>-matrices for any quiver <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathsf{ADE}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Local BPS Invariants: Enumerative Aspects and Wall-Crossing
abstract: We study the BPS invariants for local del Pezzo surfaces, which can be obtained as the signed Euler characteristic of the moduli spaces of stable one-dimensional sheaves on the surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>. We calculate the Poincaré polynomials of the moduli spaces for the curve classes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta $</tex> having arithmetic genus at most 2. We formulate a conjecture that these Poincaré polynomials are divisible by the Poincaré polynomials of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$((-K_S).\beta -1)$</tex>-dimensional projective space. This conjecture motivates the upcoming work on log BPS numbers [8].

articleTitle: Smooth Equivalence of Deformations of Domains in Complex Euclidean Spaces
abstract: We prove that two smooth families of 2-connected domains in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{C}$</tex> are smoothly equivalent if they are equivalent under a possibly discontinuous family of biholomorphisms. We construct, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\infty > m \geq 3$</tex>, two smooth families of smoothly bounded <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>-connected domains in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{C}$</tex>, and for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 2$</tex>, two families of strictly pseudoconvex domains in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{C}^n$</tex>, which are equivalent under discontinuous families of biholomorphisms but not under any continuous family of biholomorphisms. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for the smooth equivalence of two smooth families of domains.

articleTitle: Grove Arctic Curves from Periodic Cluster Modular Transformations
abstract: Groves are spanning forests of a finite region of the triangular lattice that are in bijection with Laurent monomials that arise in solutions of the cube recurrence. We introduce a large class of probability measures on groves for which we can compute exact generating functions for edge probabilities. Using the machinery of asymptotics of multivariate generating functions, this lets us explicitly compute arctic curves, generalizing the arctic circle theorem of Petersen and Speyer. Our class of probability measures is sufficiently general that the limit shapes exhibit all solid and gaseous phases expected from the classification of ergodic Gibbs measures in the resistor network model.

articleTitle: Corrigendum to: A Riemann–Hilbert Problem Approach to Infinite Gap Hill's Operators and the Korteweg–de Vries Equation
An Energy Bound in the Affine Group
abstract: We prove a nontrivial energy bound for a finite set of affine transformations over a general field and discuss a number of implications. These include new bounds on growth in the affine group, a quantitative version of a theorem by Elekes about rich lines in grids. We also give a positive answer to a question of Yufei Zhao that for a plane point set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> for which no line contains a positive proportion of points from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex>, there may be at most one line, meeting the set of lines defined by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> in at most a constant multiple of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|P|$</tex> points.

articleTitle: Excursions of Generic Geodesics in Right-Angled Artin Groups and Graph Products
abstract: Motivated by the notion of cusp excursion in geometrically finite hyperbolic manifolds, we define a notion of excursion in any subgroup of a given group and study its asymptotic distribution for right-angled Artin groups (RAAGs) and graph products. In particular, for any irreducible RAAG we show that with respect to the counting measure, the maximal excursion of a generic geodesic in any flat tends to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log n$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> is the length of the geodesic. In this regard, irreducible RAAGs behave like a free product of groups. In fact, we show that the asymptotic distribution of excursions detects the growth rate of the RAAG and whether it is reducible.

articleTitle: Algebraic Cycles and Residues of Degree 8 L-functions of GSp(4) × GL(2)
abstract: We prove a cohomological formula for noncritical residues of degree 8 automorphic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{GSp}(4) \times \mathrm{GL}(2)$</tex> in the spirit of Beilinson conjecture. We rely on the cohomological interpretation of an automorphic period integral and on the study of Novodvorsky’s integral representation of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions.

articleTitle: Chow Motives Without Projectivity, II
abstract: The purpose of this article is to provide a simplified construction of the intermediate extension of a Chow motive, provided that a condition on absence of weights in the boundary is satisfied. We give a criterion, which guarantees the validity of the condition, and compare our new construction to the theory of the interior motive established earlier. We finish the article with a review of the known applications to the boundary of Shimura varieties.

articleTitle: Vanishing of Symplectic Homology and Obstruction to Flexible Fillability
abstract: For any asymptotically dynamically convex contact manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>, we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SH_{\ast }(W)=0$</tex> is a property independent of the choice of topologically simple (i.e., <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_1(W)=0$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi _{1}(Y)\rightarrow \pi _1(W)$</tex> is injective) Liouville filling <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex>. In particular, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> is the boundary of a flexible Weinstein domain, then any topologically simple Liouville filling <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> has vanishing symplectic homology. As a consequence, we answer a question of Lazarev partially: a contact manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> admitting flexible fillings determines the integral cohomology of all the topologically simple Liouville fillings of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>. The vanishing result provides an obstruction to flexible fillability. As an application, we show that all Brieskorn manifolds of dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ge 5$</tex> cannot be filled by flexible Weinstein manifolds.

articleTitle: Gromov–Witten Theory of Toric Birational Transformations
abstract: We investigate the effect of a general toric wall crossing on genus zero Gromov–Witten theory. Given two complete toric orbifolds <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_{+}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_{-}$</tex> related by wall crossing under variation of geometric invariant theory quotients, we prove that their respective <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex>-functions are related by linear transformation and asymptotic expansion. We use this comparison to deduce a similar result for birational complete intersections in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_{+}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_{-}$</tex>. This extends the work of the previous authors in [2] to the case of complete intersections in toric varieties and generalizes some of the results of Coates–Iritani–Jiang [15] on the crepant transformation conjecture to the setting of non-zero discrepancy.

articleTitle: Irreducible Representations of the Group of Unipotent Matrices of Order 4 over Integers
abstract: We study a coarse moduli space of irreducible representations of the group of unipotent matrices of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4$</tex> over the ring of integers that have finite weight. All such representations are known to be monomial (see [4]). To describe a coarse moduli space of such representations, we need to study pairs of subgroups and their characters, which induce non-isomorphic irreducible representations. We obtain a full classification of such pairs and, respectively, a coarse moduli space.

articleTitle: Deformation Cones of Nested Braid Fans
abstract: Generalized permutohedra are deformations of regular permutohedra and arise in many different fields of mathematics. One important characterization of generalized permutohedra is the Submodularity Theorem, which is related to the deformation cone of the Braid fan. We lay out general techniques for determining deformation cones of a fixed polytope and apply it to the Braid fan to obtain a natural combinatorial proof for the Submodularity Theorem. We also consider a refinement of the Braid fan, called the nested Braid fan, and construct usual (respectively, generalized) nested permutohedra that have the nested Braid fan as (respectively, a coarsening of) their normal fan. We extend many results on generalized permutohedra to this new family of polytopes, including a one-to-one correspondence between faces of nested permutohedra and chains in ordered partition posets, and a theorem analogous to the Submodularity Theorem. Finally, we show that the nested Braid fan is the barycentric subdivision of the Braid fan, which gives another way to construct this new combinatorial object.

articleTitle: Total Variation Distance Estimates via L2-Norm for Polynomials in Log-concave Random Vectors
abstract: This paper provides an estimate of the total variation distance between distributions of polynomials defined on a space equipped with a logarithmically concave measure in terms of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-distance between these polynomials.

articleTitle: Boolean Product Polynomials, Schur Positivity, and Chern Plethysm
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k \leq n$</tex> be positive integers, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_n = (x_1, \dots , x_n)$</tex> be a list of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> variables. The Boolean product polynomial  <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{n,k}(X_n)$</tex> is the product of the linear forms <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum _{i \in S} x_i$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> ranges over all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-element subsets of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{1, 2, \dots , n\}$</tex>. We prove that Boolean product polynomials are Schur positive. We do this via a new method of proving Schur positivity using vector bundles and a symmetric function operation we call Chern plethysm. This gives a geometric method for producing a vast array of Schur positive polynomials whose Schur positivity lacks (at present) a combinatorial or representation theoretic proof. We relate the polynomials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{n,k}(X_n)$</tex> for certain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> to other combinatorial objects including derangements, positroids, alternating sign matrices, and reverse flagged fillings of a partition shape. We also relate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{n,n-1}(X_n)$</tex> to a bigraded action of the symmetric group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathfrak{S}}_n$</tex> on a divergence free quotient of superspace.

articleTitle: Conformally Kähler, Einstein–Maxwell Metrics and Boundedness of the Modified Mabuchi Functional
abstract: We prove that if a compact smooth polarized complex manifold admits in the corresponding Hodge Kähler class, a conformally Kähler, Einstein–Maxwell (cKEM) metric, or more generally, a Kähler metric of constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\xi , a, p)$</tex>-scalar curvature in the sense of [2] and [31], then this metric minimizes the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\xi ,a,p)$</tex>-Mabuchi functional introduced in [31]. Our method of proof extends the approach introduced by Donaldson [21, 22] and developed by Li [35] and Sano and Tipler [39], via finite dimensional approximations and generalized balanced metrics. As an application of our result and the recent construction of Koca–T⊘nnesen-Friedman [30], we describe the Kähler classes on a geometrically ruled complex surface of genus greater than twothat admit cKEM metrics.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Properties of the Set of Systoles of Arithmetic Riemann Surfaces
abstract: The purpose this article is to try to understand the mysterious coincidence between the asymptotic behavior of the volumes of the Moduli Space of closed hyperbolic surfaces of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> with respect to the Weil–Petersson metric and the asymptotic behavior of the number of arithmetic closed hyperbolic surfaces of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex>. If the set of arithmetic surfaces is well distributed then its image for any interesting function should be well distributed too. We investigate the distribution of the function systole. We give several results indicating that the systoles of arithmetic surfaces cannot be concentrated, consequently the same holds for the set of arithmetic surfaces. The proofs are based on different techniques: combinatorics (obtaining regular graphs with any girth from results of B. Bollobas and constructions with cages and Ramanujan graphs), group theory (constructing finite index subgroups of surface groups from finite index subgroups of free groups using results of G. Baumslag), and geometric group theory (linking the geometry of graphs with the geometry of coverings of a surface).

articleTitle: Nonlinear Weakly Sequentially Continuous Embeddings Between Banach Spaces
abstract: In these notes, we study nonlinear embeddings between Banach spaces that are also weakly sequentially continuous. In particular, our main result implies that if a Banach space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> coarsely (resp. uniformly) embeds into a Banach space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> by a weakly sequentially continuous map, then every spreading model <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(e_n)_n$</tex> of a normalized weakly null sequence in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> satisfies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$ \|e_1+\ldots+e_k\|_{\overline{\delta}_Y}\lesssim\|e_1+\ldots+e_k\|_S,$$</tex>where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\delta }_Y$</tex> is the modulus of asymptotic uniform convexity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>. Among other results, we obtain Banach spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> so that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> coarsely (resp. uniformly) embeds into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>, but so that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> cannot be mapped into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> by a weakly sequentially continuous coarse (resp. uniform) embedding.

articleTitle: Sharp Area Bounds for Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces in Conformally Euclidean Balls
abstract: We prove that the area of a free boundary minimal surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma ^2 \subset B^n$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B^n$</tex> is a geodesic ball contained in a round hemisphere <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^n_+$</tex>, is at least as big as that of a geodesic disk with the same radius as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B^n$</tex>; equality is attained only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma $</tex> coincides with such a disk. More generally, we prove analogous results for a class of conformally euclidean ambient spaces. This follows works of Brendle and Fraser–Schoen in the euclidean setting.

articleTitle: Functions of Bounded Variation on Complete and Connected One-Dimensional Metric Spaces
abstract: In this paper, we study functions of bounded variation on a complete and connected metric space with finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure. The definition of BV functions on a compact interval based on pointwise variation is extended to this general setting. We show this definition of BV functions is equivalent to the BV functions introduced by Miranda [18]. Furthermore, we study the necessity of conditions on the underlying space in Federer's characterization of sets of finite perimeter on metric measure spaces. In particular, our examples show that the doubling and Poincaré inequality conditions are essential in showing that a set has finite perimeter if the codimension one Hausdorff measure of the measure-theoretic boundary is finite.

articleTitle: Polynomial Birth–Death Processes and the 2nd Conjecture of Valent
abstract: The conjecture of Valent about the type of Jacobi matrices with polynomially growing weights is proved.

articleTitle: Thue Inequalities With Few Coefficients
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F(x, y)$</tex> be a binary form with integer coefficients, degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 3$</tex>, and irreducible over the rationals. Suppose that only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s + 1$</tex> of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n + 1$</tex> coefficients of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> are nonzero. We show that the Thue inequality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|F(x,y)|\leq m$</tex> has <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ll s m^{2/n}$</tex> solutions provided that the absolute value of the discriminant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D(F)$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> is large enough. We also give a new upper bound for the number of solutions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|F(x,y)|\leq m$</tex>, with no restriction on the discriminant of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> that depends mainly on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>, and slightly on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>. Our bound becomes independent of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m<|D(F)|^{2/(5(n-1))}$</tex>, and also independent of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|D(F)|$</tex> is large enough.

articleTitle: A Tannakian Framework for G-displays and Rapoport–Zink Spaces
abstract: We develop a Tannakian framework for group-theoretic analogs of displays, originally introduced by Bültel and Pappas, and further studied by Lau. We use this framework to define Rapoport–Zink functors associated to triples <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(G,\{\mu \},[b])$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is a flat affine group scheme over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{Z}}_p$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex> is a cocharacter of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> defined over a finite unramified extension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{Z}}_p$</tex>. We prove these functors give a quotient stack presented by Witt vector loop groups, thereby showing our definition generalizes the group-theoretic definition of Rapoport–Zink spaces given by Bültel and Pappas. As an application, we prove a special case of a conjecture of Bültel and Pappas by showing their definition coincides with that of Rapoport and Zink in the case of unramified EL-type local Shimura data.

articleTitle: On Cogrowth, Amenability, and the Spectral Radius of a Random Walk on a Semigroup
abstract: We introduce two natural notions of cogrowth for finitely generated semigroups —one local and one global — and study their relationship with amenability and random walks. We establish the minimal and maximal possible values for cogrowth rates, and show that nonmonogenic-free semigroups are exactly characterised by minimal global cogrowth. We consider the relationship with cogrowth for groups and with amenability of semigroups. We also study the relationship with random walks on finitely generated semigroups, and in particular the spectral radius of the associated Markov operators (when defined) on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell _2$</tex>-spaces. We show that either of maximal global cogrowth or the weak F⊘lner condition suffices for the spectral radius to be at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>; since left amenability implies the weak F⊘lner condition, this represents a generalisation to semigroups of one implication of Kesten’s Theorem for groups. By combining with known results about amenability, we are able to establish a number of new sufficient conditions for (left or right) amenability in broad classes of semigroups. In particular, maximal local cogrowth left implies amenability in any left reversible semigroup, while maximal global cogrowth (which is a much weaker property) suffices for left amenability in an extremely broad class of semigroups encompassing all inverse semigroups, left reversible left cancellative semigroups and left reversible regular semigroups.

articleTitle: On the Finiteness of Quantum K-Theory of a Homogeneous Space
abstract: We show that the product in the quantum K-ring of a generalized flag manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G/P$</tex> involves only finitely many powers of the Novikov variables. In contrast to previous approaches to this finiteness question, we exploit the finite difference module structure of quantum K-theory. At the core of the proof is a bound on the asymptotic growth of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex>-function, which in turn comes from an analysis of the singularities of the zastava spaces studied in geometric representation theory. An appendix by H. Iritani establishes the equivalence between finiteness and a quadratic growth condition on certain shift operators.

articleTitle: No Singular Modulus Is a Unit
abstract: A result of the 2nd-named author states that there are only finitely many complex multiplication (CM)-elliptic curves over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{C}$</tex> whose <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$j$</tex>-invariant is an algebraic unit. His proof depends on Duke’s equidistribution theorem and is hence noneffective. In this article, we give a completely effective proof of this result. To be precise, we show that every singular modulus that is an algebraic unit is associated with a CM-elliptic curve whose endomorphism ring has discriminant less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{15}$</tex>. Through further refinements and computer-assisted arguments, we eventually rule out all remaining cases, showing that no singular modulus is an algebraic unit. This allows us to exhibit classes of subvarieties in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{C}}^n$</tex> not containing any special points.

articleTitle: Exponential Concentration for Zeroes of Stationary Gaussian Processes
abstract: We show that for any centered stationary Gaussian process of absolutely integrable covariance, whose spectral measure has compact support, or finite exponential moments (and some additional regularity), the number of zeroes of the process in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[0,T]$</tex> is within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta T$</tex> of its mean value, up to an exponentially small in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> probability.

articleTitle: Multilinear Estimates for Calderón Commutators
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the multilinear boundedness properties of the higher (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-th) order Calderón commutator for dimensions larger than two. We establish all multilinear endpoint estimates for the target space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{\frac{d}{d+n},\infty }(\mathbb{R}^d)$</tex>, including that Calderón commutator maps the product of Lorentz spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{d,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)\times \cdots \times L^{d,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)\times L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{\frac{d}{d+n},\infty }(\mathbb{R}^d)$</tex>, which is the higher dimensional nontrivial generalization of the endpoint estimate that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-th order Calderón commutator maps <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{1}(\mathbb{R})\times \cdots \times L^{1}(\mathbb{R})\times L^1(\mathbb{R})$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{\frac{1}{1+n},\infty }(\mathbb{R})$</tex>. When considering the target space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{r}(\mathbb{R}^d)$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r<\frac{d}{d+n}$</tex>, some counterexamples are given to show that these multilinear estimates may not hold. The method in the present paper seems to have a wide range of applications and it can be applied to establish the similar results for Calderón commutator with a rough homogeneous kernel.

articleTitle: Gradient Estimates on Dirichlet and Neumann Eigenfunctions
abstract: By methods of stochastic analysis on Riemannian manifolds, we derive explicit constants <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_1(D)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_2(D)$</tex> for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-dimensional compact Riemannian manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> with boundary such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_1(D)\sqrt \lambda \|\phi \|_\infty \leqslant \|\nabla \phi \|_\infty \leqslant c_2(D)\sqrt \lambda \|\phi \|_\infty $</tex> holds for any Dirichlet eigenfunction <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi $</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\Delta $</tex> with eigenvalue <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda $</tex>. In particular, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> is convex with nonnegative Ricci curvature, the estimate holds for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_1(D)= 1/{d\mathrm{e}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_2(D)=\sqrt{\mathrm{e}}\left (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{\pi }}+\frac{\sqrt{\pi }}{4\sqrt{2}}\right ).$</tex> Corresponding two-sided gradient estimates for Neumann eigenfunctions are derived in the second part of the paper.

articleTitle: Lattice Simplices with a Fixed Positive Number of Interior Lattice Points: A Nearly Optimal Volume Bound
abstract: We give an explicit upper bound on the volume of lattice simplices with fixed positive number of interior lattice points. The bound differs from the conjectural sharp upper bound only by a linear factor in the dimension. This improves significantly upon the previously best results by Pikhurko from 2001.

articleTitle: A Theorem About Maximal Cohen–Macaulay Modules
abstract: It is shown that for any local strongly <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>-regular ring there exists natural number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e_0$</tex> so that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> is any finitely generated maximal Cohen–Macaulay module, then the pushforward of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> under the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e_0$</tex>th iterate of the Frobenius endomorphism contains a free summand. Consequently, the torsion subgroup of the divisor class group of a local strongly <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>-regular ring is finite.

articleTitle: Hyperboloidal Similarity Coordinates and a Globally Stable Blowup Profile for Supercritical Wave Maps
abstract: We consider co-rotational wave maps from (1+3)-dimensional Minkowski space into the three-sphere. This model exhibits an explicit blowup solution, and we prove the asymptotic nonlinear stability of this solution in the whole space under small perturbations of the initial data. The key ingredient is the introduction of a novel coordinate system that allows one to track the evolution past the blowup time and almost up to the Cauchy horizon of the singularity. As a consequence, we also obtain a result on continuation beyond blowup.

articleTitle: On the Monodromy of Meromorphic Cyclic Opers on the Riemann Sphere
abstract: We study the monodromy of meromorphic cyclic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{SL}(n,{\mathbb{C}})$</tex>-opers on the Riemann sphere with a single pole. We prove that the monodromy map, sending such an oper to its Stokes data, is an immersion in the case where the order of the pole is a multiple of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>. To do this, we develop a method based on the work of Jimbo, Miwa, and Ueno from the theory of isomonodromic deformations. Specifically, we introduce a system of equations that is equivalent to the isomonodromy equations of Jimbo–Miwa–Ueno, but which is adapted to the decomposition of the Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{sl}(n,\mathbb{C})$</tex> as a direct sum of irreducible representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$</tex>. Using properties of some structure constants for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{sl}(n,\mathbb{C})$</tex> to analyze this system of equations, we show that deformations of certain families of cyclic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{C})$</tex>-opers on the Riemann sphere with a single pole are never infinitesimally isomonodromic.

articleTitle: Constraining Images of Quadratic Arboreal Representations
abstract: In this paper, we prove several results on finitely generated dynamical Galois groups attached to quadratic polynomials. First, we show that, over global fields, quadratic post-critically finite (PCF) polynomials are precisely those having an arboreal representation whose image is topologically finitely generated. To obtain this result, we also prove the quadratic case of Hindes’ conjecture on dynamical non-isotriviality. Next, we give two applications of this result. On the one hand, we prove that quadratic polynomials over global fields with abelian dynamical Galois group are necessarily PCF, and we combine our results with local class field theory to classify quadratic pairs over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${ {\mathbb{Q}}}$</tex> with abelian dynamical Galois group, improving on recent results of Andrews and Petsche. On the other hand, we show that several infinite families of subgroups of the automorphism group of the infinite binary tree cannot appear as images of arboreal representations of quadratic polynomials over number fields, yielding unconditional evidence toward Jones’ finite index conjecture.

articleTitle: Quantitative Representation Stability Over Linear Groups
abstract: We introduce a technique for proving quantitative representation stability theorems for sequences of representations of certain finite linear groups over a field of characteristic zero. In particular, we prove a vanishing result for higher syzygies of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textsf{VIC}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textsf{SI}$</tex>-modules, which can be thought of as a weaker version of a regularity theorem of Church–Ellenberg [1, Theorem A] in the context of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textsf{FI}$</tex>-modules. We apply these techniques to the rational homology of congruence subgroups of mapping class groups and congruence subgroups of automorphism groups of free groups. This partially resolves a question raised by Church and Putman–Sam [11, Remark 1.8]. We also prove new homological stability results for mapping class groups and automorphism groups of free groups with twisted coefficients.

articleTitle: On the Sobolev–Poincaré Inequality of CR-manifolds
abstract: The purpose is to study the CR-manifold with a contact structure conformal to the Heisenberg group. In our previous work [22], we have proved that if the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q^{\prime }$</tex>-curvature is nonnegative and the integral of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q^{\prime }$</tex>-curvature is below the dimensional bound <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_1^{\prime }$</tex>, then we have the isoperimetric inequality. In this paper, we manage to deal with general contact structure conformal to the Heisenberg group, removing the condition that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q^{\prime }$</tex>-curvature is nonnegative. We prove that the volume form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e^{4u}$</tex> is a strong <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{\infty }$</tex> weight. As a corollary, we prove the Sobolev–Poincaré inequality on a class of CR-manifolds with integrable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q^{\prime }$</tex>-curvature.

articleTitle: On the Nonnegativity of Stringy Hodge Numbers
abstract: We study the nonnegativity of stringy Hodge numbers of a projective variety with Gorenstein canonical singularities, which was conjectured by Batyrev. We prove that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(p,1)$</tex>-stringy Hodge numbers are nonnegative, and for three-folds we obtain new results about the stringy Hodge diamond, which hold even when the stringy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>-function is not a polynomial. We also use the Decomposition Theorem and mixed Hodge theory to prove Batyrev's conjecture for a class of four-folds.

articleTitle: On the Minkowski Formula for Hypersurfaces in Complex Space Forms
abstract: In this paper, we discuss various Minkowski-type formulas for real hypersurfaces in complex space forms. In particular, we investigate the formulas suggested by the natural splitting of the tangent space. In this direction, our main result concerns a new kind of 2nd Minkowski formula.

articleTitle: The Chow Ring of a Cubic Hypersurface
abstract: We study the product structure on the Chow ring (with rational coefficients) of a cubic hypersurface in projective space and prove that the image of the product map is as small as possible.

articleTitle: Rigidity of Linearly Constrained Frameworks
abstract: We consider the problem of characterising the generic rigidity of bar-joint frameworks in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^d$</tex> in which each vertex is constrained to lie in a given affine subspace. The special case when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d=2$</tex> was previously solved by Streinu and Theran [14] in 2010. We will extend their characterisation to the case when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geq 3$</tex> and each vertex is constrained to lie in an affine subspace of dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t=1,2$</tex> and also when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t\geq 3$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geq t(t-1)$</tex>. We then point out that results on body–bar frameworks obtained by Katoh and Tanigawa [8] in 2013 can be used to characterise when a graph has a rigid realisation as a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-dimensional body–bar framework with a given set of linear constraints.

articleTitle: Lefschetz–Bott Fibrations on Line Bundles Over Symplectic Manifolds
abstract: We describe Lefschetz–Bott fibrations on complex line bundles over symplectic manifolds explicitly. As an application, we show that the link of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{k}$</tex>-type singularity has more than one strong symplectic filling up to homotopy and blow-up at points when the dimension of the link is greater than or equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5$</tex>. In the appendix, we show that the total space of a Lefschetz–Bott fibration over the unit disk serves as a strong symplectic filling of a contact manifold compatible with an open book induced by the fibration.

articleTitle: A Question of Norton–Sullivan in the Analytic Case
abstract: In 1996, A. Norton and D. Sullivan asked the following question: If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f:\mathbb{T}^2\rightarrow \mathbb{T}^2$</tex> is a diffeomorphism, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h:\mathbb{T}^2\rightarrow \mathbb{T}^2$</tex> is a continuous map homotopic to the identity, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h f=T_{\rho } h$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho \in \mathbb{R}^2$</tex> is a totally irrational vector and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rho }:\mathbb{T}^2\rightarrow \mathbb{T}^2,\, z\mapsto z+\rho $</tex> is a translation, are there natural geometric conditions (e.g., smoothness) on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> that force <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex> to be a homeomorphism? In [22], the 1st author and Z. Zhang gave a negative answer to the above question in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{\infty }$</tex> category: in general, not even the infinite smoothness condition can force <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex> to be a homeomorphism. In this article, we give a negative answer in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{\omega }$</tex> category (see also [22, Question 3]): we construct a real analytic conservative and minimal totally irrational pseudo-rotation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{T}^2$</tex> that is semi-conjugate to a translation but not conjugate to a translation.

articleTitle: Transcendental Liouville Inequalities on Projective Varieties
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> be an algebraic point of a projective variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> defined over a number field. Liouville inequality tells us that the norm at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> of a non-vanishing integral global section of a hermitian line bundle over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is zero or it cannot be too small with respect to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sup $</tex> norm of the section itself. We study inequalities similar to Liouville’s for subvarietes and for transcendental points of a projective variety defined over a number field. We prove that almost all transcendental points verify a good inequality of Liouville type. We also relate our methods to a (former) conjecture by Chudnovsky and give two applications to the growth of the number of rational points of bounded height on the image of an analytic map from a disk to a projective variety.

articleTitle: A Vanishing Associated With Irregular MSP Fields
abstract: In [7] and [8], the notion of Mixed-Spin-P (MSP) fields is introduced and their <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{C}}^\ast $</tex>-equivariant moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathcal{W}}}_{g,\gamma ,{\textbf d}}$</tex> is constructed. In this paper, we prove a vanishing of a class of localization terms in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[(\mathcal{W}_{g,\gamma ,\mathbf{d}})^{\mathbb{C}^*}]^{\textrm{vir}}$</tex>, which implies the only quintic FJRW invariants that contribute to the relations derived from the theory of MSP fields are those with pure insertions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2/5$</tex>. It is critical in a proof of BCOV Feynman sum formula for quintic Calabi–Yau three-folds.

articleTitle: Vertical Distribution Relations for Special Cycles on Unitary Shimura Varieties
abstract: We consider cycles on three-dimensional Shimura varieties attached to unitary groups, defined over extensions of a complex multiplication (CM) field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>, which appear in the context of the conjectures of Gan et al. [6]. We establish a vertical distribution relation for these cycles over an anticyclotomic extension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>, complementing the horizontal distribution relation of [8], and use this to define a family of norm-compatible cycles over these fields, thus obtaining a universal norm construction similar to the Heegner <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda $</tex>-module constructed from Heegner points.

articleTitle: Semiorthogonal Decompositions on Total Spaces of Tautological Bundles
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex> be the tautological subbundle on the Grassmannian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Gr}(k, n)$</tex>. There is a natural morphism <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{Tot}(U) \to{\mathbb{A}}^n$</tex>. Using it, we give a semiorthogonal decomposition for the bounded derived category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D^b_{\!\textrm{coh}}(\textrm{Tot}(U))$</tex> into several exceptional objects and several copies of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D^b_{\!\textrm{coh}}({\mathbb{A}}^n)$</tex>. We also prove a global version of this result: given a vector bundle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> with a regular section <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>, consider a subvariety of the relative Grassmannian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Gr}(k, E)$</tex> of those subspaces that contain the value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>. The derived category of this subvariety admits a similar decomposition into copies of the base and the zero locus of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>. This may be viewed as a generalization of the blow-up formula of Orlov, which is the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k = 1$</tex>.

articleTitle: Eigenfunctions with Infinitely Many Isolated Critical Points
abstract: We construct a Riemannian metric on the 2D torus, such that for infinitely many eigenvalues of the Laplace–Beltrami operator, a corresponding eigenfunction has infinitely many isolated critical points. A minor modification of our construction implies that each of these eigenfunctions has a level set with infinitely many connected components (i.e., a linear combination of two eigenfunctions may have infinitely many nodal domains).

articleTitle: Littlewood's Problem for Sets with Multidimensional Structure
abstract: We give <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^1$</tex>-norm estimates for exponential sums of a finite sets <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> consisting of integers or lattice points. Under the assumption that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> possesses sufficient multidimensional structure, our estimates are stronger than those of McGehee–Pigno–Smith and Konyagin. These theorems improve upon past work of Petridis.

articleTitle: Minimal Asymptotic Translation Lengths of Torelli Groups and Pure Braid Groups on the Curve Graph
abstract: In this paper, we show that the minimal asymptotic translation length of the Torelli group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{I}}_g$</tex> of the surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_g$</tex> of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> on the curve graph asymptotically behaves like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/g$</tex>, contrary to the mapping class group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{Mod}}(S_g)$</tex>, which behaves like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/g^2$</tex>. We also show that the minimal asymptotic translation length of the pure braid group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{PB}}_n$</tex> on the curve graph asymptotically behaves like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/n$</tex>, contrary to the braid group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textrm{B}}_n$</tex>, which behaves like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/n^2$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Continuity Method on Fano Fibrations
abstract: We study finite-time collapsing limits of the continuity method. When the continuity method starting from a rational initial Kähler metric on a projective manifold encounters a finite-time volume collapsing, this projective manifold admits a Fano fibration over a lower-dimensional base. In this case, we prove the continuity method converges to a singular Kähler metric on the base in the weak sense; moreover, if the base is smooth and the fibration has no singular fibers, then the convergence takes place in Gromov–Hausdorff topology.

articleTitle: A Trilinear Restriction Estimate for the Hyperbolic Paraboloid with Sharp Dependence on Transversality
abstract: The problem of restriction in harmonic analysis revolves around the operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{R}:f\mapsto \hat{f}|_{S}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> is a manifold in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^n$</tex>. A fundamental inequality of the multilinear theory of the restriction operator is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\big \lVert{\prod _{k=1}^{n}\mathcal{R}^{*} f_{k}}\big \rVert _{L^{2/(n-1)}(\mathbb{R}^{n})}\le C\prod _{k=1}^{n}\lVert{f_k}\rVert _{L^{2}(S_k)}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{R}^{*}$</tex> is the dual operator and the hypersurfaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_k$</tex> satisfy a condition of transversality. This estimate was proven by Bennett, Carbery, and Tao, up to logarithmic losses, but without optimal dependence on transversality in the constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>. For subsets of the paraboloid in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^{3}$</tex>, Ramos got the sharp dependence on transversality. In this paper we extend this result to subsets of the hyperbolic paraboloid.

articleTitle: Generalised BGP Reflection Functors via the Grothendieck Construction
abstract: Inspired by work of Ladkani and Groth–Šťovíček, we explain how to construct generalisations of the classical reflection functors of Bernšteĭn, Gel′fand, and Ponomarev by means of the Grothendieck construction.

articleTitle: On the Number of Products Which Form Perfect Powers and Discriminants of Multiquadratic Extensions
abstract: We study some counting questions concerning products of positive integers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_1, \ldots , u_n$</tex>, which form a nonzero perfect square, or more generally, a perfect <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-th power. We obtain an asymptotic formula for the number of such integers of bounded size and in particular improve and generalize a result of D. I. Tolev (2011). We also use similar ideas to count the discriminants of number fields that are multiquadratic extensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{Q}}$</tex> and improve and generalize a result of N. Rome (2017).

articleTitle: Two Moduli Spaces of Calabi–Yau type
abstract: We show <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{10, 10}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\mathcal{F}}_{11,9}$</tex> have Kodaira dimension zero. Our method relies on the construction of a number of curves via nodal Lefschetz pencils on blown-up <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K3$</tex> surfaces. The construction further yields that any effective divisor in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g}$</tex> with slope <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<6+(12-\delta )/(g+1)$</tex> must contain the locus of curves that are the normalization of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta $</tex>-nodal curve lying on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K3$</tex> surface of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g+\delta $</tex>.

articleTitle: On the Existence of Extremals for Moser-Type Inequalities in Gauss Space
abstract: The existence of an extremal in an exponential Sobolev-type inequality, with optimal constant, in Gauss space is established. A key step in the proof is an augmented version of the relevant inequality, which, by contrast, fails for a parallel classical inequality by Moser in the Euclidean space.

articleTitle: Stability of the Cohomology of the Space of Complex Irreducible Polynomials in Several Variables
abstract: We prove that the space of complex irreducible polynomials of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> variables satisfies two forms of homological stability: first, its cohomology stabilizes as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\to \infty $</tex>, and second, its compactly supported cohomology stabilizes as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\to \infty $</tex>. Our topological results are inspired by counting results over finite fields due to Carlitz and Hyde.

articleTitle: Random Eigenfunctions on Flat Tori: Universality for the Number of Intersections
abstract: We show that several statistics of the number of intersections between random eigenfunctions of general eigenvalues and a given smooth curve in flat tori are universal under various families of randomness.

articleTitle: The Dynamical Mordell–Lang Conjecture for Skew-Linear Self-Maps. Appendix by Michael Wibmer
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> be an algebraically closed field of characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex>, let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N\in{\mathbb{N}}$</tex>, let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g:{\mathbb{P}}^1{\longrightarrow } {\mathbb{P}}^1$</tex> be a nonconstant morphism, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A:{\mathbb{A}}^N{\longrightarrow } {\mathbb{A}}^N$</tex> be a linear transformation defined over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k({\mathbb{P}}^1)$</tex>, that is, for a Zariski-open dense subset <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U\subset{\mathbb{P}}^1$</tex>, we have that for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x\in U(k)$</tex>, the specialization <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A(x)$</tex> is an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-by-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> matrix with entries in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>.
