We let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f:{\mathbb{P}}^1\times{\mathbb{A}}^N{\dashrightarrow } {\mathbb{P}}^1\times{\mathbb{A}}^N$</tex> be the rational endomorphism given by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(x,y)\mapsto (\,g(x), A(x)y)$</tex>. We prove that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> induces an automorphism of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{A}}^1\subset{\mathbb{P}}^1$</tex>, then each irreducible curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C\subset{\mathbb{A}}^1\times{\mathbb{A}}^N$</tex> that intersects some orbit <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O}_f(z)$</tex> in infinitely many points must be periodic under the action of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>. Furthermore, in the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g:{\mathbb{P}}^1{\longrightarrow } {\mathbb{P}}^1$</tex> is an endomorphism of degree greater than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>, then we prove that each irreducible subvariety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y\subset{\mathbb{P}}^1\times{\mathbb{A}}^N$</tex> intersecting an orbit <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O}_f(z)$</tex> in a Zariski dense set of points must be periodic. Our results provide the desired conclusion in the Dynamical Mordell–Lang Conjecture in a couple new instances. Moreover, our results have interesting consequences toward a conjecture of Rubel and toward a generalized Skolem–Mahler–Lech problem proposed by Wibmer in the context of difference equations. In the appendix it is shown that the results can also be used to construct Picard–Vessiot extensions in the ring of sequences.

articleTitle: Linear Equations in Singular Moduli
abstract: We establish an effective version of the André–Oort conjecture for linear subspaces of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y(1)^n_{\mathbb{C}} \approx \mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{C}}^n$</tex>. This gives the first effective nontrivial results of André–Oort type for higher-dimensional varieties in products of modular curves.

articleTitle: An Extension of Polynomial Integrability to Dual Quermassintegrals
abstract: A bounded domain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> is called polynomially integrable if its parallel section function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{n-1}(K\cap \{\xi ^\perp +t\xi \})$</tex> is a polynomial of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> (on its support) for every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\xi $</tex>. A complete characterization of such domains was given recently. Here we obtain a generalization of these results in the setting of dual quermassintegrals. We also address the associated smoothness issues.

articleTitle: Polynomial Factorization Statistics and Point Configurations in ℝ3
abstract: We use combinatorial methods to relate the expected values of polynomial factorization statistics over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_q$</tex> to the cohomology of ordered configurations in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^3$</tex> as a representation of the symmetric group. Our method gives a new proof of the twisted Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula for squarefree polynomial factorization statistics of Church, Ellenberg, and Farb.

articleTitle: Regularity of the Dirichlet Problem for the Non-degenerate Complex Quotient Equations
abstract: We study the solvability for the Dirichlet problem of a class of fully nonlinear elliptic equations over complex domains in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{C}^n$</tex>. The equations are in the form of the linear combinations of the elementary symmetric functions of the Hessian matrix of the unknown functions, which include the complex Hessian equations and quotient equations as special cases.

articleTitle: On Representation Zeta Functions for Special Linear Groups
abstract: We prove that the numbers of irreducible n-dimensional complex continuous representations of the special linear groups over p-adic integers grow slower than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n^{2}$</tex>. We deduce that the abscissas of convergence of the representation zeta functions of the special linear groups over the ring of integers are bounded above by 2. In order to show these results we prove also that if G is a connected, simply connected, semi-simple algebraic group defined over the field of rational numbers, then the G-representation variety of the fundamental group of a compact Riemann surface of genus n has rational singularities if and only if the G-character variety has rational singularities.

articleTitle: Pointwise Asymptotics for Orthonormal Polynomials at the Endpoints of the Interval via Universality
abstract: We show that universality limits and other bounds imply pointwise asymptotics for orthonormal polynomials at the endpoints of the interval of orthonormality. As a consequence, we show that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex> is a regular measure supported on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left [ -1,1\right ] $</tex>, and in a neighborhood of 1, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \mu $</tex> is absolutely continuous, while for some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha>-1$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu ^{\prime }\left ( t\right ) =h\left ( t\right ) \left ( 1-t\right )^{\alpha }$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ h\left ( t\right ) \rightarrow 1$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t\rightarrow 1-$</tex>, then the corresponding orthonormal polynomials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left \{ p_{n}\right \} $</tex> satisfy the asymptotic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$ \lim_{n\rightarrow \infty }\frac{p_{n}\left( 1-\frac{z^{2}}{2n^{2}}\right) }{ p_{n}\left( 1\right) }=\frac{J_{\alpha }^{\ast }\left( z\right) }{J_{\alpha }^{\ast }\left( 0\right) } $$</tex>uniformly in compact subsets of the plane. Here <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J_{\alpha }^{\ast }\left ( z\right ) =J_{\alpha }\left ( z\right ) /z^{\alpha }$</tex> is the normalized Bessel function of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex>. These are by far the most general conditions for such endpoint asymptotics.

articleTitle: Consequences of Strong Stability of Minimal Submanifolds
abstract: In this note we show that the recent dynamical stability result for small <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^1$</tex>-perturbations of strongly stable minimal submanifolds of C.-J. Tsai and M.-T. Wang [12] directly extends to the enhanced Brakke flows of Ilmanen [5]. We illustrate applications of this result, including a local uniqueness statement for strongly stable minimal submanifolds amongst stationary varifolds, and a mechanism to flow through some singularities of Lagrangian mean curvature flow, which are proved to occur by Neves [7].

articleTitle: Factorization of Noncommutative Polynomials and Nullstellensätze for the Free Algebra
abstract: This article gives a class of Nullstellensätze for noncommutative polynomials. The singularity set of a noncommutative polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f=f(x_1,\dots ,x_g)$</tex> is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{Z}(\,f)=(\mathscr{Z}_n(\,f))_n$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{Z}_n(\,f)=\{X \in{\operatorname{M}}_{n}({\mathbb{C}})^g \colon \det f(X) = 0\}.$</tex> The 1st main theorem of this article shows that the irreducible factors of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> are in a natural bijective correspondence with irreducible components of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{Z}_n(\,f)$</tex> for every sufficiently large <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>. With each polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x^*$</tex> one also associates its real singularity set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{Z}^{{\operatorname{re}}}(h)=\{X\colon \det h(X,X^*)=0\}$</tex>. A polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> that depends on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> alone (no <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x^*$</tex> variables) will be called analytic. The main Nullstellensatz proved here is as follows: for analytic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> but for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex> dependent on possibly both <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x^*$</tex>, the containment <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{Z}(\,f) \subseteq \mathscr{Z}^{{\operatorname{re}}} (h)$</tex> is equivalent to each factor of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> being “stably associated” to a factor of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex> or of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^*$</tex>. For perspective, classical Hilbert-type Nullstellensätze typically apply only to analytic polynomials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f,h $</tex>, while real Nullstellensätze typically require adjusting the functions by sums of squares of polynomials (sos). Since the above “algebraic certificate” does not involve a sos, it seems justified to think of this as the natural determinantal Hilbert Nullstellensatz. An earlier paper of the authors (Adv. Math. 331 (2018): 589–626) obtained such a theorem for special classes of analytic polynomials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex>. This paper requires few hypotheses and hopefully brings this type of Nullstellensatz to near final form. Finally, the paper gives a Nullstellensatz for zeros <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{V}}(\,f)=\{X\colon f(X,X^*)=0\}$</tex> of a hermitian polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>, leading to a strong Positivstellensatz for quadratic free semialgebraic sets by the use of a slack variable.

articleTitle: Real Representations of Finite Symplectic Groups over Fields of Characteristic Two
abstract: We prove that when q is a power of 2 every complex irreducible representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{Sp}\big (2n, \mathbb{F}_{q}\big )$</tex> may be defined over the real numbers, that is, all Frobenius–Schur indicators are 1. We also obtain a generating function for the sum of the degrees of the unipotent characters of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{Sp}\big(2n, \mathbb{F}_{q}\big )$</tex>, or of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{SO}\big(2n+1,\mathbb{F}_{q}\big )$</tex>, for any prime power q.

articleTitle: Hyperbolicity of Varieties Supporting a Variation of Hodge Structure
abstract: We generalize former results of Zuo and the 1st author showing some hyperbolicity properties of varieties supporting a variation of Hodge structure. Our proof only uses the special curvature properties of period domains. In particular, in contrast to the former approaches, it does not use any result on the asymptotic behavior of the Hodge metric.

articleTitle: On the Topological Rigidity of Compact Self-shrinkers in ℝ3
abstract: In this note we show that self-shrinkers in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^{3}$</tex> are “topologically standard” in that any genus g compact self-shrinker is ambiently isotopic to the standard genus g embedded surface in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb R^{3}$</tex>. As a consequence self-shrinking tori are unknotted.

articleTitle: Shadows of a Closed Curve
abstract: A shadow of a geometric object A in a given direction v is the orthogonal projection of A on the hyperplane orthogonal to v. We show that any topological embedding of a circle into Euclidean d-space can have at most two shadows that are simple paths in linearly independent directions. The proof is topological and uses an analog of basic properties of degree of maps on a circle to relations on a circle. This extends a previous result that dealt with the case d = 3.

articleTitle: Weak Containment by Restrictions of Induced Representations
abstract: A QSIN group is a locally compact group G whose group algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm L^{1}(G)$</tex> admits a quasi-central bounded approximate identity. Examples of QSIN groups include every amenable group and every discrete group. It is shown that if G is a QSIN group, H is a closed subgroup of G, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi \!: H\to \mathcal B(\mathcal{H})$</tex> is a unitary representation of H, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex> is weakly contained in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Big (\mathrm{Ind}_{H}^{G}\pi \Big )|_{H}$</tex>. This provides a powerful tool in studying the C∗-algebras of QSIN groups. In particular, it is shown that if G is a QSIN group which contains a copy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_{2}$</tex> as a closed subgroup, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm C^{\ast }(G)$</tex> is not locally reflexive and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm C^{\ast }_{r}(G)$</tex> does not admit the local lifting property. Further applications are drawn to the “(weak) extendability” of Fourier spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm A_{\pi }$</tex> and Fourier–Stieltjes spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm B_{\pi }$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Mean Value Formula and a Liouville Theorem for the Complex Monge–Ampère Equation
abstract: In this paper, we prove a mean value formula for bounded subharmonic Hermitian matrix valued function on a complete Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature. As its application, we obtain a Liouville type theorem for the complex Monge–Ampère equation on product manifolds.

articleTitle: Beilinson–Bernstein Localization Over ℚ and Periods of Automorphic Forms: Erratum
On the Cohomology of Calogero–Moser Spaces
abstract: We compute the equivariant cohomology of smooth Calogero–Moser spaces and some associated symplectic resolutions of symplectic quotient singularities.

articleTitle: Rigidity Results for Elliptic Boundary Value Problems: Stable Solutions for Quasilinear Equations with Neumann or Robin Boundary Conditions
abstract: We provide a general approach to the classification results of stable solutions of (possibly nonlinear) elliptic problems with Robin conditions. The method is based on a geometric formula of Poincaré type, which is inspired by a classical work of Sternberg and Zumbrun and which gives an accurate description of the curvatures of the level sets of the stable solutions. From this, we show that the stable solutions of a quasilinear problem with Neumann data are necessarily constant. As a byproduct of this, we obtain an alternative proof of a celebrated result of Casten and Holland, and Matano. In addition, we will obtain as a consequence a new proof of a result recently established by Bandle, Mastrolia, Monticelli, and Punzo.

articleTitle: Deforming a Canonical Curve Inside a Quadric
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C\subset{\mathbb{P}}^{g-1}$</tex> be a canonically embedded nonsingular nonhyperelliptic curve of genus g and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X\subset{\mathbb{P}}^{g-1}$</tex> be a quadric containing C. Our main result states among other things that the Hilbert scheme of X is at [C ⊂ X] a local complete intersection of dimension g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> − 1 and is smooth when X is. It also includes the assertion that the minimal obstruction space for this deformation problem is in fact the full associated Ext<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>-group and that in particular the deformations of C in X are obstructed in case C meets the singular locus of X. Applications will be given in a forthcoming paper.

articleTitle: Isomorphisms Between Big Mapping Class Groups
abstract: We show that any isomorphism between mapping class groups of orientable infinite-type surfaces is induced by a homeomorphism between the surfaces. Our argument additionally applies to automorphisms between finite-index subgroups of these “big” mapping class groups and shows that each finite-index subgroup has finite outer automorphism group. As a key ingredient, we prove that all simplicial automorphisms between curve complexes of infinite-type orientable surfaces are induced by homeomorphisms.

articleTitle: Continuous Cocycle Superrigidity for the Full Shift Over a Finitely Generated Torsion Group
abstract: Chung and Jiang showed that if a one-ended group contains an infinite order element, then every continuous cocycle over the full shift, taking values in a discrete group, must be cohomologous to a homomorphism. We show that their conclusion holds for all one-ended groups, so that the hypothesis of admitting an infinite order element may be omitted.

articleTitle: Length of Local Cohomology in Positive Characteristic and Ordinarity
abstract: Let D be the ring of Grothendieck differential operators of the ring R of polynomials in d ≥ 3 variables with coefficients in a perfect field of characteristic p. We compute the D-module length of the 1st local cohomology module <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${H^{1}_{f}}(R)$</tex> with respect to a polynomial f with an isolated singularity, for p large enough. The expression we give is in terms of the Frobenius action on the top coherent cohomology of the exceptional fibre of a resolution of the singularity. Our proof rests on a tight closure computation of Hara. Since the above length is quite different from that of the corresponding local cohomology module in characteristic zero, we also consider a characteristic zero D-module whose length is expected to equal that above, for ordinary primes.

articleTitle: Universal Gröbner Bases and Cartwright–Sturmfels Ideals
abstract: The main theoretical contribution of the paper is the description of two classes of multigraded ideals named after Cartwright and Sturmfels and the study of their surprising properties. Among other things we prove that these classes of ideals have very special multigraded generic initial ideals and are closed under several operations including arbitrary multigraded hyperplane sections. As a main application we describe the universal Gröbner basis of the ideal of maximal minors and the ideal of 2-minors of a multigraded matrix of linear forms generalizing earlier results of various authors including Bernstein, Sturmfels, Zelevinsky, and Boocher.

articleTitle: Abelian Varieties as Automorphism Groups of Smooth Projective Varieties
abstract: We determine which complex abelian varieties can be realized as the automorphism group of a smooth projective variety.

articleTitle: Random Lattice Vectors in a Set of Size O(n)
abstract: We adopt the sieve ideas of Schmidt [10, 11] and Södergren [14] in order to study the statistics of vectors of a random lattice of dimension n contained in a set of volume O(n). We also give some sporadic applications of our results to number theory.

articleTitle: Supersaturated Sparse Graphs and Hypergraphs
abstract: A central problem in extremal graph theory is to estimate, for a given graph H, the number of H-free graphs on a given set of n vertices. In the case when H is not bipartite, Erd̋s, Frankl, and Rödl proved that there are 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1+o(1))ex(n, H)</sup> such graphs. In the bipartite case, however, bounds of the form 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O(ex(n, H))</sup> have been proven only for relatively few special graphs H. As a 1st attempt at addressing this problem in full generality, we show that such a bound follows merely from a rather natural assumption on the growth rate of n ↦ ex(n, H); an analogous statement remains true when H is a uniform hypergraph. Subsequently, we derive several new results, along with most previously known estimates, as simple corollaries of our theorem. At the heart of our proof lies a general supersaturation statement that extends the seminal work of Erd̋s and Simonovits. The bounds on the number of H-free hypergraphs are derived from it using the method of hypergraph containers.

articleTitle: Factorization Norms and Hereditary Discrepancy
abstract: The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma _{2}$</tex> norm of a real m × n matrix A is the minimumnumber t such that the column vectors of A are contained in a 0-centered ellipsoid <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E\subseteq{\mathbb{R}}^{m}$</tex> which in turn is contained in the hypercube <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[-t, t]^{m}$</tex>. We prove that this classical quantity approximates the hereditary discrepancy herdisc A as follows: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma _{2}(A) ={O(\log m)}\cdot \operatorname{herdisc} A$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{herdisc}\, A = O\big (\sqrt{\log m}\,\big )\cdot \gamma _{2}(A) $</tex>. Since <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma _{2}$</tex> is polynomial-time computable, this gives a polynomial-time approximation algorithm for hereditary discrepancy. Both inequalities are shown to be asymptotically tight. We then demonstrate on several examples the power of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma _{2}$</tex> norm as a tool for proving lower and upper bounds in discrepancy theory. Most notably, we prove a new lower bound of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varOmega\!\! \left (\log ^{d-1} n \right )$</tex> for the d-dimensional Tusnády problem, asking for the combinatorial discrepancy of an n-point set in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{R}}^{d}$</tex> with respect to axis-parallel boxes. For d > 2, this improves the previous best lower bound, which was of order approximately <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log ^{(d-1)/2}n$</tex>.

articleTitle: On the Isotypic Decomposition of Cohomology Modules of Symmetric Semi-algebraic Sets: Polynomial Bounds on Multiplicities
abstract: We consider symmetric (under the action of products of finite symmetric groups) real algebraic varieties and semi-algebraic sets, as well as symmetric complex varieties in affine and projective spaces, defined by polynomials of degrees bounded by a fixed constant d. We prove that if a Specht module, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{\lambda }$</tex>, appears with positive multiplicity in the isotypic decomposition of the cohomology modules of such sets, then the rank of the partition <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> is bounded by O(d). This implies a polynomial (in the dimension of the ambient space) bound on the number of such modules. Furthermore, we prove a polynomial bound on the multiplicities of those that do appear with positive multiplicity in the isotypic decomposition of the abovementioned cohomology modules. We give some applications of our methods in proving lower bounds on the degrees of defining polynomials of certain symmetric semi-algebraic sets, as well as improved bounds on the Betti numbers of the images under projections of (not necessarily symmetric) bounded real algebraic sets, improving in certain situations prior results of Gabrielov, Vorobjov, and Zell.

articleTitle: Dimension Formulae in Genus Zero and Uniqueness of Vertex Operator Algebras
abstract: We prove a dimension formula for orbifold vertex operator algebras of central charge 24 by automorphisms of order n such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma _{0}(n)$</tex> is a genus zero group. We then use this formula together with the inverse orbifold construction for automorphisms of orders 2, 4, 5, 6, and 8 to establish that each of the following fifteen Lie algebras is the weight-one space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{1}$</tex> of exactly one holomorphic, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{2}$</tex>-cofinite vertex operator algebra V of CFT type and central charge 24: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{5}C_{5}E_{6,2}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{3}A_{7,2}{C_{3}^{2}}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{8,2}F_{4,2}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{8}E_{8,2}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${A_{2}^{2}}A_{5,2}^{2}B_{2}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{8}{F_{4}^{2}}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{4,2}^{2}C_{4,2}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{2,2}^{4}D_{4,4}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{5}E_{7,2}F_{4}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{4}{C_{6}^{2}}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{4,5}^{2}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{4}A_{9,2}B_{3}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{6}C_{10}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{1}C_{5,3}G_{2,2}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{1,2}A_{3,4}^{3}$</tex>.

articleTitle: On Generalized Minors and Quiver Representations
abstract: The cluster algebra of any acyclic quiver can be realized as the coordinate ring of a subvariety of a Kac–Moody group—the quiver is an orientation of its Dynkin diagram, defining a Coxeter element and thereby a double Bruhat cell. We use this realization to connect representations of the quiver with those of the group. We show that cluster variables of preprojective (resp. postinjective) quiver representations are realized by generalized minors of highest-weight (resp. lowest-weight) group representations, generalizing results of Yang–Zelevinsky in finite type. In type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{n}^{\!(1)}$</tex> and finitely many other affine types, we show that cluster variables of regular quiver representations are realized by generalized minors of group representations that are neither highest- nor lowest-weight; we conjecture this holds more generally.

articleTitle: Formal Abel–Jacobi Maps
abstract: We realize the infinitesimal Abel–Jacobi map as a morphism of formal deformation theories, realized as a morphism in the homotopy category of differential graded Lie algebras. The whole construction is carried out in a general setting, of which the classical Abel–Jacobi map is a special example.

articleTitle: Off-diagonal Asymptotic Properties of Bergman Kernels Associated to Analytic Kähler Potentials
abstract: We prove a new off-diagonal asymptotic of the Bergman kernels associated to tensor powers of a positive line bundle on a compact Kähler manifold. We show that if the Kähler potential is real analytic, then the Bergman kernel accepts a complete asymptotic expansion in a neighborhood of the diagonal of shrinking size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k^{-\frac 14}$</tex>. These improve the earlier results in the subject for smooth potentials, where an expansion exists in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k^{-\frac 12}$</tex> neighborhood of the diagonal. We obtain our results by finding upper bounds of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^m m!^{2}$</tex> for the Bergman coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b_m(x, \bar y)$</tex>, which is an interesting problem on its own. We find such upper bounds using the method of [3]. We also show that sharpening these upper bounds would improve the rate of shrinking neighborhoods of the diagonal x = y in our results. In the special case of metrics with local constant holomorphic sectional curvatures, we obtain off-diagonal asymptotic in a fixed (as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k \to \infty$</tex>) neighborhood of the diagonal, which recovers a result of Berman [2] (see Remark 3.5 of [2] for higher dimensions). In this case, we also find an explicit formula for the Bergman kernel mod <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(e^{-k \delta } )$</tex>.

articleTitle: Flexible Lagrangians
abstract: We introduce and discuss notions of regularity and flexibility for Lagrangian manifolds with Legendrian boundary in Weinstein domains. There is a surprising abundance of flexible Lagrangians. In turn, this leads to new constructions of Legendrians submanifolds and Weinstein manifolds. For instance, many closed n-manifolds of dimension n > 2 can be realized as exact Lagrangian submanifolds of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T^{\ast }S^n$</tex> with possibly exotic Weinstein symplectic structures. These Weinstein structures on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T^{\ast } S^n$</tex>, infinitely many of which are distinct, are formed by a single handle attachment to the standard 2n-ball along the Legendrian boundaries of flexible Lagrangians. We also formulate a number of open problems.

articleTitle: Model Transition for Representations of Unitary Type
abstract: We study an explicit relationship between different models of the same irreducible representation of p-adic reductive groups. For example, we study a relationship of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\textrm{GL}_{2n}(F), 1)$</tex>-model and Whittaker model for irreducible tempered representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{GL}_{2n}(E)$</tex> where E is a quadratic extension of a non-archimedean local field F of characteristic zero. Further, we inflate this relation to certain Langlands quotients of the quasi-split unitary group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{U}_{4n}(F)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Valuations on Banach Lattices
abstract: We provide a general framework for the study of valuations on Banach lattices. This complements and expands several recent works about valuations on function spaces, including <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p(\mu )$</tex>, Orlicz spaces, and spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C(K)$</tex> of continuous functions on a compact Hausdorff space. In particular, we study decomposition properties, boundedness, and integral representation of continuous valuations.

articleTitle: On Domains Biholomorphic to Teichmüller Spaces
abstract: We prove that the Teichmüller space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{T}$</tex> of a closed surface of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g \ge 2$</tex> cannot be biholomorphic to any domain which is locally strictly convex at some boundary point.

articleTitle: Almost Positive Curvature on an Irreducible Compact Rank 2 Symmetric Space
abstract: A Riemannian manifold is said to be almost positively curved if the set of points for which all two-planes have positive sectional curvature is open and dense. We show that the Grassmannian of oriented two-planes in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^{7}$</tex> admits a metric of almost positive curvature, giving the first example of an almost positively curved metric on an irreducible compact symmetric space of rank greater than 1. The construction and verification rely on the Lie group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{G}_{2}$</tex> and the octonions, so do not obviously generalize to any other Grassmannians.

articleTitle: Ruelle and Quantum Resonances for Open Hyperbolic Manifolds
abstract: We establish a direct classical-quantum correspondence on convex cocompact hyperbolic manifolds between the spectra of the geodesic flow and the Laplacian acting on natural tensor bundles. This extends previous work detailing the correspondence for cocompact quotients.

articleTitle: Stretching Convex Domains to Capture Many Lattice Points
abstract: We consider an optimal stretching problem for strictly convex domains in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^d$</tex> that are symmetric with respect to each coordinate hyperplane, where stretching refers to transformation by a diagonal matrix of determinant 1. Specifically, we prove that the stretched convex domain which captures the most positive lattice points in the large volume limit is balanced: the (d − 1)-dimensional measures of the intersections of the domain with each coordinate hyperplane are equal. Our results extend those of Antunes and Freitas, van den Berg, Bucur and Gittins, Ariturk and Laugesen, van den Berg and Gittins, and Gittins and Larson. The approach is motivated by the Fourier analysis techniques used to prove the classical <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\#\{(i,j) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 : i^2 +j^2 \le r^2 \} =\pi r^2 + \mathcal{O}(r^{2/3})$</tex> result for the Gauss circle problem.

articleTitle: Invariant Hopf 2-Cocycles for Affine Algebraic Groups
abstract: We generalize the theory of the second invariant cohomology group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^{2}_{\textrm{inv}}(G)$</tex> for finite groups G, developed in [3, 4, 14], to the case of affine algebraic groups G, using the methods of [9, 10, 12]. In particular, we show that for connected affine algebraic groups G over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, the map Θ from [14] is bijective (unlike for some finite groups, as shown in [14]). This allows us to compute <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^{2}_{\textrm{inv}}(G)$</tex> in this case, and in particular show that this group is commutative (while for finite groups it can be noncommutative, as shown in [14]).

articleTitle: New Sharp Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev Inequalities and an Improved Borell–Brascamp–Lieb Inequality
abstract: We propose a new Borell–Brascamp–Lieb inequality that leads to novel sharp Euclidean inequalities such as Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev inequalities in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ {\mathbb{R}}^n$</tex> and in the half-space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ {\mathbb{R}}^n_+$</tex>. This gives a new bridge between the geometric point of view of the Brunn–Minkowski inequality and the functional point of view of the Sobolev-type inequalities. In this way we unify, simplify, and generalize results by S. Bobkov–M. Ledoux, M. del Pino–J. Dolbeault, and B. Nazaret.

articleTitle: ε-Regularity and Structure of Four-dimensional Shrinking Ricci Solitons
abstract: A closed four-dimensional manifold cannot possess a non-flat Ricci soliton metric with arbitrarily small <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{2}$</tex>-norm of the curvature. In this paper, we localize this fact in the case of gradient shrinking Ricci solitons by proving an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon $</tex>-regularity theorem, thus confirming a conjecture of Cheeger–Tian [20]. As applications, we will also derive structural results concerning the degeneration of the metrics on a family of complete non-compact four-dimensional gradient shrinking Ricci solitons without a uniform entropy lower bound. In the appendix, we provide a detailed account of the equivariant good chopping theorem when collapsing with locally bounded curvature happens.

articleTitle: Non-Formality of Planar Configuration Spaces in Characteristic 2
abstract: We prove that the ordered configuration space of four points or more in the plane has a nonformal singular cochain algebra in characteristic 2. This is proved by constructing an explicit nontrivial obstruction class in the Hochschild cohomology of the cohomology ring of the configuration space, by means of the Barratt–Eccles–Smith simplicial model. We also show that if the number of points does not exceed its dimension then a Euclidean configuration space is intrinsically formal over any ring.

articleTitle: Hölder Regularity for Singular Parabolic Obstacle Problems of Porous Medium Type
abstract: We study the regularity of weak solutions to parabolic obstacle problems related to equations of singular porous medium type that are modeled after the nonlinear equation<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\partial_{t} u - \Delta u^{m} = 0.$$</tex>For the range of exponents 0 < m < 1, we prove that locally bounded weak solutions are locally Hölder continuous, provided the obstacle function is. Moreover, in the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{(n-2)_{+}}{n+2} < m < 1$</tex> we show that every weak solution is locally bounded and therefore Hölder continuous.

articleTitle: Normal Scalar Curvature Inequality on the Focal Submanifolds of Isoparametric Hypersurfaces
abstract: An isoparametric hypersurface in unit spheres has two focal submanifolds. Condition A plays a crucial role in the classification theory of isoparametric hypersurfaces in [1], [7], and [25]. This paper determines <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{A}$</tex>, the set of points with Condition A in focal submanifolds. It turns out that the points in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{A}$</tex> reach an upper bound of the normal scalar curvature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho ^{\bot }$</tex> (sharper than that in DDVV inequality [16], [23]). We also determine the sets <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{P}$</tex> (points with parallel second fundamental form) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{E}$</tex> (points with Einstein condition), which achieve two lower bounds of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho ^{\bot }$</tex>.

articleTitle: Strange Duality on Rational Surfaces II: Higher-Rank Cases
abstract: We study Le Potier’s strange duality conjecture on a rational surface. We focus on the strange duality map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SD_{c_n^r,L}$</tex> that involves the moduli space of rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex> sheaves with trivial 1st Chern class and 2nd Chern class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>, and the moduli space of one-dimensional sheaves with determinant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> and Euler characteristic 0. We show there is an exact sequence relating the map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SD_{c_r^r,L}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SD_{c^{r-1}_{r},L}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SD_{c_r^r,L\otimes K_X}$</tex> for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r\geq 1$</tex> under some conditions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> that applies to a large number of cases on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{P}^2$</tex> or Hirzebruch surfaces. Also on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{P}^2$</tex> we show that for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r>0$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SD_{c^r_r,dH}$</tex> is an isomorphism for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d=1,2$</tex>, injective for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d=3,$</tex> and moreover <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SD_{c_3^3,rH}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SD_{c_3^2,rH}$</tex> are injective. At the end we prove that the map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SD_{c_n^2,L}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 2$</tex>) is an isomorphism for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X=\mathbb{P}^2$</tex> or Fano rational-ruled surfaces and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g_L=3$</tex>, and hence so is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SD_{c_3^3,L}$</tex> as a corollary of our main result.

articleTitle: Ramsey Graphs Induce Subgraphs of Quadratically Many Sizes
abstract: An n-vertex graph is called C-Ramsey if it has no clique or independent set of size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C\log n$</tex>. All known constructions of Ramsey graphs involve randomness in an essential way, and there is an ongoing line of research towards showing that in fact all Ramsey graphs must obey certain “richness” properties characteristic of random graphs. Motivated by an old problem of Erd̋s and McKay, recently Narayanan, Sahasrabudhe, and Tomon conjectured that for any fixed C, every n-vertex C-Ramsey graph induces subgraphs of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varTheta (n^{2} )$</tex> different sizes. In this paper we prove this conjecture.

articleTitle: K-Theory of Locally Compact Modules over Rings of Integers
abstract: We generalize a recent result of Clausen; for a number field with integers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O}$</tex>, we compute the K-theory of locally compact <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O}$</tex>-modules. For the rational integers this recovers Clausen’s result as a special case. Our method of proof is quite different; instead of a homotopy coherent cone construction in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\infty$</tex>-categories, we rely on calculus of fraction type results in the style of Schlichting. This produces concrete exact category models for certain quotients, a fact that might be of independent interest. As in Clausen’s work, our computation works for all localizing invariants, not just K-theory.

articleTitle: Doppelgängers: Bijections of Plane Partitions
abstract: We say two posets are doppelgängers if they have the same number of P-partitions of each height k. We give a uniform framework for bijective proofs that posets are doppelgängers by synthesizing K-theoretic Schubert calculus techniques of H. Thomas and A. Yong with M. Haiman’s rectification bijection and an observation of R. Proctor. Geometrically, these bijections reflect the rational equivalence of certain subvarieties of minuscule flag manifolds. As a special case, we provide the 1st bijective proof of a 1983 theorem of R. Proctor—that plane partitions of height k in a rectangle are equinumerous with plane partitions of height k in a shifted trapezoid.

articleTitle: Waist of Balls in Hyperbolic and Spherical Spaces
abstract: In this paper we find a tight estimate for Gromov’s waist of the balls in spaces of constant curvature, deduce the estimates for the balls in Riemannian manifolds with upper bounds on the curvature (CAT(ϰ)-spaces), and establish similar result for normed spaces.

articleTitle: Components of Affine Springer Fibers
abstract: Let G be a connected split reductive group over a field of characteristic zero or sufficiently large characteristic, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma _0\in (\operatorname{Lie}\mathbf{G})((t))$</tex> be any topologically nilpotent regular semisimple element, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma =t\gamma _0$</tex>. Using methods from p-adic orbital integrals, we show that the number of components of the Iwahori affine Springer fiber over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> modulo <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z_{\mathbf{G}((t))}(\gamma )$</tex> is equal to the order of the Weyl group.

articleTitle: Galois Conjugates of Entropies of Real Unimodal Maps
abstract: Around 2011, Thurston considered the set of Galois conjugates of all entropies of superattracting real quadratic polynomials and produced pictures showing that its closure has a rich fractal structure. In this paper, we investigate the geometry of this set, which we call the entropy spectrum, relate it to the set of zeros of polynomials with restricted coefficients, and prove that it is path-connected and locally connected.

articleTitle: On Groups, Slow Heat Kernel Decay Yields Liouville Property and Sharp Entropy Bounds
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex> be a symmetric probability measure of finite entropy on a group G. We show that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\log \mu ^{(2n)}(\textrm{id})=o\left(n^{1/2}\right)$</tex>, then the pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(G,\mu )$</tex> has the Liouville property (all bounded <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>-harmonic functions on G are constant). Furthermore, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\log \mu ^{(2n)}(\textrm{id})=O\left(n^{\beta }\right)$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta \in (0,1/2)$</tex>, then the entropy of the n-fold convolution power <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu ^{(n)}$</tex> satisfies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H\left(\mu ^{(n)}\right)=O\Big (n^{\frac{\beta }{1-\beta }}\Big )$</tex>. These results improve earlier work of Gournay [16] and Saloff-Coste and Zheng [27]. We illustrate the sharpness of the bounds on a family of groups.

articleTitle: Fractal Uncertainty for Transfer Operators
abstract: We show directly that the fractal uncertainty principle of Bourgain–Dyatlov [3] implies that there exists σ > 0 for which the Selberg zeta function (1.2) for a convex co-compact hyperbolic surface has only finitely many zeros with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \textrm{Re}\, s \geq \frac 12 - \sigma $</tex>. That eliminates advanced microlocal techniques of Dyatlov–Zahl [6], though we stress that these techniques are still needed for resolvent bounds and for possible generalizations to the case of nonconstant curvature.

articleTitle: Equality Cases in Viterbo’s Conjecture and Isoperimetric Billiard Inequalities
abstract: We apply the billiard technique to deduce some results on Viterbo’s conjectured inequality between the volume of a convex body and its symplectic capacity. We show that the product of a permutohedron and a simplex (properly related to each other) delivers equality in Viterbo’s conjecture. Using this result as well as previously known equality cases, we prove some special cases of Viterbo’s conjecture and interpret them as isoperimetric-like inequalities for billiard trajectories.

articleTitle: Higher-Order Parabolic Equations with VMO Assumptions and General Boundary Conditions with Variable Leading Coefficients
abstract: We prove weighted mixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{p}(L_{q})$</tex>-estimates, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p,q\in (1,\infty )$</tex>, and the corresponding solvability results for higher-order elliptic and parabolic equations on the half space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{R}}^{d+1}_{+}$</tex> and on general <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{2m-1,1}$</tex> domains with general boundary conditions, which satisfy the Lopatinskii–Shapiro condition. We assume that the elliptic operators A have leading coefficients that are in the class of vanishing mean oscillations both in the time and the space variables and that the boundary operators have variable leading coefficients. The proofs are based on and generalize the estimates recently obtained by the authors in [6].

articleTitle: Crystallization of Random Matrix Orbits
abstract: Three operations on eigenvalues of real/complex/quaternion (corresponding to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta =1,2,4$</tex>) matrices, obtained from cutting out principal corners, adding, and multiplying matrices, can be extrapolated to general values of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta>0$</tex> through associated special functions. We show that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta \to \infty $</tex> limit for these operations leads to the finite free projection, additive convolution, and multiplicative convolution, respectively. The limit is the most transparent for cutting out the corners, where the joint distribution of the eigenvalues of principal corners of a uniformly-random general <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta $</tex> self-adjoint matrix with fixed eigenvalues is known as the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta $</tex>-corners process. We show that as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta \to \infty $</tex> these eigenvalues crystallize on an irregular lattice consisting of the roots of derivatives of a single polynomial. In the second order, we observe a version of the discrete Gaussian Free Field put on top of this lattice, which provides a new explanation as to why the (continuous) Gaussian Free Field governs the global asymptotics of random matrix ensembles.

articleTitle: Asymptotics for a Class of Meandric Systems, via the Hasse Diagram of NC(n)
abstract: We consider the framework of closed meandric systems and its equivalent description in terms of the Hasse diagrams of the lattices of non-crossing partitions NC(n). In this equivalent description, considerations on the number of components of a random meandric system of order n translate into considerations about the distance between two random partitions in NC(n). We put into evidence a class of couples <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\pi ,\rho )\in \textrm{NC}(n)^{2}$</tex>—namely the ones where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi $</tex> is conditioned to be an interval partition—for which it turns out to be tractable to study distances in the Hasse diagram. As a consequence, we observe a nontrivial class of meanders (i.e., connected meandric systems), which we call “meanders with shallow top” and which can be explicitly enumerated. Moreover, denoting by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_{n}$</tex> the expected number of components for the corresponding notion of “meandric system with shallow top” of order n, we find the precise asymptotic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_{n}\approx \frac{n}{3}+\frac{28}{27}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\to \infty $</tex>. Our calculations concerning expected number of components are related to the idea of taking the derivative at t = 1 in a semigroup for the operation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boxplus $</tex> of free probability (but the underlying considerations are presented in a self-contained way and can be followed without assuming a free probability background). Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_{n}^{\prime }$</tex> denote the expected number of components of a general, unconditioned, meandric system of order n. A variation of the methods used in the shallow-top case allows us to prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{lim\ inf}_{n\to \infty }c_{n}^{\prime }/n\geq 0.17$</tex>. We also note that, by a direct elementary argument, one has <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{lim\ sup}_{n\to \infty }c_{n}^{\prime }/n\leq 0.5$</tex>. These bounds support the conjecture that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_{n}^{\prime }$</tex> follows a regime of “constant times n” (where numerical experiments suggest that the constant should be ≈ 0.23).

articleTitle: Symmetries of Projective Spaces and Spheres
abstract: Let H be either a complex inner product space of dimension at least two or a real inner product space of dimension at least three, and let us fix an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \in (0,\tfrac{\pi }{2} )$</tex>. The purpose of this paper is to characterise all bijective transformations on the projective space P(H) which preserve the quantum angle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> (or Fubini–Study distance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>) between lines in both directions. (Let us emphasise that we do not assume anything about the preservation of other quantum angles). For real inner product spaces and when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H=\mathbb{C}^2$</tex> we do this for every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>, and when H is a complex inner product space of dimension at least three we describe the structure of such transformations for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \leq \tfrac{\pi }{4}$</tex>. Our result immediately gives an Uhlhorn-type generalisation of Wigner’s theorem on quantum mechanical symmetry transformations, that is considered to be a cornerstone of the mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics. Namely, under the above assumptions, every bijective map on the set of pure states of a quantum mechanical system that preserves the transition probability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cos ^2\alpha$</tex> in both directions is a Wigner symmetry (thus automatically preserves all transition probabilities), except for the case when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H=\mathbb{C}^2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha = \tfrac{\pi }{4}$</tex> where an additional possibility occurs. (Note that the classical theorem of Uhlhorn is the solution for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha = \tfrac{\pi }{2}$</tex> case). Usually in the literature, results which are connected to Wigner’s theorem are discussed under the assumption of completeness of H; however, here we shall remove this unnecessary hypothesis in our investigation. Our main tool is a characterisation of bijective maps on unit spheres of real inner product spaces which preserve one spherical angle in both directions.

articleTitle: On Irreducible Components of Rapoport–Zink Spaces
abstract: Under a mild condition, we prove that the action of the group of self-quasi-isogenies on the set of irreducible components of a Rapoport–Zink space has finite orbits. Our method allows both ramified and nonbasic cases. As a consequence, we obtain some finiteness results on the representation obtained from the ℓ-adic cohomology of a Rapoport–Zink tower.

articleTitle: Conformally Covariant Bi-differential Operators on a Simple Real Jordan Algebra
abstract: For a simple real Jordan algebra V, a family of bi-differential operators from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{C}^\infty (V\times V)$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{C}^\infty (V)$</tex> is constructed. These operators are covariant under the rational action of the conformal group of V. They generalize the classical Rankin–Cohen brackets (case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V=\mathbb{R}$</tex>).

articleTitle: Toric Contact Geometry in Arbitrary Codimension
abstract: We define toric contact manifolds in arbitrary codimension and give a description of such manifolds in terms of a kind of labelled polytope embedded into a grassmannian, analogous to the Delzant polytope of a toric symplectic manifold.

articleTitle: Homology Class of a Deligne–Lusztig Variety and Its Analogs
abstract: We consider Deligne–Lusztig varieties and their analogs when the Frobenius endomorphism is replaced with conjugation by an element in a reductive group, especially a regular semisimple or regular unipotent one. We calculate their homology classes in the Chow group of the flag variety in terms of Schubert classes.

articleTitle: On Jensen-type Inequalities for Nonsmooth Radial Scattering Solutions of a Loglog Energy-Supercritical Schrödinger Equation
A Structure Theorem for Level Sets of Multiplicative Functions and Applications
abstract: Given a level set E of an arbitrary multiplicative function f, we establish, by building on the fundamental work of Frantzikinakis and Host [14, 15], a structure theorem that gives a decomposition of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1_{E}$</tex> into an almost periodic and a pseudo-random part. Using this structure theorem together with the technique developed by the authors in [3], we obtain the following result pertaining to polynomial multiple recurrence.

articleTitle: Plancherel Distribution of Satake Parameters of Maass Cusp Forms on GL3
abstract: We prove an equidistribution result for the Satake parameters of Maass cusp forms on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{GL}_{3}$</tex> with respect to the p-adic Plancherel measure by using an application of the Kuznetsov trace formula. The techniques developed in this paper deal with the removal of arithmetic weight <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L(1,F,\operatorname{Ad})^{-1}$</tex> in the Kuznetsov trace formula on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{GL}_{3}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Stratification for Multiplicative Character Sums
abstract: We prove a stratification result for certain families of n-dimensional (complete algebraic) multiplicative character sums. The character sums we consider are sums of products of r multiplicative characters evaluated at rational functions, and the families (with nr parameters) are obtained by allowing each of the r rational functions to be replaced by an “offset”, that is, a translate, of itself. For very general such families, we show that the stratum of the parameter space on which the character sum has maximum weight <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n+j$</tex> has codimension at least j⌊(r − 1)/2(n − 1)⌋ for 1 ≤ j ≤ n − 1 and ⌈nr/2⌉ for j = n. This result is used to obtain multivariate Burgess bounds in joint work with Lillian Pierce.

articleTitle: Affine Wreath Product Algebras
abstract: We study the structure and representation theory of affine wreath product algebras and their cyclotomic quotients. These algebras, which appear naturally in Heisenberg categorification, simultaneously unify and generalize many important algebras appearing in the literature. In particular, special cases include degenerate affine Hecke algebras, affine Sergeev algebras (degenerate affine Hecke–Clifford algebras), and wreath Hecke algebras. In some cases, specializing the results of the current paper recovers known results, but with unified and simplified proofs. In other cases, we obtain new results, including proofs of two open conjectures of Kleshchev and Muth.

articleTitle: Almost Euclidean Isoperimetric Inequalities in Spaces Satisfying Local Ricci Curvature Lower Bounds
abstract: Motivated by Perelman’s Pseudo-Locality Theorem for the Ricci flow, we prove that if a Riemannian manifold has Ricci curvature bounded below in a metric ball which moreover has almost maximal volume, then in a smaller ball (in a quantified sense) it holds an almost euclidean isoperimetric inequality. The result is actually established in the more general framework of non-smooth spaces satisfying local Ricci curvature lower bounds in a synthetic sense via optimal transportation.

articleTitle: The Homology Class of a Poisson Transversal
abstract: This note is devoted to the study of the homology class of a compact Poisson transversal in a Poisson manifold. For specific classes of Poisson structures, such as unimodular Poisson structures and Poisson manifolds with closed leaves, we prove that all their compact Poisson transversals represent nontrivial homology classes, generalizing the symplectic case. We discuss several examples in which this property does not hold, as well as a weaker version of this property, which holds for log-symplectic structures. Finally, we extend our results to Dirac geometry.

articleTitle: Classifying Spaces for the Family of Virtually Cyclic Subgroups of Braid Groups
abstract: We prove that, for n ≥ 3, the minimal dimension of a model of the classifying space of the braid group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{n}$</tex>, and of the pure braid group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{n}$</tex>, with respect to the family of virtually cyclic groups is n.

articleTitle: Torsion and K-theory for Some Free Wreath Products
abstract: We classify torsion actions of free wreath products of arbitrary compact quantum groups by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{N}^{+}$</tex> and use this to prove that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{G}$</tex> is a torsion-free compact quantum group satisfying the strong Baum–Connes property then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{G}\wr _{\ast }S_{N}^{+}$</tex> also satisfies the strong Baum–Connes property. We then compute the K-theory of free wreath products of classical and quantum free groups by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SO_{q}(3)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Compactifications of Universal Moduli Spaces of Vector Bundles and the Log-Minimal Model Program on M‾g
abstract: Recent work on the log-minimal model program for the moduli space of curves, as well as past results of Caporaso, Pandharipande, and Simpson motivate an investigation of compactifications of the universal moduli space of slope semi-stable vector bundles over moduli spaces of curves arising in the Hassett–Keel program. Our main result is the construction of a compactification of the universal moduli space of vector bundles over several of these moduli spaces, along with a complete description in the case of pseudo-stable curves.

articleTitle: Moduli Spaces of Representations of Special Biserial Algebras
abstract: We show that the irreducible components of any moduli space of semistable representations of a special biserial algebra are always isomorphic to products of projective spaces of various dimensions. This is done by showing that irreducible components of varieties of representations of special biserial algebras are isomorphic to irreducible components of products of varieties of circular complexes and therefore normal, allowing us to apply recent results of the second and third authors on moduli spaces.

articleTitle: Universal Series for Hilbert Schemes and Strange Duality
abstract: We show how the “finite Quot scheme method” applied to Le Potier’s strange duality on del Pezzo surfaces leads to conjectures (valid for all smooth complex projective surfaces) relating two sets of universal power series on Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces: those for top Chern classes of tautological sheaves and those for Euler characteristics of line bundles. We have verified these predictions computationally for low order. We then give an analysis of these conjectures in small ranks. We also give a combinatorial proof of a formula predicted by our conjectures: the top Chern class of the tautological sheaf on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^{[n]}$</tex> associated to the structure sheaf of a point is equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-1)^n$</tex> times the nth Catalan number.

articleTitle: The Average of the Smallest Prime in a Conjugacy Class
abstract: Let C be a conjugacy class of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{n}$</tex> and K an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{n}$</tex>-field. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n_{K,C}$</tex> be the smallest prime, which is ramified or whose Frobenius automorphism Frob<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{p}$</tex> does not belong to C. Under some technical conjectures, we show that the average of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n_{K,C}$</tex> is a constant. We explicitly compute the constant. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{3}$</tex>- and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{4}$</tex>-fields, our result is unconditional. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{K,C}$</tex> be the smallest prime for which Frob<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{p}$</tex> belongs to C. We obtain the average of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{K,C}$</tex> under some technical conjectures. For n = 3 and C = [(12)], we have the average value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{K,C}$</tex> unconditionally.

articleTitle: Local Spectral Gap in the Group of Euclidean Isometries
abstract: We provide new examples of translation actions on locally compact groups with the “local spectral gap property” introduced in [5]. This property has applications to strong ergodicity, the Banach–Ruziewicz problem, orbit equivalence rigidity, and equidecomposable sets. The main group of study here is the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Isom}\left (\mathbb{R}^{d}\right )$</tex> of orientation-preserving isometries of the Euclidean space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^{d}$</tex>, for d ≥ 3. We prove that the translation action of a countable dense subgroup Γ on Isom<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left (\mathbb R^{d}\right )$</tex> has local spectral gap, whenever the translation action of the rotation projection of Γ on SO(d) has spectral gap. Our proof relies on the amenability of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Isom}\left (\mathbb{R}^{d}\right )$</tex> and on work of Lindenstrauss and Varjú [12].

articleTitle: Six-vertex Models and the GUE-corners Process
abstract: We consider a class of probability distributions on the six-vertex model, which originates from the higher spin vertex models of [13]. We define operators, inspired by the Macdonald difference operators, which extract various correlation functions, measuring the probability of observing different arrow configurations. For the class of models we consider, the correlation functions can be expressed in terms of multiple contour integrals, which are suitable for asymptotic analysis. For a particular choice of parameters we analyze the limit of the correlation functions through the steepest descent method. Combining this asymptotic statement with some new results about Gibbs measures on Gelfand–Tsetlin cones and patterns, we show that the asymptotic behavior of our six-vertex model near the boundary is described by the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble-corners process.

articleTitle: On Strongly Anisotropic Type I Blowup
abstract: We consider the energy super critical four-dimensional semilinear heat equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$ \partial_{t}u=\Delta u+|u|^{p-1}u, \ \ x\in \mathbb R^{4}, \ \ p>5.$$</tex>Let Φ(r) be a three-dimensional radial self-similar solution for the three supercritical problem as exhibited and studied in [7].
