We show the finite codimensional transversal stability of the corresponding blow-up solution by exhibiting a manifold of finite energy blow-up solutions of the four-dimensional problem with cylindrical symmetry which blows up as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$ u(t,x)\sim \frac{1}{(T-t)^{\frac{1}{p-1}}}U(t,Y), \ \ Y=\frac{x}{\sqrt{T-t}}$$</tex>with the profile U given to leading order by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$ U(t,Y)\sim\frac{1}{(1+b(t)z^{2})^{\frac{1}{p-1}}}\Phi\left(\frac{r}{\sqrt{1+b(t)z^{2}}}\right), \ \ Y=(r,z), \ \ b(t)=\frac{c}{|\log (T-t)|}$$</tex>corresponding to a constant profile Φ(r) in the z direction reconnected to zero along the moving free boundary <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|z(t)|\sim \frac{1}{\sqrt{b}}\sim \sqrt{|\log (T-t)|}.$</tex> Our analysis revisits the stability analysis of the self-similar ordinary differential equations (ODE) blowup [1, 28, 29] and combines it with the study of the type I self-similar blowup [7]. This provides a robust canonical framework for the construction of strongly anisotropic blow-up bubbles.

articleTitle: Mapping Borel Sets onto Balls and Self-similar Sets by Lipschitz and Nearly Lipschitz Maps
abstract: If X is an analytic metric space satisfying a very mild doubling condition, then for any finite Borel measure μ on X there is a set N ⊆ X such that μ(N) > 0, an ultrametric space Z and a Lipschitz bijection ϕ : N → Z whose inverse is nearly Lipschitz, i.e., β-Hölder for all β < 1. As an application it is shown that a Borel set in a Euclidean space maps onto [0, 1]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> by a nearly Lipschitz map if and only if it cannot be covered by countably many sets of Hausdorff dimension strictly below n. The argument extends to analytic metric spaces satisfying the mild condition. Further generalization replaces cubes with self-similar sets, nearly Lipschitz maps with nearly Hölder maps and integer dimension with arbitrary finite dimension.

articleTitle: Dynamic ASEP, Duality, and Continuous q−1-Hermite Polynomials
abstract: We demonstrate a Markov duality between the dynamic asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) and the standard ASEP. We then apply this to step initial data, as well as a half-stationary initial data (which we introduce). While investigating the duality for half-stationary initial data, we uncover and utilize connections to the continuous q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>-Hermite polynomials. Finally, we introduce a family of stationary initial data which are related to the indeterminate moment problem associated with these q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>-Hermite polynomials.

articleTitle: Change of Polarization for Moduli of Sheaves on Surfaces as Bridgeland Wall-crossing
abstract: We prove that the “Thaddeus flips” of L-twisted sheaves constructed by Matsuki and Wentworth explaining the change of polarization for Gieseker semistable sheaves on a surface can be obtained via Bridgeland wall-crossing. Similarly, we realize the change of polarization for moduli spaces of one-dimensional Gieseker semistable sheaves on a surface by varying a family of stability conditions.

articleTitle: Miquel Dynamics for Circle Patterns
abstract: We study a new discrete-time dynamical system on circle patterns with the combinatorics of the square grid. This dynamics, called Miquel dynamics, relies on Miquel’s six circles theorem. We provide a coordinatization of the appropriate space of circle patterns on which the dynamics acts and use it to derive local recurrence formulas. Isoradial circle patterns arise as periodic points of Miquel dynamics. Furthermore, we prove that certain signed sums of intersection angles are preserved by the dynamics. Finally, when the initial circle pattern is spatially biperiodic with a fundamental domain of size two by two, we show that the appropriately normalized motion of intersection points of circles takes place along an explicit quartic curve.

articleTitle: On the Random Wave Conjecture for Eisenstein Series
abstract: We obtain an asymptotic for the regularized 4th moment of the Eisenstein series for the full modular group, in agreement with the Random Wave Conjecture.

articleTitle: Universal Sums of m-Gonal Numbers
abstract: In this paper we study universal quadratic polynomials, which arise as sums of polygonal numbers. Specifically, we determine an asymptotic upper bound (as a function of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>) on the size of the set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_m\subset{\mathbb{N}}$</tex> such that if a sum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>-gonal numbers represents <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_m$</tex>, then it represents <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{N}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Exponential Sums Over Finite Fields and the Large Sieve
abstract: By using a variant of the large sieve for Frobenius in compatible systems developed in [24] and [27], we obtain zero-density estimates for arguments of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell $</tex>-adic trace functions over finite fields with values in some algebraic subsets of the cyclotomic integers, when the monodromy groups are known. This applies in particular to hyper-Kloosterman sums and general exponential sums considered by Katz.

articleTitle: Dirichlet Problem for Maximal Graphs of Higher Codimension
abstract: We consider the Dirichlet boundary value problem for graphical maximal submanifolds inside Lorentzian-type ambient spaces and obtain general existence and uniqueness results that apply to any codimension.

articleTitle: The Equations Defining Affine Grassmannians in Type A and a Conjecture of Kreiman, Lakshmibai, Magyar, and Weyman
abstract: The affine Grassmannian of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SL_n$</tex> admits an embedding into the Sato Grassmannian, which further admits a Plücker embedding into the projectivization of Fermion Fock space. Kreiman, Lakshmibai, Magyar, and Weyman describe the linear part of the ideal defining this embedding in terms of certain elements of the dual of Fock space called shuffles, and they conjecture that these elements together with the Plücker relations suffice to cut out the affine Grassmannian. We give a proof of this conjecture in two steps; first, we reinterpret the shuffle equations in terms of Frobenius twists of symmetric functions. Using this, we reduce to a finite-dimensional problem, which we solve. For the 2nd step, we introduce a finite-dimensional analogue of the affine Grassmannian of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SL_n$</tex>, which we conjecture to be precisely the reduced subscheme of a finite-dimensional Grassmannian consisting of subspaces invariant under a nilpotent operator.

articleTitle: Seshadri Constants for Curve Classes
abstract: We develop a local positivity theory for movable curves on projective varieties similar to the classical Seshadri constants of nef divisors. We give analogues of the Seshadri ampleness criterion, of a characterization of the augmented base locus of a big and nef divisor, and of the interpretation of Seshadri constants as an asymptotic measure of jet separation. As application, we show in any characteristic that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> is a smooth curve with ample normal bundle in a smooth projective variety then the class of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> is in the strict interior of the Mori cone. This was conjectured by Peternell and proved by Ottem and Lau in Characteristic 0.

articleTitle: Localizing Virtual Structure Sheaves by Cosections
abstract: We construct a cosection-localized virtual structure sheaf when a Deligne–Mumford stack is equipped with a perfect obstruction theory and a cosection of the obstruction sheaf.

articleTitle: Stable Polarized del Pezzo Surfaces
abstract: We give a simple sufficient condition for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-stability of polarized del Pezzo surfaces and for the existence of a constant scalar curvature Kähler metric in the Kähler class corresponding to the polarization.

articleTitle: On Representation of Integers from Thin Subgroups of SL(2, ℤ) with Parabolics
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda <SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$</tex> be a finitely generated, nonelementary Fuchsian group of the 2nd kind, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{v},\mathbf{w}$</tex> be two primitive vectors in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}^2\!-\!\mathbf{0}$</tex>. We consider the set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{S}\!=\!\{\left \langle \mathbf{v}\gamma ,\mathbf{w}\right \rangle _{\mathbb{R}^2}\!:\!\gamma\! \in\! \Lambda \}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left \langle \cdot ,\cdot \right \rangle _{\mathbb{R}^2}$</tex> is the standard inner product in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^2$</tex>. Using Hardy–Littlewood circle method and some infinite co-volume lattice point counting techniques developed by Bourgain, Kontorovich, and Sarnak, together with Gamburd’s 5/6 spectral gap, we show that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda $</tex> has parabolic elements, and the critical exponent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta $</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda $</tex> exceeds 0.998317, then a density-one subset of all admissible integers (i.e., integers passing all local obstructions) are actually in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{S}$</tex>, with a power savings on the size of the exceptional set (i.e., the set of admissible integers failing to appear in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{S}$</tex>). This supplements a result of Bourgain–Kontorovich, which proves a density-one statement for the case when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda $</tex> is free, finitely generated, has no parabolics, and has critical exponent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta>0.999950$</tex>.

articleTitle: On Higher Special Elements of p-adic Representations
abstract: As a natural generalisation of the notion of “higher rank Euler system”, we develop a theory of “higher special elements” in the exterior power biduals of the Galois cohomology of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic representations. We show, in particular, that such elements encode detailed information about the structure of Galois cohomology groups and are related by families of congruences involving natural height pairings on cohomology. As a first concrete application of the approach, we use it to refine, and extend, a variety of existing results and conjectures concerning the values of derivatives of Dirichlet <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-series.

articleTitle: Generic IllPosedness for Wave Equation of Power Type on Three-Dimensional Torus
abstract: In the present work, we show that the wave equation in three-dimensional torus of power-type nonlinearity is ill posed around any (relatively) regular dynamics in the super-critical regime. In the cubic case, we can even choose the regular dynamics to be the smooth one. This result can serve as one motivation to consider initial datum as an “ensemble” to measure the size of the set of these “bad” datum in the sense of probability. This work also indicates that the probabilistic solutions constructed, for instance, in Burq–Tzvetkov [4] can only be well approximated by smooth solutions issued from certain regularized datum.

articleTitle: The Centre-Quotient Property and Weak Centrality for C*-Algebras
abstract: We give a number of equivalent conditions (including weak centrality) for a general <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*$</tex>-algebra to have the centre-quotient property. We show that every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*$</tex>-algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> has a largest weakly central ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J_{wc}(A)$</tex>. For an ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex> of a unital <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*$</tex>-algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>, we find a necessary and sufficient condition for a central element of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A/I$</tex> to lift to a central element of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>. This leads to a characterisation of the set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_A$</tex> of elements of an arbitrary <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*$</tex>-algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>, which prevent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> from having the centre-quotient property. The complement <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{CQ}(A):= A \setminus V_A$</tex> always contains <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z(A)+J_{wc}(A)$</tex> (where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z(A)$</tex> is the centre of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>), with equality if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A/J_{wc}(A)$</tex> is abelian. Otherwise, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{CQ}(A)$</tex> fails spectacularly to be a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*$</tex>-subalgebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>.

articleTitle: Optimal Estimates for Steklov Eigenvalue Gaps and Ratios on Warped Product Manifolds
abstract: We consider an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-dimensional smooth Riemannian manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M^n=[0,R)\times \mathbb{S}^{n-1}$</tex> endowed with a warped product metric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g=dr^2+h^2(r)g_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}$</tex> and diffeomorphic to a Euclidean ball. Suppose that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> has strictly convex boundary. First, for the classical Steklov eigenvalue problem, we derive an optimal lower (upper, respectively) bound for its eigenvalue gaps in terms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^{\prime}(R)/h(R)$</tex> when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Ric_g\geq 0$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq 0$</tex>, respectively). Second, in the same spirit, for two 4th-order Steklov eigenvalue problems studied by Kuttler and Sigillito in 1968, we deduce an optimal lower bound for their eigenvalue gaps in terms of either <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^{\prime}(R)/h^3(R)$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^{\prime}(R)/h(R)$</tex> when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=2$</tex> and the Gaussian curvature is nonnegative. We also consider optimal estimates on the eigenvalue ratios for these eigenvalue problems.

articleTitle: Species with Potential Arising from Surfaces with Orbifold Points of Order 2, Part II: Arbitrary Weights
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\boldsymbol{\Sigma }}=(\Sigma ,\mathbb{M},\mathbb{O})$</tex> be either an unpunctured surface with marked points and order-2 orbifold points or a once-punctured closed surface with order-2 orbifold points. For each pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\tau ,\omega )$</tex> consisting of a triangulation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau $</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\boldsymbol{\Sigma }}$</tex> and a function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega :\mathbb{O}\rightarrow \{1,4\}$</tex>, we define a chain complex <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_\bullet (\tau , \omega )$</tex> with coefficients in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_2=\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$</tex>. Given <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\boldsymbol{\Sigma }}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega $</tex>, we define a colored triangulation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\boldsymbol{\Sigma }_\omega }=(\Sigma ,\mathbb{M},\mathbb{O},\omega )$</tex> to be a pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\tau ,\xi )$</tex> consisting of a triangulation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\boldsymbol{\Sigma }}$</tex> and a 1-cocycle in the cochain complex that is dual to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_\bullet (\tau , \omega )$</tex>; the combinatorial notion of colored flip of colored triangulations is then defined as a refinement of the notion of flip of triangulations. Our main construction associates to each colored triangulation a species and a potential, and our main result shows that colored triangulations related by a flip have species with potentials (SPs) related by the corresponding SP-mutation as defined in [25]. We define the flip graph of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\boldsymbol{\Sigma }_\omega }$</tex> as the graph whose vertices are the pairs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\tau ,x)$</tex> consisting of a triangulation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau $</tex> and a cohomology class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x\in H^1(C^\bullet (\tau , \omega ))$</tex>, with an edge connecting two such pairs, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\tau ,x)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\sigma ,z),$</tex> if and only if there exist 1-cocycles <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\xi \in x$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\zeta \in z$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\tau ,\xi )$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\sigma ,\zeta )$</tex> are colored triangulations related by a colored flip; then we prove that this flip graph is always disconnected provided the underlying surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma $</tex> is not contractible. In the absence of punctures, we show that the Jacobian algebras of the SPs constructed are finite-dimensional and that whenever two colored triangulations have the same underlying triangulation, the Jacobian algebras of their associated SPs are isomorphic if and only if the underlying 1-cocycles have the same cohomology class. We also give a full classification of the nondegenerate SPs one can associate to any given pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\tau ,\omega )$</tex> over cyclic Galois extensions with certain roots of unity. The species constructed here are species realizations of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{|\mathbb{O}|}$</tex> skew-symmetrizable matrices that Felikson–Shapiro–Tumarkin associated in [17] to any given triangulation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\boldsymbol{\Sigma }}$</tex>. In the prequel [25] of this paper we constructed a species realization of only one of these matrices, but therein we allowed the presence of arbitrarily many punctures.

articleTitle: On the Geometry of Some Equivariantly Related Manifolds
abstract: We provide geometric realizations of both classical and “exotic” <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>-manifolds such as spheres, Kervaire manifolds, bundles over spheres, homogeneous spaces, and connected sums among them. As an application, we apply the process known as Cheeger deformation to produce new metrics of both positive Ricci and almost non-negative curvature on such objects.

articleTitle: Topologically Nontrivial Counterexamples to Sard’s Theorem
abstract: We prove the following dichotomy: if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=2,3$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\in C^1(\mathbb{S}^{n+1},\mathbb{S}^n)$</tex> is not homotopic to a constant map, then there is an open set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega \subset \mathbb{S}^{n+1}$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{rank} df=n$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega $</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f(\Omega )$</tex> is dense in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^n$</tex>, while for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 4$</tex>, there is a map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\in C^1(\mathbb{S}^{n+1},\mathbb{S}^n)$</tex> that is not homotopic to a constant map and such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{rank} df<n$</tex> everywhere. The result in the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 4$</tex> answers a question of Larry Guth.

articleTitle: Tensor Diagrams and Chebyshev Polynomials
abstract: In this paper, we describe a class of elements in the ring of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{SL}(V)$</tex>-invariant polynomial functions on the space of configurations of vectors and linear forms of a 3D vector space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V.$</tex> These elements are related to one another by an induction formula using Chebyshev polynomials. We also investigate the relation between these polynomials and G. Lusztig’s dual canonical basis in tensor products of representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3(\mathbb C)).$</tex>

articleTitle: Rabinowitz Floer Homology for Tentacular Hamiltonians
abstract: This paper extends the definition of Rabinowitz Floer homology to non-compact hypersurfaces. We present a general framework for the construction of Rabinowitz Floer homology in the non-compact setting under suitable compactness assumptions on the periodic orbits and the moduli spaces of Floer trajectories. We introduce a class of hypersurfaces arising as the level sets of specific Hamiltonians: strongly tentacular Hamiltonians for which the compactness conditions are satisfied, cf. [21], thus enabling us to define the Rabinowitz Floer homology for this class. Rabinowitz Floer homology in turn serves as a tool to address the Weinstein conjecture and establish existence of closed characteristics for non-compact contact manifolds.

articleTitle: Toric Geometry of Spin(7)-Manifolds
abstract: We study <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \operatorname{Spin}(7) $</tex>-manifolds with an effective multi-Hamiltonian action of a four-torus. On an open dense set, we provide a Gibbons–Hawking type ansatz that describes such geometries in terms of a symmetric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ 4\times 4 $</tex>-matrix of functions. This description leads to the 1st known <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \operatorname{Spin}(7) $</tex>-manifolds with a rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ 4 $</tex> symmetry group and full holonomy. We also show that the multi-moment map exhibits the full orbit space topologically as a smooth four-manifold, containing a trivalent graph in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \mathbb{R}^4 $</tex> as the image of the set of the special orbits.

articleTitle: Manifolds of Isospectral Matrices and Hessenberg Varieties
abstract: We consider the space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_h$</tex> of Hermitian matrices having staircase form and the given simple spectrum. There is a natural action of a compact torus on this space. Using generalized Toda flow, we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_h$</tex> is a smooth manifold and its smooth type is independent of the spectrum. Morse theory is then used to show the vanishing of odd degree cohomology, so that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_h$</tex> is an equivariantly formal manifold. The equivariant and ordinary cohomology rings of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_h$</tex> are described using GKM theory. The main goal of this paper is to show the connection between the manifolds <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_h$</tex> and regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties well known in algebraic geometry. Both spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_h$</tex> and Hessenberg varieties form wonderful families of submanifolds in the complete flag variety. There is a certain symmetry between these families, which can be generalized to other submanifolds of the flag variety.

articleTitle: The 8th Moment of the Family of Γ1(q)-Automorphic L-Functions
abstract: We prove a Lindelöf on average bound for the 8th moment of a family of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions attached to automorphic forms on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL(2)$</tex>, the first time this has been accomplished. Previously, such a bound had been proven for the 6th moment for our family by Djanković [3] and for a similar family by Young [9]. Our proof rests on a new approach that overcomes the lack of perfect orthogonality in the family initially observed by Iwaniec and Li [6].

articleTitle: On the Monoidality of Saito Reflection Functors
abstract: We extend the definition of the Saito reflection functor of the Khovanov–Lauda–Rouquier algebras to the case of symmetric Kac–Moody algebras and prove that it defines a monoidal functor.

articleTitle: A Non-varying Phenomenon with an Application to the Wind-Tree Model
abstract: We exhibit a non-varying phenomenon for the counting problem of cylinders, weighted by their area, passing through two marked (regular) Weierstrass points of a translation surface in a hyperelliptic connected component <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{H}^{hyp}(2g-2)$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{H}^{hyp}(g-1,g-1)$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g> 1$</tex>. As an application, we obtain the non-varying phenomenon for the counting problem of (weighted) periodic trajectories on the Ehrenfest wind-tree model, a billiard in the plane endowed with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}^2$</tex>-periodically located identical rectangular obstacles.

articleTitle: The Groupoids of Adaptable Separated Graphs and Their Type Semigroups
abstract: Given an adaptable separated graph, we construct an associated groupoid and explore its type semigroup. Specifically, we first attach to each adaptable separated graph a corresponding semigroup, which we prove is an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E^*$</tex>-unitary inverse semigroup. As a consequence, the tight groupoid of this semigroup is a Hausdorff étale groupoid. We show that this groupoid is always amenable and that the type semigroups of groupoids obtained from adaptable separated graphs in this way include all finitely generated conical refinement monoids. The first three named authors will utilize this construction in forthcoming work to solve the realization problem for von Neumann regular rings, in the finitely generated case.

articleTitle: On BMO and Carleson Measures on Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{M}$</tex> be a Riemannian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-manifold with a metric such that the manifold is Ahlfors regular. We also assume either non-negative Ricci curvature or the Ricci curvature is bounded from below together with a bound on the gradient of the heat kernel. We characterize BMO-functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u: \mathcal{M} \to \mathbb{R}$</tex> by a Carleson measure condition of their <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma $</tex>-harmonic extension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U: \mathcal{M} \times (0,\infty ) \to \mathbb{R}$</tex>. We make crucial use of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T(b)$</tex> theorem proved by Hofmann, Mitrea, Mitrea, and Morris. As an application, we show that the famous theorem of Coifman–Lions–Meyer–Semmes holds in this class of manifolds: Jacobians of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W^{1,n}$</tex>-maps from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{M}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^n$</tex> can be estimated against BMO-functions, which now follows from the arguments for commutators recently proposed by Lenzmann and the 2nd-named author using only harmonic extensions, integration by parts, and trace space characterizations.

articleTitle: Fock Space Representation of the Circle Quantum Group
abstract: In [12] we have defined quantum groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{U}_{\upsilon }(\mathfrak{sl}(\mathbb{R}))$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{U}_{\upsilon }(\mathfrak{sl}(S^1))$</tex>, which can be interpreted as continuum generalizations of the quantum groups of the Kac–Moody Lie algebras of finite, respectively affine type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>. In the present paper, we define the Fock space representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{F}_{\mathbb{R}}$</tex> of the quantum group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{U}_{\upsilon }(\mathfrak{sl}(\mathbb{R}))$</tex> as the vector space generated by real pyramids (a continuum generalization of the notion of partition). In addition, by using a variant version of the “folding procedure” of Hayashi–Misra–Miwa, we define an action of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{U}_{\upsilon }(\mathfrak{sl}(S^1))$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{F}_{\mathbb{R}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Bochner-type Formulas for the Weyl Tensor on Four-dimensional Einstein Manifolds
abstract: The very definition of an Einstein metric implies that all its geometry is encoded in the Weyl tensor. With this in mind, in this paper we derive higher-order Bochner-type formulas for the Weyl tensor on a four-dimensional Einstein manifold. In particular, we prove a 2nd Bochner-type formula that, formally, extends to the covariant derivative level the classical one for the Weyl tensor obtained by Derdziński in 1983. As a consequence, we deduce new integral identities involving the Weyl tensor and its derivatives on a compact four-dimensional Einstein manifold and we derive a new rigidity result.

articleTitle: Real Algebraic Curves on Real del Pezzo Surfaces
abstract: The study of the topology of real algebraic varieties dates back to the work of Harnack, Klein, and Hilbert in the 19th century; in particular, the isotopy-type classification of real algebraic curves in real toric surfaces is a classical subject that has undergone considerable evolution. On the other hand, not much is known for more general ambient surfaces. We take a step forward in the study of topological-type classification of real algebraic curves on non-toric surfaces focusing on real del Pezzo surfaces of degree 1 and 2 with multi-components real part. We use degeneration methods and real enumerative geometry in combination with variations of classical methods to give obstructions to the existence of topological-type classes realized by real algebraic curves and to give constructions of real algebraic curves with prescribed topology.

articleTitle: An Integralgeometric Approach to Dorronsoro Estimates
abstract: A theorem of Dorronsoro from 1985 quantifies the fact that a Lipschitz function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f \colon \mathbb{R}^{n} \to \mathbb{R}$</tex> can be approximated by affine functions almost everywhere, and at sufficiently small scales. This paper contains a new, purely geometric, proof of Dorronsoro's theorem. In brief, it reduces the problem in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^{n}$</tex> to a problem in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^{n - 1}$</tex> via integralgeometric considerations. For the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n = 1$</tex>, a short geometric proof already exists in the literature. A similar proof technique applies to parabolic Lipschitz functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f \colon \mathbb{R}^{n - 1} \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$</tex>. A natural Dorronsoro estimate in this class is known, due to Hofmann. The method presented here allows one to reduce the parabolic problem to the Euclidean one and to obtain an elementary proof also in this setting. As a corollary, I deduce an analogue of Rademacher's theorem for parabolic Lipschitz functions.

articleTitle: Algebraic Tangent Cones of Reflexive Sheaves
abstract: We study the notion of algebraic tangent cones at singularities of reflexive sheaves. These correspond to extensions of reflexive sheaves across a negative divisor. We show the existence of optimal extensions in a constructive manner, and we prove the uniqueness in a suitable sense. The results here are an algebro-geometric counterpart of our previous study on singularities of Hermitian–Yang–Mills connections.

articleTitle: $q$-Racah Ensemble and Discrete Painlevé Equation
abstract: The goal of this paper is to investigate the missing part of the story about the relationship between the orthogonal polynomial ensembles and Painlevé equations. Namely, we consider the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-Racah polynomial ensemble and show that the one-interval gap probabilities in this case can be expressed through a solution of the discrete <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-P<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left (E_7^{(1)}/A_{1}^{(1)}\right )$</tex> equation. Our approach also gives a new Lax pair for this equation. This Lax pair has an interesting additional involutive symmetry structure.

articleTitle: On the Supersingular Reduction of K3 Surfaces with Complex Multiplication
abstract: We study the good reduction modulo <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K3$</tex> surfaces with complex multiplication. If a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K3$</tex> surface with complex multiplication has good reduction, we calculate the Picard number and the height of the formal Brauer group of the reduction. Moreover, if the reduction is supersingular, we calculate its Artin invariant under some assumptions. Our results generalize some results of Shimada for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K3$</tex> surfaces with Picard number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20$</tex>. Our methods rely on the main theorem of complex multiplication for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K3$</tex> surfaces by Rizov, an explicit description of the Breuil–Kisin modules associated with Lubin–Tate characters due to Andreatta, Goren, Howard, and Madapusi Pera, and the integral comparison theorem recently established by Bhatt, Morrow, and Scholze.

articleTitle: Counting One-Sided Simple Closed Geodesics on Fuchsian Thrice Punctured Projective Planes
abstract: We prove that there is a true asymptotic formula for the number of one-sided simple closed curves of length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq L$</tex> on any Fuchsian real projective plane with three points removed. The exponent of growth is independent of the hyperbolic metric, and it is noninteger, in contrast to counting results of Mirzakhani for simple closed curves on orientable Fuchsian surfaces.

articleTitle: Quasi-Affineness and the 1-Resolution Property
abstract: We prove that, under mild hypothesis, every normal algebraic space that satisfies the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>-resolution property is quasi-affine. More generally, we show that for algebraic stacks satisfying similar hypotheses, the 1-resolution property guarantees the existence of a finite flat cover by a quasi-affine scheme.

articleTitle: Hopf-algebraic Deformations of Products and Wick Polynomials
abstract: We present an approach to cumulant–moment relations and Wick polynomials based on extensive use of convolution products of linear functionals on a coalgebra. This allows, in particular, to understand the construction of Wick polynomials as the result of a Hopf algebra deformation under the action of linear automorphisms induced by multivariate moments associated to an arbitrary family of random variables with moments of all orders. We also generalize the notion of deformed product in order to discuss how these ideas appear in the recent theory of regularity structures.

articleTitle: Log Picard Algebroids and Meromorphic Line Bundles
abstract: We introduce logarithmic Picard algebroids, a natural class of Lie algebroids adapted to a simple normal crossings divisor on a smooth projective variety. We show that such algebroids are classified by a subspace of the de Rham cohomology of the divisor complement determined by its mixed Hodge structure. We then solve the prequantization problem, showing that under the appropriate integrality condition, a log Picard algebroid is the Lie algebroid of symmetries of what is called a meromorphic line bundle, a generalization of the usual notion of line bundle in which the fibers degenerate along the divisor. We give a geometric description of such bundles and establish a classification theorem for them, showing that they correspond to a subgroup of the holomorphic line bundles on the divisor complement. Importantly, these holomorphic line bundles need not be algebraic. Finally, we provide concrete methods for explicitly constructing examples of meromorphic line bundles, such as for a smooth cubic divisor in the projective plane.

articleTitle: Singularities of Divisors of Low Degree on Simple Abelian Varieties
abstract: It is known by the results of Kollár, Ein, Lazarsfeld, Hacon, and Debarre that effective divisors representing principal and other low-degree polarizations on complex abelian varieties have mild singularities. In this note, we extend these results to all polarizations of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<g$</tex> on simple <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex>-dimensional abelian varieties, settling a conjecture of Debarre and Hacon.

articleTitle: Counterexamples to Quasiconcavity for the Heat Equation
abstract: We construct solutions to the heat equation on convex rings showing that quasiconcavity may not be preserved along the flow, even for smooth and subharmonic initial data.

articleTitle: Gaussian Width Bounds with Applications to Arithmetic Progressions in Random Settings
abstract: Motivated by a problem on random differences in Szemerédi’s theorem and another problem on large deviations for arithmetic progressions in random sets, we prove upper bounds on the Gaussian width of special point sets in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^k$</tex>. The point sets are formed by the image of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-dimensional Boolean hypercube under a mapping <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi :\mathbb{R}^n\to \mathbb{R}^k$</tex>, where each coordinate is a constant-degree multilinear polynomial with 0-1 coefficients. We show the following applications of our bounds. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\mathbb{Z}/N\,\mathbb{Z}]_p$</tex> be the random subset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}/N\,\mathbb{Z}$</tex> containing each element independently with probability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1) $</tex> A set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D\subseteq \mathbb{Z}/N\,\mathbb{Z}$</tex> is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell $</tex>-intersective if any dense subset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}/N\,\mathbb{Z}$</tex> contains a proper <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\ell +1)$</tex>-term arithmetic progression with common difference in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>. Our main result implies that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\mathbb{Z}/N\,\mathbb{Z}]_p$</tex> is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell $</tex>-intersective with probability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 - o(1)$</tex> provided <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p \geq \omega (N^{-\beta _\ell }\log N)$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta _\ell = (\lceil (\ell +1)/2\rceil )^{-1}$</tex>. This gives a polynomial improvement for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell \ge 2$</tex> of a previous bound due to Frantzikinakis, Lesigne, and Wierdl, and reproves more directly the same improvement shown recently by the authors and Dvir (here we avoid the theories of locally decodable codes and quantum information). <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2) $</tex> Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_k$</tex> be the number of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-term arithmetic progressions in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\mathbb{Z}/N\,\mathbb{Z}]_p$</tex> and consider the large deviation rate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho _k(\delta ) = \log \textrm{ Pr}[\,X_k \geq (1+\delta )\mathbb{E}X_k\,]$</tex>. We give quadratic improvements of the best-known range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> for which a highly precise estimate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho _k(\delta )$</tex> due to Bhattacharya, Ganguly, Shao, and Zhao is valid for all odd <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k \geq 5$</tex>. In particular, the estimate holds if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p \geq \omega (N^{-c_k}\log N)$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_k = (6k\lceil (k-1)/2\rceil )^{-1}$</tex>. We also discuss connections with the above-mentioned error correcting codes (locally decodable codes) and the Banach-space notion of type for injective tensor products of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell _p$</tex>-spaces.

articleTitle: On Nonlinear Profile Decompositions and Scattering for an NLS–ODE Model
abstract: In this paper, we consider a Hamiltonian system combining a nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS) and an ordinary differential equation. This system is a simplified model of the NLS around soliton solutions. Following Nakanishi [33], we show scattering of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex> small <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^1$</tex> radial solutions. The proof is based on Nakanishi’s framework and Fermi Golden Rule estimates on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^4$</tex> in time norms.

articleTitle: On Smooth Solutions to One Phase-Free Boundary Problem in ℝn
abstract: We construct a smooth axially symmetric solution to the classical one phase free boundary problem in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^{n}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 3.$</tex> Its free boundary is of “catenoid” type. This is a higher dimensional analogy of the Hauswirth–Helein–Pacard solution [18] in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^{2}$</tex>. The existence of such solution is conjectured in [18, Remark 2.4]. This is the 1st nontrivial smooth solution to the one phase-free boundary problem in higher dimensions.

articleTitle: Volume Growth, Curvature, and Buser-Type Inequalities in Graphs
abstract: We study the volume growth of metric balls as a function of the radius in discrete spaces and focus on the relationship between volume growth and discrete curvature. We improve volume growth bounds under a lower bound on the so-called Ollivier curvature and discuss similar results under other types of discrete Ricci curvature. Following recent work in the continuous setting of Riemannian manifolds (by the 1st author), we then bound the eigenvalues of the Laplacian of a graph under bounds on the volume growth. In particular, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _2$</tex> of the graph can be bounded using a weighted discrete Hardy inequality and the higher eigenvalues of the graph can be bounded by the eigenvalues of a tridiagonal matrix times a multiplicative factor, both of which only depend on the volume growth of the graph. As a direct application, we relate the eigenvalues to the Cheeger isoperimetric constant. Using these methods, we describe classes of graphs for which the Cheeger inequality is tight on the 2nd eigenvalue (i.e. the 1st nonzero eigenvalue). We also describe a method for proving Buser's Inequality in graphs, particularly under a lower bound assumption on curvature.

articleTitle: Coalescence Phenomenon of Quantum Cohomology of Grassmannians and the Distribution of Prime Numbers
abstract: The occurrence and frequency of a phenomenon of resonance (namely the coalescence of some Dubrovin canonical coordinates) in the locus of small quantum cohomology of complex Grassmannians are studied. It is shown that surprisingly this frequency is strictly subordinate and highly influenced by the distribution of prime numbers. Two equivalent formulations of the Riemann hypothesis are given in terms of numbers of complex Grassmannians without coalescence: the former as a constraint on the disposition of singularities of the analytic continuation of the Dirichlet series associated to the sequence counting non-coalescing Grassmannians, and the latter as asymptotic estimate (whose error term cannot be improved) for their distribution function.

articleTitle: Bergman-Harmonic Functions on Classical Domains
abstract: We study Bergman-harmonic functions on classical domains from a new point of view in this paper. We first establish a boundary pluriharmonicity result for Bergman-harmonic functions on classical domains: a Bergman-harmonic function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u$</tex> on a classical domain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> must be pluriharmonic on germs of complex manifolds in the boundary of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u$</tex> has some appropriate boundary regularity. Next we give a new characterization of pluriharmonicity on classical domains which may shed a new light on future study of Bergman-harmonic functions. We also prove characterization results for Bergman-harmonic functions on type I domains.

articleTitle: Orbital Degeneracy Loci II: Gorenstein Orbits
abstract: In [3] we introduced orbital degeneracy loci as generalizations of degeneracy loci of morphisms between vector bundles. Orbital degeneracy loci can be constructed from any stable subvariety of a representation of an algebraic group. In this paper we show that their canonical bundles can be conveniently controlled in the case where the affine coordinate ring of the subvariety is Gorenstein. We then study in a systematic way the subvarieties obtained as orbit closures in representations with finitely many orbits, and we determine the canonical bundles of the corresponding orbital degeneracy loci in the Gorenstein cases. Applications are given to the construction of low-dimensional varieties with negative or trivial canonical bundle.

articleTitle: Homology Smale–Barden Manifolds with K-contact but not Sasakian Structures
abstract: Kollár has found subtle obstructions to the existence of Sasakian structures on five-dimensional manifolds. In the present article we develop methods of using these obstructions to distinguish K-contact manifolds from Sasakian ones. In particular, we find the first example of a closed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5$</tex>-manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_1(M,\mathbb{Z})=0,$</tex> which is K-contact but which carries no semi-regular Sasakian structures.

articleTitle: Decomposition Spaces and Restriction Species
abstract: We show that Schmitt’s restriction species (such as graphs, matroids, posets, etc.) naturally induce decomposition spaces (a.k.a. unital <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>-Segal spaces), and that their associated coalgebras are an instance of the general construction of incidence coalgebras of decomposition spaces. We introduce directed restriction species that subsume Schmitt’s restriction species and also induce decomposition spaces. Whereas ordinary restriction species are presheaves on the category of finite sets and injections, directed restriction species are presheaves on the category of finite posets and convex maps. We also introduce the notion of monoidal (directed) restriction species, which induce monoidal decomposition spaces and hence bialgebras, most often Hopf algebras. Examples of this notion include rooted forests, directed graphs, posets, double posets, and many related structures. A prominent instance of a resulting incidence bialgebra is the Butcher–Connes–Kreimer Hopf algebra of rooted trees. Both ordinary and directed restriction species are shown to be examples of a construction of decomposition spaces from certain cocartesian fibrations over the category of finite ordinals that are also cartesian over convex maps. The proofs rely on some beautiful simplicial combinatorics, where the notion of convexity plays a key role. The methods developed are of independent interest as techniques for constructing decomposition spaces.

articleTitle: Collections of Hypersurfaces Containing a Curve
abstract: We consider the closed locus parameterizing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-tuples of hypersurfaces that have positive dimensional intersection and fail to intersect properly, and show in a large range of degrees that its unique irreducible component of maximal dimension consists of tuples of hypersurfaces whose intersection contains a line. We then apply our methods in conjunction with a known reduction to positive characteristic argument to find the unique component of maximal dimension of the locus of hypersurfaces with positive dimensional singular loci. We will also find the components of maximal dimension of the locus of smooth hypersurfaces with a higher dimensional family of lines through a point than expected.

articleTitle: Asymptotics for the Expected Number of Nodal Components for Random Lemniscates
abstract: We determine the true asymptotic behaviour for the expected number of connected components for a model of random lemniscates proposed recently by Lerario and Lundberg. These are defined as the subsets of the Riemann sphere, where the absolute value of certain random, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{SO}(3)$</tex>-invariant rational function of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> equals to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>. We show that the expected number of the connected components of these lemniscates, divided by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>, converges to a positive constant defined in terms of the quotient of two independent plane Gaussian analytic functions. A major obstacle in applying the novel non-local techniques due to Nazarov and Sodin on this problem is the underlying non-Gaussianity, intrinsic to the studied model.

articleTitle: Translating Solitons of the Mean Curvature Flow Asymptotic to Hyperplanes in ℝn+1
abstract: A translating soliton is a hypersurface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{R}}^{n+1}$</tex> such that the family <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_t= M- t \,\mathbf e_{n+1}$</tex> is a mean curvature flow, that is, such that normal component of the velocity at each point is equal to the mean curvature at that point <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{H}=\mathbf e_{n+1}^{\perp }.$</tex> In this paper we obtain a characterization of hyperplanes that are parallel to the velocity and the family of tilted grim reaper cylinders as the only translating solitons in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$</tex> that are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^1$</tex>-asymptotic to two half-hyperplanes outside a non-vertical cylinder. This result was proven for translators in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^3$</tex> by the 2nd author, Perez-Garcia, Savas-Halilaj, and Smoczyk under the additional hypotheses that the genus of the surface was locally bounded and the cylinder was perpendicular to the translating velocity.

articleTitle: Jacobi–Trudi Identity and Drinfeld Functor for Super Yangian
abstract: We show that the quantum Berezinian that gives a generating function of the integrals of motions of XXX spin chains associated to super Yangian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{Y}(\mathfrak{g}\mathfrak{l}_{m|n})$</tex> can be written as a ratio of two difference operators of orders <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> whose coefficients are ratios of transfer matrices corresponding to explicit skew Young diagrams. In the process, we develop several missing parts of the representation theory of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{Y}(\mathfrak{g}\mathfrak{l}_{m|n})$</tex> such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-character theory, Jacobi–Trudi identity, Drinfeld functor, extended T-systems, and Harish-Chandra map.

articleTitle: Highest Weights for Categorical Representations
abstract: We present a criterion for establishing Morita equivalence of monoidal categories and apply it to the categorical representation theory of reductive groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>. We show that the “de Rham group algebra” <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal D(G)$</tex> (the monoidal category of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal D$</tex>-modules on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>) is Morita equivalent to the universal Hecke category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal D({N}\backslash{G}/{N})$</tex> and to its monodromic variant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde{\mathcal D}({B}\backslash{G}/{B})$</tex>. In other words, de Rham <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>-categories, that is, module categories for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal D(G)$</tex>, satisfy a “highest weight theorem”—they all appear in the decomposition of the universal principal series representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal D(G/N)$</tex> or in twisted <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal D$</tex>-modules on the flag variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde{\mathcal D}(G/B)$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Linearized Calderón Problem in Transversally Anisotropic Geometries
abstract: In this article we study the linearized anisotropic Calderón problem. In a compact manifold with boundary, this problem amounts to showing that products of harmonic functions form a complete set. Assuming that the manifold is transversally anisotropic, we show that the boundary measurements determine an Fourier—Bros—Iagolnitzer-type transform at certain points in the transversal manifold. This leads to proving a uniqueness result for transversal singularities in the linearized problem. The method requires a geometric condition on the transversal manifold related to pairs of intersecting geodesics, but it does not involve the geodesic X-ray transform, which has limited earlier results on this problem.

articleTitle: On the Inner Products of Some Deligne–Lusztig-type Representations
abstract: In this paper we introduce a family of Deligne–Lusztig-type varieties attached to connected reductive groups over quotients of discrete valuation rings, naturally generalising the higher Deligne–Lusztig varieties and some constructions related to the algebraisation problem raised by Lusztig. We establish the inner product formula between the representations associated to these varieties and the higherDeligne–Lusztig representations.

articleTitle: Minimal Boundaries in Tonelli Lagrangian Systems
abstract: We prove several new results concerning action minimizing periodic orbits of Tonelli Lagrangian systems on an oriented closed surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>. More specifically, we show that for every energy larger than the maximal energy of a constant orbit and smaller than or equal to the Mañé critical value of the universal abelian cover, the Lagrangian system admits a minimal boundary, that is, a global minimizer of the Lagrangian action on the space of smooth boundaries of open sets of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>. We also extend the celebrated graph theorem of Mather in this context: in the tangent bundle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{T} M$</tex>, the union of the supports of all lifted minimal boundaries with a given energy projects injectively to the base <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>. Finally, we prove the existence of action minimizing simple periodic orbits on energies just above the Mañé critical value of the universal abelian cover. This provides in particular a class of nonreversible Finsler metrics on the two-sphere possessing infinitely many closed geodesics.

articleTitle: Ricci Iteration for Coupled Kähler–Einstein Metrics
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the “coupled Ricci iteration”, a dynamical system related to the Ricci operator and twisted Kähler–Einstein metrics as an approach to the study of coupled Kähler–Einstein (CKE) metrics. For negative 1st Chern class, we prove the smooth convergence of the iteration. For positive 1st Chern class, we also provide a notion of coercivity of the Ding functional and show its equivalence to the existence of CKE metrics. As an application, we prove the smooth convergence of the iteration on CKE Fano manifolds assuming that the automorphism group is discrete.

articleTitle: Restriction of Laplace–Beltrami Eigenfunctions to Arbitrary Sets on Manifolds
abstract: Given a compact Riemannian manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M, g)$</tex> without boundary, we estimate the Lebesgue norm of Laplace–Beltrami eigenfunctions when restricted to a wide variety of subsets <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>. The sets <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> that we consider are Borel measurable, Lebesguenull but otherwise arbitrary with positive Hausdorff dimension. Our estimates are based on Frostman-type ball growth conditions for measures supported on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex>. For large Lebesgue exponents <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>, these estimates provide a natural generalization of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^p$</tex> bounds for eigenfunctions restricted to submanifolds, previously obtained in [8, 18, 19, 32]. Under an additional measure-theoretic assumption on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex>, the estimates are shown to be sharp in this range. As evidence of the genericity of the sharp estimates, we provide a large family of random, Cantor-type sets that are not submanifolds, where the above-mentioned sharp bounds hold almost surely.

articleTitle: Ulrich Bundles on Intersections of Two 4-Dimensional Quadrics
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the moduli space of Ulrich bundles on a smooth complete intersection of two <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4$</tex>-dimensional quadrics in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^5$</tex>. The main ingredient is the semiorthogonal decomposition by Bondal–Orlov, combined with the categorical methods pioneered by Kuznetsov and Lahoz–Macrì–Stellari. Using these methods, we prove that any smooth intersection of two 4-dimensional quadrics in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^5$</tex> carries an Ulrich bundle of rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex> for every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r \ge 2$</tex>. Moreover, we provide a description of the moduli space of stable Ulrich bundles.

articleTitle: Leading Terms of SL3 Web Invariants
abstract: We use Khovanov and Kuperberg’s web growth rules to identify the leading term in the invariant associated to an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{SL}_3$</tex> web diagram, with respect to a particular term order.

articleTitle: Crystalline Cohomology of Towers of Curves
abstract: We investigate the geometry of finite maps and correspondences between curves, and construct canonical trace and pullback maps between Hyodo–Kato integral structures on de Rham cohomology of curves, which are functorial for finite morphisms of the generic fibres. This leads to a crystalline version of the étale cohomology of towers of modular curves considered by Hida and Ohta, whose ordinary part satisfies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda $</tex>-adic control and Eichler–Shimura theorems.

articleTitle: Transfer to Characteristic Zero of the Jacquet–Mao’s Metaplectic Fundamental Lemma
abstract: Jacquet conjectured that globally a cuspidal automorphic representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{G}\mathrm{L}_r$</tex> should be in the image of the metaplectic correspondence precisely when it is distinguished with respect to a split orthogonal similitude group. Jacquet–Mao have suggested an approach to solve this problem by using “relative” traces formula. One of the steps of this approach is the Jacquet–Mao’s metaplectic fundamental lemma. The author proved this fundamental lemma for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex> in the case of positive characteristic. The aim of this paper is to extend this result to the more general case.

articleTitle: Fourier–Mukai Transform on a Compactified Jacobian
abstract: We use Fourier–Mukai transform to compute the cohomology of the Picard bundles on the compactified Jacobian of an integral nodal curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>. We prove that the transform gives an injective morphism from the moduli space of vector bundles of rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r \ge 2$</tex> and degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> sufficiently large) on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> to the moduli space of vector bundles of a fixed rank and fixed Chern classes on the compactified Jacobian of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>. We show that this morphism induces a morphism from the moduli space of vector bundles of rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r \ge 2$</tex> and a fixed determinant of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> to the moduli space of vector bundles of a fixed rank with a fixed determinant and fixed Chern classes on the compactified Jacobian of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>.

articleTitle: On a Discretization of Confocal Quadrics. A Geometric Approach to General Parametrizations
abstract: We propose a discretization of classical confocal coordinates. It is based on a novel characterization thereof as factorizable orthogonal coordinate systems. Our geometric discretization leads to factorizable discrete nets with a novel discrete analog of the orthogonality property. A discrete confocal coordinate system may be constructed geometrically via polarity with respect to a sequence of classical confocal quadrics. Various sequences correspond to various discrete parametrizations. The coordinate functions of discrete confocal quadrics are computed explicitly. The theory is illustrated with a variety of examples in two and three dimensions. These include confocal coordinate systems parametrized in terms of Jacobi elliptic functions. Connections with incircular nets and a generalized Euler–Poisson–Darboux system are established.

articleTitle: Applications of the Ohsawa–Takegoshi Extension Theorem to Direct Image Problems
abstract: In the 1st part of the paper, we study a Fujita-type conjecture by Popa and Schnell and obtain an effective bound on the generic global generation of direct images of twisted pluricanonical bundles. We also point out the relation between the Seshadri constant and the optimal bound. In the 2nd part, we give an affirmative answer to a question by Demailly, Peternell, and Schneider in a more general setting. As byproducts of our proofs, we extend a result by Fujino and Gongyo on images of weak Fano manifolds to the Kawamata log terminal settings and refine a theorem by Broustet and Pacienza on the rational connectedness of the image.

articleTitle: Generalized Cesàro Operators: Geometry of Spectra and Quasi-Nilpotency
abstract: For the class of Hardy spaces and standard weighted Bergman spaces of the unit disk, we prove that the spectrum of a generalized Cesàro operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_g$</tex> is unchanged if the symbol <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> is perturbed to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g+h$</tex> by an analytic function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex> inducing a quasi-nilpotent operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_h$</tex>, that is, spectrum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_h$</tex> equals <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{0\}$</tex>.
