We also show that any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_g$</tex> operator that can be approximated in the operator norm by an operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_h$</tex> with bounded symbol <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex> is quasi-nilpotent. In the converse direction, we establish an equivalent condition for the function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g \in \textbf{BMOA}$</tex> to be in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{BMOA}$</tex> norm closure of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^{\infty }$</tex>. This condition turns out to be equivalent to quasi-nilpotency of the operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_g$</tex> on the Hardy spaces. This raises the question whether similar statement is true in the context of Bergman spaces and the Bloch space. Furthermore, we provide some general geometric properties of the spectrum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{g}$</tex> operators.

articleTitle: Exceptional Legendrian Torus Knots
abstract: We present classification results for exceptional Legendrian realisations of torus knots. These are the first results of that kind for non-trivial topological knot types. Enumeration results of Ding–Li–Zhang concerning tight contact structures on certain Seifert fibred manifolds with boundary allow us to place upper bounds on the number of tight contact structures on the complements of torus knots; the classification of exceptional realisations of these torus knots is then achieved by exhibiting sufficiently many realisations in terms of contact surgery diagrams. We also discuss a couple of general theorems about the existence of exceptional Legendrian knots.

articleTitle: Necessary Condition for Rectifiability Involving Wasserstein Distance W2
abstract: A Radon measure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex> is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-rectifiable if it is absolutely continuous with respect to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-dimensional Hausdorff measure and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex>-almost all of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\operatorname{supp}}\mu $</tex> can be covered by Lipschitz images of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^n$</tex>. In this paper, we give a necessary condition for rectifiability in terms of the so-called <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha _2$</tex> numbers — coefficients quantifying flatness using Wasserstein distance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W_2$</tex>. In a recent article, we showed that the same condition is also sufficient for rectifiability, and so we get a new characterization of rectifiable measures.

articleTitle: Criteria for Embedded Eigenvalues for Discrete Schrödinger Operators
abstract: In this paper, we consider discrete Schrödinger operators of the form, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*} (Hu)(n) = u({n+1})+u({n-1})+V(n)u(n). \end{equation*}$$</tex>We view <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> as a perturbation of the free operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_0$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(H_0u)(n)= u({n+1})+u({n-1})$</tex>. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_0$</tex> (no perturbation), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma _{\textrm{ess}}(H_0)=\sigma _{\textrm{ac}}(H)=[-2,2]$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_0$</tex> does not have eigenvalues embedded into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-2,2)$</tex>. It is an interesting and important problem to identify the perturbation such that the operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_0+V$</tex> has one eigenvalue (finitely many eigenvalues or countable eigenvalues) embedded into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-2,2)$</tex>. We introduce the almost sign type potentials and develop the Prüfer transformation to address this problem, which leads to the following five results. 1: We obtain the sharp spectral transition for the existence of irrational type eigenvalues or rational type eigenvalues with even denominators. 2: Suppose <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\limsup _{n\to \infty } n|V(n)|=a<\infty .$</tex> We obtain a lower/upper bound of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_0+V$</tex> has one rational type eigenvalue with odd denominator. 3: We obtain the asymptotical behavior of embedded eigenvalues around the boundaries of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-2,2)$</tex>. 4: Given any finite set of points <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{ E_j\}_{j=1}^N$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-2,2)$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\notin \{ E_j\}_{j=1}^N+\{ E_j\}_{j=1}^N$</tex>, we construct the explicit potential <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V(n)=\frac{O(1)}{1+|n|}$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H=H_0+V$</tex> has eigenvalues <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{ E_j\}_{j=1}^N$</tex>. 5: Given any countable set of points <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{ E_j\}$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-2,2)$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\notin \{ E_j\}+\{ E_j\}$</tex>, and any function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h(n)>0$</tex> going to infinity arbitrarily slowly, we construct the explicit potential <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|V(n)|\leq \frac{h(n)}{1+|n|}$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H=H_0+V$</tex> has eigenvalues <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{ E_j\}$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Large Genus Asymptotic Expansion of Masur–Veech Volumes
abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of Masur–Veech volumes as the genus goes to infinity. We show the existence of a complete asymptotic expansion of these volumes that depends only on the genus and the number of singularities. The computation of the 1st term of this asymptotics expansion was a long-standing problem. This problem was recently solved in [2] using purely combinatorial arguments and then in [3] using algebro-geometric insights. Our proof relies on a combination of both methods.

articleTitle: Fourier Frames for Surface-Carried Measures
abstract: In this paper, we show that the surface measure on the boundary of a convex body of everywhere positive Gaussian curvature does not admit a Fourier frame. This answers a question proposed by Lev and provides the 1st example of a uniformly distributed measure supported on a set of Lebesgue measure zero that does not admit a Fourier frame. In contrast, we show that the surface measure on the boundary of a polytope always admits a Fourier frame. We also explore orthogonal bases and frames adopted to sets under consideration. More precisely, given a compact manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> without a boundary and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D \subset M$</tex>, we ask whether <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2(D)$</tex> possesses an orthogonal basis of eigenfunctions. The non-abelian nature of this problem, in general, puts it outside the realm of the previously explored questions about the existence of bases of characters for subsets of locally compact abelian groups. This paper is dedicated to Alexander Olevskii on the occasion of his birthday. Olevskii’s mathematical depth and personal kindness serve as a major source of inspiration for us and many others in the field of mathematics.

articleTitle: Endpoint Sobolev Continuity of the Fractional Maximal Function in Higher Dimensions
abstract: We establish continuity mapping properties of the noncentered fractional maximal operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\beta }$</tex> in the endpoint input space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W^{1,1}({\mathbb R}^d)$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d \geq 2$</tex> in the cases for which its boundedness is known. More precisely, we prove that for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q=d/(d-\beta )$</tex> the map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f \mapsto |\nabla M_\beta f|$</tex> is continuous from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W^{1,1}({\mathbb R}^d)$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{q}({\mathbb R}^d)$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ 0 < \beta < 1$</tex> if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> is radial and for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \leq \beta < d$</tex> for general <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>. The results for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\leq \beta < d$</tex> extend to the centered counterpart <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_\beta ^c$</tex>. Moreover, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d=1$</tex>, we show that the conjectured boundedness of that map for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_\beta ^c$</tex> implies its continuity.

articleTitle: Symmetric Quantum Sets and L-Algebras
abstract: Quantum analogues of sets are defined by two simple assumptions, allowing enumeration, reminiscent of the Gram–Schmidt orthogonalization process. It is shown that any symmetric quantum set is a classical set of irreducible components, and that each irreducible component of size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>3$</tex> is representable by an orthomodular space over a skew field with involution. For finite or sufficiently large irreducible components, invariance of quantum cardinality is proved. Topological quantum sets are introduced as quantum analogues of topological spaces; irreducible ones of size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>3$</tex> are shown to be representable by Hilbert spaces over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{R}}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{C}}$</tex>, or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{H}}$</tex>. Symmetric quantum sets are characterized as a class of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-algebras with an intrinsic geometry, and they are shown to be equivalent to Piron’s quantum formalism. Equivalences between symmetric quantum sets and several other structures are established. To any symmetric quantum set, a group with a right invariant lattice structure is associated as a complete invariant. A simple and self-contained proof of Solèr’s theorem is included, which is used to prove that sufficiently large irreducible symmetric quantum sets come from a classical Hilbert space.

articleTitle: The Bicanonical Map of Fake Projective Planes with an Automorphism
abstract: We show, for several fake projective planes with a nontrivial group of automorphisms, that the bicanonical map is an embedding.

articleTitle: Chromatic Numbers of Stable Kneser Hypergraphs via Topological Tverberg-Type Theorems
abstract: Kneser’s 1955 conjecture—proven by Lovász in 1978—asserts that in any partition of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-subsets of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{1, 2, \dots , n\}$</tex> into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n-2k+1$</tex> parts, one part contains two disjoint sets. Schrijver showed that one can restrict to significantly fewer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-sets and still observe the same intersection pattern. Alon, Frankl, and Lovász proved a different generalization of Kneser’s conjecture for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex> pairwise disjoint sets. Dolnikov generalized Lovász’ result to arbitrary set systems, while Kříž did the same for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>-fold extension of Kneser’s conjecture. Here we prove a common generalization of all of these results. Moreover, we prove additional strengthenings by determining the chromatic number of certain sparse stable Kneser hypergraphs, and further develop a general approach to establishing lower bounds for chromatic numbers of hypergraphs using a combination of methods from equivariant topology and intersection results for convex hulls of points in Euclidean space.

articleTitle: A Rigidity Theorem for Surfaces in Schwarzschild Manifold
abstract: In this article, we prove a rigidity theorem for isometric embeddings into the Schwarzschild manifold, by using the variational formula of quasi-local mass.

articleTitle: Unitary Representations with Dirac Cohomology: Finiteness in the Real Case
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> be a complex connected simple algebraic group with a fixed real form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma $</tex>. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G({\mathbb{R}})=G^\sigma $</tex> be the corresponding group of real points. This paper reports a finiteness theorem for the classification of irreducible unitary Harish-Chandra modules of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G({\mathbb{R}})$</tex> (up to equivalence) having nonvanishing Dirac cohomology. Moreover, we study the distribution of the spin norm along Vogan pencils for certain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G({\mathbb{R}})$</tex>, with particular attention paid to the unitarily small convex hull introduced by Salamanca-Riba and Vogan.

articleTitle: The Neumann Problem of Complex Hessian Quotient Equations
abstract: In this paper, we consider the Neumann problem of complex Hessian quotient equations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{\sigma _k (\partial \bar{\partial } u)}{\sigma _l (\partial \bar{\partial } u)} = f(z)$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0 \leq l < k \leq n$</tex> and establish the global <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^1$</tex> estimates and reduce the global 2nd derivative estimate to the estimate of double normal 2nd derivatives on the boundary. In particular, we can prove the global <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^2$</tex> estimates and the existence theorem for the Neumann problem of complex Hessian quotient equations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{\sigma _n (\partial \bar{\partial } u)}{\sigma _l (\partial \bar{\partial } u)} = f(z)$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0 \leq l < n$</tex> by the method of continuity.

articleTitle: Meromorphic Modular Forms with Rational Cycle Integrals
abstract: We study rationality properties of geodesic cycle integrals of meromorphic modular forms associated to positive definite binary quadratic forms. In particular, we obtain finite rational formulas for the cycle integrals of suitable linear combinations of these meromorphic modular forms.

articleTitle: Lp Estimates for Joint Quasimodes of Semiclassical Pseudodifferential Operators Whose Characteristic Sets Have kth Order Contact
abstract: In this paper we develop <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{p}$</tex> estimates for functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u$</tex>, which are joint quasimodes of semiclassical pseudodifferential operators <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_{1}(x,hD)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_{2}(x,hD)$</tex> whose characteristic sets meet with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>th order contact, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k\geq{}1$</tex>. As part of the technical development we use Fourier integral operators to adapt a flat wavelet analysis to the curved level sets of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_{1}(x,\xi )$</tex>.

articleTitle: Removing a Ray from a Noncompact Symplectic Manifold
abstract: We prove that any noncompact symplectic manifold that admits a properly embedded ray with a wide neighborhood is symplectomorphic to the complement of the ray by constructing an explicit symplectomorphism in the case of the standard Euclidean space. This allows us to excide a ray from a symplectic manifold and we use this excision trick to find a nowhere vanishing Liouville vector field on every cotangent bundle.

articleTitle: Stochastic Dominance and Weak Concentration for Sums of Independent Symmetric Random Vectors
abstract: Kwapień and Woyczyński asked in their monograph (1992) whether their notion of superstrong domination is inherited when taking sums of independent symmetric random vectors (one vector dominates another if, essentially, tail probabilities of any norm of the two vectors compare up to some scaling constants). We answer this question positively. As a by-product of our methods, we establish that a certain notion of weak concentration is also preserved by taking sums of independent symmetric random vectors.

articleTitle: Integrable Systems of Double Ramification Type
abstract: In this paper we study various aspects of the double ramification (DR) hierarchy, introduced by the 1st author, and its quantization. We extend the notion of tau-symmetry to quantum integrable hierarchies and prove that the quantum DR hierarchy enjoys this property. We determine explicitly the genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> quantum correction and, as an application, compute completely the quantization of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>- and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4$</tex>-KdV hierarchies (the DR hierarchies for Witten’s <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>- and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4$</tex>-spin theories). We then focus on the recursion relation satisfied by the DR Hamiltonian densities and, abstracting from its geometric origin, we use it to characterize and construct a new family of quantum and classical integrable systems that we call of DR type, as they satisfy all of the main properties of the DR hierarchy. In the 2nd part, we obtain new insight towards the Miura equivalence conjecture between the DR and Dubrovin-Zhang (DZ) hierarchies, via a geometric interpretation of the correlators forming the DR tau-function. We then show that the candidate Miura transformation between the DR and DZ hierarchies (which we uniquely identified in our previous paper) indeed turns the DZ Poisson structure into the standard form. Eventually, we focus on integrable hierarchies associated with rank-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> cohomological field theories and their deformations, and we prove the DR/DZ equivalence conjecture up to genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5$</tex> in this context.

articleTitle: d-elliptic Loci in Genus 2 and 3
abstract: We consider the loci of curves of genus 2 and 3 admitting a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-to-1 map to a genus 1 curve. After compactifying these loci via admissible covers, we obtain formulas for their Chow classes, recovering results of Faber–Pagani and van Zelm when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d=2$</tex>. The answers exhibit quasimodularity properties similar to those in the Gromov–Witten theory of a fixed genus 1 curve; we conjecture that the quasimodularity persists in higher genus and indicate a number of possible variants.

articleTitle: Rank, Coclass, and Cohomology
abstract: We prove that for any prime <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> the finite <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-groups of fixed coclass have only finitely many different mod-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> cohomology rings between them. This was conjectured by Carlson; we prove it by first proving a stronger version for groups of fixed rank.

articleTitle: The GL4 Rapoport–Zink Space
abstract: We give a description of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{GL}_4$</tex> Rapoport–Zink space, including the connected components, irreducible components, intersection behavior of the irreducible components, and Ekedahl–Oort stratification. As an application of this, we also give a description of the supersingular locus of the Shimura variety for the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{GU}(2,2)$</tex> over a prime split in the relevant imaginary quadratic field.

articleTitle: On the Question of Genericity of Hyperbolic Knots
abstract: A well-known conjecture in knot theory says that the proportion of hyperbolic knots among all of the prime knots of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> or fewer crossings approaches <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> approaches infinity. In this article, it is proved that this conjecture contradicts several other plausible conjectures, including the 120-year-old conjecture on additivity of the crossing number of knots under connected sum and the conjecture that the crossing number of a satellite knot is not less than that of its companion.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Stability for Some Non positive Perturbations of the Camassa–Holm Peakon with Application to the Antipeakon–peakon Profile
abstract: We continue our investigation on the asymptotic stability of the peakon. In a 1st step we extend our asymptotic stability result [30] in the class of functions whose negative part of the momentum density is supported in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$]-\infty ,x_0] $</tex> and the positive part in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[x_0,+\infty [$</tex> for some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ x_0\in{\mathbb{R}}$</tex>. In a 2nd step this enables us to prove the asymptotic stability of well-ordered train of antipeakons–peakons and, in particular, of the antipeakon–peakon profile. Finally, in the appendix we prove that in the case of a nonnegative momentum density the energy at the left of any given point decays to zero as time goes to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+\infty $</tex>. This leads to an improvement of the asymptotic stability result stated in [30].

articleTitle: An Application of Collapsing Levels to the Representation Theory of Affine Vertex Algebras
abstract: We discover a large class of simple affine vertex algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{k} ({\mathfrak{g}})$</tex>, associated to basic Lie superalgebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathfrak{g}}$</tex> at non-admissible collapsing levels <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>, having exactly one irreducible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathfrak{g}}$</tex>-locally finite module in the category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal O}$</tex>. In the case when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathfrak{g}}$</tex> is a Lie algebra, we prove a complete reducibility result for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_k({\mathfrak{g}})$</tex>-modules at an arbitrary collapsing level. We also determine the generators of the maximal ideal in the universal affine vertex algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V^k ({\mathfrak{g}})$</tex> at certain negative integer levels. Considering some conformal embeddings in the simple affine vertex algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{-1/2} (C_n)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{-4}(E_7)$</tex>, we surprisingly obtain the realization of non-simple affine vertex algebras of types <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> having exactly one nontrivial ideal.

articleTitle: Intrinsic and Dual Volume Deviations of Convex Bodies and Polytopes
abstract: We establish estimates for the asymptotic best approximation of the Euclidean unit ball by polytopes under a notion of distance induced by the intrinsic volumes. We also introduce a notion of distance between convex bodies that is induced by the Wills functional and apply it to derive asymptotically sharp bounds for approximating the ball in high dimensions. Remarkably, it turns out that there is a polytope that is almost optimal with respect to all intrinsic volumes simultaneously, up to absolute constants. Finally, we establish asymptotic formulas for the best approximation of smooth convex bodies by polytopes with respect to a distance induced by dual volumes, which originate from Lutwak's dual Brunn–Minkowski theory.

articleTitle: Multiplicity-freeness of Unitary Representations in Sections of Holomorphic Hilbert Bundles
abstract: We prove several results asserting that the action of a Banach–Lie group on Hilbert spaces of holomorphic sections of a holomorphic Hilbert space bundle over a complex Banach manifold is multiplicity-free. These results require the existence of compatible anti-holomorphic bundle maps and certain multiplicity-freeness assumptions for stabilizer groups. For the group action on the base, the notion of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S,\sigma )$</tex>-weakly visible action (generalizing T. Koboyashi’s visible actions) provides an effective way to express the assumptions in an economical fashion. In particular, we derive a version for group actions on homogeneous bundles for larger groups. We illustrate these general results by several examples related to operator groups and von Neumann algebras.

articleTitle: Counting Bounded Elements of a Number Field
abstract: We estimate, in a number field, the number of elements and the maximal number of linearly independent elements, with prescribed bounds on their valuations. As a by-product, we obtain new bounds for the successive minima of ideal lattices. Our arguments combine group theory, ramification theory, and the geometry of numbers.

articleTitle: Gevrey Expansions of Hypergeometric Integrals II
abstract: We study integral representations of the Gevrey series solutions of irregular hypergeometric systems under certain assumptions. We prove that, for such systems, any Gevrey series solution, along a coordinate hyperplane of its singular support, is the asymptotic expansion of a holomorphic solution given by a carefully chosen integral representation.

articleTitle: Alexandrov–Bakelman–Pucci-Type Estimate for Plurisubharmonic Functions
abstract: We prove an optimal Alexandrov–Bakelman–Pucci-type estimate for plurisubharmonic functions without assuming their continuity. This generalizes a result of Wang. As a corollary, we generalize an estimate from [15]. We also address a problem posed in [29].

articleTitle: Stable Rationality of del Pezzo Fibrations of Low Degree Over Projective Spaces
abstract: The main aim of this article is to show that a very general three-dimensional del Pezzo fibration of degrees 1, 2, and 3 is not stably rational except for a del Pezzo fibration of degree 3 belonging to explicitly described two families. Higher-dimensional generalizations are also discussed and we prove that a very general del Pezzo fibration of degrees 1, 2, and 3 defined over the projective space is not stably rational provided that the anti-canonical divisor is not ample.

articleTitle: Towards the Finite Slope Part for GLn
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> be a finite extension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{Q}}_p$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 2$</tex>. We associate to a crystabelline <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-dimensional representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\operatorname{Gal}}(\overline L/L)$</tex> satisfying mild genericity assumptions a finite length locally <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{Q}}_p$</tex>-analytic representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\operatorname{GL}}_n(L)$</tex>. In the crystalline case and in a global context, using the recent results on the locally analytic socle from [6], we prove that this representation indeed occurs in spaces of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic automorphic forms. We then use this latter result in the ordinary case to show that certain “ordinary” <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic Banach space representations constructed in our previous work appear in spaces of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic automorphic forms. This gives strong new evidence to our previous conjecture in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic case.

articleTitle: A Rigid Hyperfinite Type II1 Factor
abstract: We show that it is relatively consistent with Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory with the axiom of choice that there exists a hyperfinite type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{II}_1$</tex>-factor of density character <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\aleph _1$</tex> that is not isomorphic to its opposite, does not have any outer automorphisms, and has trivial fundamental group.

articleTitle: A Generalization of Steinberg Theory and an Exotic Moment Map
abstract: For a reductive group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>, Steinberg established a map from the Weyl group to the set of nilpotent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>-orbits by using moment maps on double flag varieties. In particular, in the case of the general linear group, it provides a geometric interpretation of the Robinson–Schensted correspondence between permutations and pairs of standard tableaux of the same shape. We extend Steinberg’s approach to the case of a symmetric pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(G, K)$</tex> to obtain two different maps, namely a generalized Steinberg map and an exotic moment map. Although the framework is general, in this paper we focus on the pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(G,K) = (\textrm{GL}_{2n}({\mathbb{C}}), \textrm{GL}_n({\mathbb{C}}) \times \textrm{GL}_n({\mathbb{C}}))$</tex>. Then the generalized Steinberg map is a map from partial permutations to the pairs of nilpotent orbits in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \mathfrak{gl}_n({\mathbb{C}}) $</tex>. It involves a generalization of the classical Robinson–Schensted correspondence to the case of partial permutations. The other map, the exotic moment map, establishes a combinatorial map from the set of partial permutations to that of signed Young diagrams, that is, the set of nilpotent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ K$</tex>-orbits in the Cartan space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\textrm{Lie}(G)/\textrm{Lie}(K))^* $</tex>. We explain the geometric background of the theory and combinatorial algorithms, which produce the above-mentioned maps.

articleTitle: On Manifolds with Lower Quadratic Curvature Decay and Volume Pinching
abstract: We give some conditions for a complete noncompact Riemannian manifold with lower quadratic curvature decay to have finite topological type. Most of our curvature conditions are much weaker than the assumptions in Lott [5] and in Sha–Shen [10], hence our results can be viewed as natural generalizations of those works.

articleTitle: Example of Compact Special Lagrangians with a Stable Singularity
abstract: We construct a family of compact almost Calabi–Yau manifolds of complex dimension 3 and therein a corresponding family of compact special Lagrangians with one-point singularities modelled upon that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T^2$</tex>-cone constructed by Harvey and Lawson [7, Chapter III.3.A, Theorem 3.1] and characterised by Haskins [8, Theorem A] as a stable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T^2$</tex>-cone in the terminology by Joyce [16, Definition 3.4 and Example 3.5].

articleTitle: Time Fractional Parabolic Equations with Measurable Coefficients and Embeddings for Fractional Parabolic Sobolev Spaces
abstract: We consider time fractional parabolic equations in divergence and non-divergence form when the leading coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a^{ij}$</tex> are measurable functions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(t,x_1)$</tex> except for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a^{11}$</tex>, which is a measurable function of either <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_1$</tex>. We obtain the solvability in Sobolev spaces of the equations in the whole space, on a half space, and on a partially bounded domain. The proofs use a level set argument, a scaling argument, and embeddings in fractional parabolic Sobolev spaces for which we give a direct and elementary proof.
